items.quote: Táraka Brahma literally means a special manifestation of Parama Puruśa which ensures emancipation to the microcosms. The word Táraka means “liberator”, one who shows the correct way, one who loves as well as punishes, on who makes the microcosms His own.
items.statement: Táraka Brahma designates a specific manifestation of Parama Puruśa that acts as the liberator and loving guide providing emancipation to microcosmic beings.
items.title: A Devotee's Object of Ideation

items.quote: I have said many a time that Parama Puruśa cannot do two things: He cannot create a second Parama Puruśa like Himself, because whoever has established an intimate friendship with Him, whoever has identified himself with Him, becomes one with Him. Secondly, however hard He may try, He can never hate anyone, because everything is in His mind. Even if He wanted to hate someone, to hate would mean that He was indirectly hating Himself.
items.statement: Parama Puruśa is incapable of creating a duplicate of Himself or hating any entity because everything exists within His own mind.
items.title: A Few of Tantra's Special Characteristics

items.qualifiers: Actions taken for self-defense or preservation of life without harmful intent do not constitute hiḿsá.
items.quote: Ahiḿsá means not inflicting pain or hurt on anybody by thought, word or action. This word is wrongly interpreted by many. Some so-called learned persons in fact, define the word ahiḿsá in such a manner that if one adheres to it strictly, it is impossible to live not only in a society but also in forests, hills and caves.
items.statement: Ahiḿsá is defined as refraining from causing hurt or pain to any living being through thought, word, or deed with malicious intent, rather than an absolute ban on physical force or necessary biological destruction.
items.title: A Guide to Human Conduct

items.quote: Satya implies proper action of mind and the right use of words with the spirit of welfare. It has no English synonym. The word “true” or “truth” would be translated in Saḿskrta as “rta” (to state the fact). The Sádhaka is not asked to follow the path of rta. One is to practise Satya.
items.statement: Satya requires thought and action directed toward the benevolent welfare of others, differing from rta which merely states factual truth.
items.title: A Guide to Human Conduct

items.quote: The correct meaning of Brahmacarya is “to remain attached to Brahma”. “Brahmańi vicarańam iti Brahmacaryam”. Whenever people do some work or think of doing any work extroversially, they look upon the object, with which they come in contact, as a crude finite entity. Because of their constant aspiration for material achievement their mind is so engrossed in material objects that their very consciousness becomes crude. The meaning of practising Brahmacarya Sádhaná is to treat the object with which one comes in contact as different expressions of Brahma and not as crude forms.
items.statement: Brahmacarya is the practice of ideating on every object and being as an expression of Brahma, rather than the physical suppression of semen.
items.title: A Guide to Human Conduct

items.quote: Amongst devotees there are three clear categories. One category, call it “third-grade,” says, “O Lord, You belong to everybody – You belong to one and all – and because I am also included within the scope of ‘all’, You belong to me also.” And the second-grade devotee will say, “No, no, no. That is not the correct psychic approach. You belong to me, and because You belong to me You belong to all. That is, the first thing is that You belong to me. And the second thing, because You belong to me, is that You belong to others also.” And the first-grade devotee says, “No, no, no, that’s not the correct approach. You belong to me and You belong to me only and not to others. The relationship is purely personal.
items.statement: Devotees approach the relationship with the Supreme Creator across three distinct grades of personal intimacy.
items.title: A Purely Personal Entity

items.quote: The average longevity of a script is 2000 years and the average longevity of a language is 1000 years. After this period they undergo metamorphosis. Vedic and Saḿskrta are not the same languages. The language of the Aryans is Vedic Saḿskrta, or rather Rg Vedic Saḿskrta. Saḿskrta is of Indian origin.
items.statement: Scripts undergo metamorphosis roughly every two thousand years, whereas languages metamorphose on an average cycle of one thousand years.
items.title: A Scriptological and Linguistic Survey of the World

items.qualifiers: Removal of differences can occur in psychic and spiritual spheres, not physical.
items.quote: What are the criteria of relativity? Wherever there are svajátiiya, vijátiiya and svagata bheda (intra-specific, inter-specific and intra-structural differences), we shall call that entity relative. The moment these differences are removed, the relative entity merges into the Absolute.
items.statement: Relativity in entities is defined and classified by the presence of svajátiiya, vijátiiya, and svagata differences.
items.title: Abhedajiṋána and Daeshika Vyavadhána Vilopa

items.quote: During the state of samprajiṋáta samádhi, the unit citta is converted into Cognitive Faculty and thus the vikalpátmaka action of mind is suspended, although the samkalpátmaka state of mind is still quite active. But during the state of savikalpa samádhi, the samkalpátmaka state of mind remains only nominally active. And during the state of nirvikalpa samádhi both the samkalpátmaka and vikalpátmaka states of the mind are completely suspended.
items.statement: In samprajiṋáta samádhi the vikalpátmaka functioning is suspended while saḿkalpátmaka remains active; in savikalpa samádhi saḿkalpátmaka is nominal; in nirvikalpa samádhi both are fully suspended.
items.title: Abhedajiṋána and Nirvikalpa Samádhi

items.qualifiers: provided that spatial, temporal, and personal factors remain unchanged
items.quote: Whenever there is an action, there is an equal and opposite reaction, provided that the three fundamental relative factors remain unchanged. Whenever there is any change in any of these three fundamental relative factors, the reaction won’t be equal to the action. These three fundamental relative factors are the spatial factor, temporal factor, and personal factor.
items.statement: The Newtonian principle of equal and opposite reaction is modified to hold only when time, space, and person remain strictly unaltered; otherwise the reaction deviates.
items.title: Action and Reaction

items.quote: Yes, go on doing good actions. And while doing good actions, offer the good reactions, the good reactive momenta, offer it at the altar of Parama Puruśa. “Oh, Parama Puruśa! All these good actions done by me should be enjoyed by You, not by me. Let the bad reactions of bad actions be undergone by me, but let the good reactions of good actions be enjoyed by You. What good actions I did in the past, what good actions I am doing at present, and what good actions I will be doing in the future, the reactions should go to You. You please enjoy it. I don’t want to enjoy it. Let me suffer. Let me undergo the suffering for my bad deeds, and may You enjoy the good fruits of my good actions.” Then you won’t be undergoing any good reactions of good actions, and you will attain Salvation. This is the only way, and it is a very intelligent way.
items.statement: To achieve liberation without being bound by the consequences of positive actions, one must surrender the fruits of good deeds to Parama Puruśa while enduring the reactions of bad deeds.
items.title: Action and Reaction

items.qualifiers: These three rules represent different facets of a single integrated process.
items.quote: There are three processes for attaining freedom from the bondage of action: (1) relinquishing any desire for the fruits of action, or Phalákáḿkśá Tyága, (2) Abandoning the vanity of performing an act, or Kartrtvábhimána Tyága, and (3) surrendering all actions unto Brahma. All of these have to be followed in the individual life, but it must be kept in mind that they all have to be strictly observed. To be more explicit, these rules are the different aspects of one and the same process.
items.statement: Liberation from the bondages of action is accomplished through three unified methods: relinquishing desire for fruits, discarding doership vanity, and surrendering all actions to Brahma.
items.title: Actions and Their Results (Karma and Karmaphala)

items.quote: What are the special characteristics of Bhágavata dharma? They are: vistára (expansion), rasa (flow), seva (service), and tadsthiti (realization of the Supreme). The first criterion of human greatness is the spirit of expansion. Human beings want to give an aesthetic expression to all internal feelings and propensities; this is the first aspect of Bhágavata dharma - vistára.
items.statement: Bhágavata dharma is defined by four core components: vistára (expansion), rasa (flow), sevá (service), and tadsthiti (realization of the Supreme).
items.title: Ádarsha and Iśt́a

items.qualifiers: Strenuous work must be strictly avoided.
items.quote: Normally, in the advanced stage of pregnancy, women are not permitted to do physical labour. This is wrong. Women in that condition should be allowed to do a little work. (The same principle applies to pregnant animals.) Otherwise, there remains a risk during labour. Pregnant women and female animals may work half of what they usually do at other times; but under no circumstances should they be allowed to do strenuous work, as it may lead to premature delivery or stillbirth.
items.statement: Pregnant women should engage in moderate physical activity (about half their normal workload) rather than remaining completely inactive, to avoid complications during labour.
items.title: Advice for Pregnant Women

items.quote: According to most scholars these occult powers are eight in number and their combined name is aeshii siddhi [the eight occult powers]. They are ańimá, laghimá, mahimá (garimá), iishitva, vashitva, prápti, prakámya, and antaryámitva. Some people do not accept occult powers such as káyavasáyitva, moving from one body to another, entering another’s body, telepathy, clairvoyance, hypnotism, mesmerism, etc., as aśt́asiddhi; they say that these are included within one or the other of the accepted eight occult powers.
items.statement: Occult power (aeshii siddhi or vibhúti) comprises eight distinct capacities: ańimá, laghimá, mahimá/garimá, iishitva, vashitva, prápti, prakámya, and antaryámitva.
items.title: Aekya to Aekśava (Discourse 13)

items.quote: As long as I enjoy, my unit existence persists. As I exist, I can enjoy, and when I lose myself, when ́I’ becomes dear to that Entity, when ́I’ becomes the source of joy to that Entity, a stage is finally reached when my unit existence is completely lost in that Entity. The losing of oneself, the state of being lost or as a matter of fact, the beginning of the process of losing oneself to the very source of joy, is known as mohanavijiṋána, or the science of supra-aesthetics. And the Entity to whom we lose ourselves is Mohana, or the embodiment of enchantment.
items.statement: Mohanavijiṋána (supra-aesthetic science) is the stage where the lover's individual entity dissolves as they become the object of delight for Parama Puruśa (Mohana).
items.title: Aesthetic Science and Saḿgiita

items.quote: These days, due to reckless deforestation in many parts of the world, forest trees are deprived of that source of water. If this wanton destruction of plants and trees is not stopped, then in the near future the rainfall will drastically decrease and the frequency and intensity of floods will increase. Consequently lush, green vegetation will be transformed into arid deserts. This has already happened in the south-eastern portion of Rajasthan.
items.statement: Reckless deforestation eliminates the natural soil-water regulation provided by root systems, resulting in diminished rainfall, increased flood frequency, and desertification.
items.title: Afforestation

items.quote: Átmajiṋánam means a stage of objectlessness. Seeing one’s own self within oneself and not guiding any cognitive or psychic faculty towards any objectivity. You have got so many psychic faculties. You have got so many cognitive faculties, too but you always try to goad your psychic and cognitive faculties to other objects. But, if you withdraw all your psychic and cognitive faculties and goad these faculties towards yourself and be at peace without coming in contact with any objective world that phase of your mind and spirit, that stance of [[non-]]relativity, is átmajiṋánam.
items.statement: Átmajiṋánam (self-knowledge) is defined as a non-relative state of objectlessness achieved when all cognitive and psychic faculties are retracted from the external world into the self.
items.title: Ágama and Nigama

items.quote: The fundamental characteristic of any developed economy is this: about thirty percent to forty-five percent of the people should remain engaged in agriculture and the rest of the population should be employed in industry or other sectors of the economy. Excessive pressure on agriculture is not a sign of a healthy economy. At present about seventy-five percent of the Indian population is dependent upon agriculture for its livelihood.
items.statement: A balanced, healthy economy requires thirty to forty-five percent of the populace engaged in agriculture, with the rest employed in industrial and other sectors.
items.title: Agrarian Revolution

items.qualifiers: The ratio to laborers must never decrease and should increase over time.
items.quote: According to PROUT, in the first phase of agrarian revolution private ownership of land within the cooperative system will be recognized. People should have the right to employ labour for cultivation, but in such cases fifty percent of the total produce should be distributed as wages to the agricultural labourers who work in the cooperative. That is, the owners of the land will get fifty percent of the total produce and those who create the produce through their labour will get the other fifty percent. This ratio must never decrease – rather it should increase in favour of the agricultural labourers who work in the cooperative.
items.statement: In the initial phase of agrarian reform, fifty percent of cooperative agricultural yield must go to the landholder and fifty percent to the laborers performing the work.
items.title: Agrarian Revolution

items.quote: The idea of Gańesha is a prehistoric one: it proves the supremacy of the group leader, or the head of the clan, of prehistoric days. With the decline of the matrilineal order, and with the increasing growth of the patrilineal order, the group leader became more and more powerful. Thus Gańesha precedes all other entities in order of preference.
items.statement: Gańesha originated as a prehistoric group leader (gańapati) representing clan survival and leadership, entirely unrelated to Shiva, Párvatii, or Durgá.
items.title: All Bask In the Glory of Shiva – 3 (Discourse 8)

items.quote: Now in the process of synthesis among Jain, Buddhist and Shivottara Tantra, there evolved a new concept, the concept of Dashamahávidyá [Ten Mahávidyás], centring around those deities who had general influence in all three systems of Tantra. The idea of Dashamahávidyá arose out of ten Tantric deities, some from Jain Tantra, some from Buddhist Tantra and some from Shivottara Tantra.
items.statement: The Dashamahávidyá emerged from an ideological synthesis between Jain Tantra, Buddhist Tantra, and Post-Shiva Tantra following the invention and spread of written scripts.
items.title: All Bask in the Glory of Shiva – 1 (Discourse 6)

items.quote: This Ardha-Náriishvara Shiva is a personification of a philosophical idea: that Shiva and Shakti – knowledge and energy – work in harmony. Energy is a blind force. A little child may die of electrocution, because electricity is merely a form of energy devoid of consciousness; being a blind force, it never stops to think that it is killing an innocent child. Thus there should be proper coordination between energy and cognition. This energy, unless guided and controlled by consciousness, may indulge in destructive activities.
items.statement: The image of Ardha-Náriishvara Shiva symbolizes the philosophical necessity of unifying blind operative energy (Prakrti) with conscious cognition (Puruśa).
items.title: All Bask in the Glory of Shiva – 2 (Discourse 7)

items.qualifiers: Internal characteristics exist only in the form of internal ideation/conation.
items.quote: Is Brahma really devoid of external characteristics? Yes. There is nothing outside Him and thus no way to discern His characteristics from without. So is He also devoid of internal characteristics? No. Regarding actional expression, He is certainly devoid of characteristics, but where there is an expression of internal assimilation, He certainly does possess characteristics. In His internal body there is an incessant flow of thought which causes the creation, maintenance and dissolution of the entire universe.
items.statement: Brahma lacks external characteristics because no second entity exists outside Him, yet possesses internal characteristics in the form of Cosmic psychic ideation.
items.title: All Shine with His Effulgence

items.quote: Why does kiirtana have to be vocalized? The science behind it is that when you do kiirtana loudly your mind remains engaged. It cannot do anything else. At that time it is not possible to abuse someone or to have a worldly conversation. The mind is busy vocalizing, rather I will say that it is given over to the vocalization. The vocal cords are busy in that, the mind is employed in that thought, and the ears are hearing it, they don’t have any chance to go here and there. For this reason the rule of vocalizing kiirtana loudly makes it both heard and sung. Kiirtan is not done softly.
items.statement: Kiirtana must be sung out loud because loud vocalization fully engages the vocal cords, hearing, and mental focus, preventing the mind from drifting into negative thoughts.
items.title: “Always Do the Kiirtana of the Lord”

items.quote: Sukrtaermánavo bhútvá jiṋániicenmokśamápnuyát. By passing through so many frameworks of so many animals and so many other beings, one acquires the human framework, one gets the human structure. And when one gets the human structure, one becomes eligible for self-knowledge, átmajiṋánam. And by dint of acquiring that átmajiṋánam, one attains salvation. So Shiva’s reply is that the minimum qualification for getting salvation, for doing sádhaná, is just a human structure. He never said that it should be a male structure, that it should be the body of a male. He said it should be the body of a human being.
items.statement: The sole minimum qualification for spiritual practice and attaining salvation is possessing a human body, entitling women and men to equal rights without distinction.
items.title: An Equal Birthright

items.quote: When one no longer makes such a mistake, that is, when one always remembers to use guru mantra before starting any activity, one is said to have attained “dhruva smrti” or “fixed memory”. Dhruva means “fixed”, “stationary”. When, by dint of sádhaná, one establishes oneself in dhruva smrti, one experiences an unbroken flow of bliss in one’s mind. In the scriptures, this intense spiritual bliss is termed “dharma meghánanda”.
items.statement: Dhruva smrti (fixed memory) is achieved when an aspirant consistently maintains unbroken awareness of the guru mantra before undertaking any activity, resulting in dharma meghánanda.
items.title: An Exemplary Life

items.quote: And it is called “proto” in the sense that it is a flickering entity – it is like a flickering flame, not like a steady flame. It is not something unruffled or fixed; it is expressive of movement. Hence it is not complete psycho-spirituality but proto-psycho-spirituality. And the mobility portion within the systalsis of proto-psycho-spirituality is purely psychic; and the blissful staticity within the systalsis is purely spiritual. So it is a happy blending of psychic and spiritual strata. Thus I call it “psycho-spirituality”.
items.statement: Proto-psycho-spirituality is an active mental stance where mobility is psychic and staticity is spiritual, aligning unit consciousness with the circum-rotarian universal Nucleus to overcome narrow socio-sentiments.
items.title: An Ideology for a New Generation (Discourse 10)

items.qualifiers: conditioned on the state of mind (pure spiritual thoughts vs. crude thoughts)
items.quote: At that time if one’s mind remains engaged in pure spiritual thoughts that hormone flows from the pineal gland down the left side to the pituitary gland, and then to other plexii, glands and sub-glands, nerve fibres, nerve cells, veins and arteries, etc. This excessive flow of pineal hormone revitalises all the lower plexii. On the other hand, if one’s mind remain preoccupied with crude thoughts then the pineal hormone gets burnt up at the pituitary plexus.
items.statement: When a spiritual aspirant maintains pure spiritual thoughts, pineal gland secretion flows down to the pituitary gland and other plexuses, revitalizing the lower nerve centers; crude thoughts cause this secretion to burn up at the pituitary plexus.
items.title: Anindyánanda Rasa Samádhi

items.qualifiers: distinct characteristic among the thirty-two prominent bliss states
items.quote: The special characteristics of this samádhi is that it cannot be attained by one’s own personal efforts, but only through the grace of the Guru.
items.statement: Anindyánanda rasa samádhi cannot be achieved through individual effort alone; it requires the grace of the Guru.
items.title: Anindyánanda Rasa Samádhi

items.qualifiers: comparing the terms conduct (ácarańa) and character (ácára)
items.quote: Ácára is the composite of eating, living, behaviour and all external expressions and their concerning mentalities. Thus we can say that ácára is the reflection of life in its totality. Just as one cannot comment on the conduct of a person if they do not know them very well, one is even less able to comment on their character.
items.statement: Ácarańa refers to conduct or external expressions of a portion of life, whereas ácára reflects the composite of eating, living, and mentalities constituting the totality of life.
items.title: Áṋka to Ád́hya (Discourse 4)

items.qualifiers: distinguishing ancient manuscript copying from modern metaphorical sense
items.quote: Á – drsh + ghaiṋ = ádarsha: that which we keep in front of us or watch, and follow while we act. In ancient times, when there was no scope for printing, that authentic manuscript that the pandits would place in front of themselves and transcribe or copy was called the ádarsha manuscript. Whenever some person or individual was held up before others so that they could watch him and do as he did, or try to emulate him, then that individual was called ádarsha puruśa.
items.statement: Ádarsha etymologically denotes an authentic model or standard to follow, whereas in Vedic usage it meant a mirror.
items.title: Áṋt to Áhiira (Discourse 5)

items.quote: In the same way, many people use the word bhaotika to mean “concerning ghosts”. Bhúta + t́hak = bhaotika. This word means “physical” or “material”, that is, concerning the five elements. The word bhúta, which is used in the sense of “ghost” or “spirit”, is a native Bengali word, thus the word bhaotika cannot be created by adding the suffix t́hak. If we say bhaotika káńd́a, it does not mean “ghostly affair”, but rather “material affair”. Thus it is better not to use the word bhaotika to mean “concerning ghosts”. What we call bhúta in Bengali is called preta in Sanskrit. From preta one gets the word praetika, although its use is extremely limited.
items.statement: The term bhúta as a colloquial Bengali term for ghost cannot be modified with the Sanskrit suffix t́hak to mean ghostly; bhaotika technically denotes the material or elemental realm of the five fundamental factors, while praetika pertains to ghosts.
items.title: Aoktha/Aokthaka/Aokthika to Aokśa (Discourse 15)

items.qualifiers: distinguishing direct revelation from mediated perception
items.quote: What we receive through some medium is known as “prápta vastu” and what we receive directly from the Nucleus of the universe, what we receive from the Parama Puruśa is called “ápta vastu”. Now in this realm of spirituality, whatever we receive, we receive directly from Him, and not through any medium, and that is why the secrets of his spirituality are known as “ápta vákyam” and not “prápta vákyam”. Prápta vákyas come through different media, through different physical media, and that is why they may vary, or undergo metamorphosis. After their metamorphosis, they may come within the scope of relativity and undergo distortion.
items.statement: Prápta vastu refers to inferential or physical entities received through intermediary media subject to distortion, whereas ápta vákya represents spiritual truth received directly from the Cosmic Nucleus.
items.title: Ápta Vákya and Prápta Vákya

items.qualifiers: categorized strictly by mental propensities/desires at death
items.quote: It is said that there are seven kinds of luminous bodies: yakśa, siddha, gandharva, kinnara, vidyádhara, Prakrtiliina and videhaliina. They are categorized according to their respective psychologies.
items.statement: Luminous bodies (devayonis) are composed of only three fundamental factors (luminous, aerial, ethereal) without solid or liquid elements, and are categorized into seven classes based on psychology: yakśa, siddha, gandharva, kinnara, vidyádhara, Prakrtiliina, and videhaliina.
items.title: Are Ghosts Hallucinations?

items.qualifiers: lasts only for a few minutes and relies on a living person's ectoplasm
items.quote: A living person’s ectoplasmic cells become the mental body of a dead person for a few minutes until – after a few minutes – that mental body again dies. This mental body I will call preśitamánas – “recreated mind.”
items.statement: A preśitamánas (recreated mind) occurs when the ectoplasmic cells of a living person temporarily associate with the potential mind of a deceased person, granting it a functional mental body for a few minutes.
items.title: Are Ghosts Hallucinations?

items.quote: This exalted state beyond even aesthetic science is called mohana vijiṋána or supra-aesthetic science. That is, those who are enthralled with delight can no longer experience anything at all, because their very entitative rhythm is almost lost.
items.statement: Mohana vijiṋána (supra-aesthetic science) is the state beyond aesthetic appreciation where the individual entity loses its separate identity and merges its entitative rhythm in the infinite rhythm of Parama Puruśa.
items.title: Supra-Aesthetic Science and Music

items.quote: When a man knows something, what is the actional side of knowing? The science of knowing is but the internal projection of external vibration; introversial projection of external feeling, external vibration, is known as knowledge. In philosophical language, you may say that knowledge means subjectivization of objectivities.
items.statement: Extroversial knowledge is the subjectivization of external objectivity, whereas true self-knowledge (átmajiṋánam) occurs when the subjective portion of the mind is metamorphosed into Consciousness.
items.title: Art and Science

items.qualifiers: temporary vs. permanent cessation of afflictions
items.quote: To obtain temporary liberation from pains and miseries, money or Artha is required but to attain permanent liberation, we need Paramártha. This is the basic difference between Artha and Paramártha.
items.statement: Artha provides temporary liberation from specific material afflictions, whereas Paramártha provides permanent cessation of all physical, psychic, and spiritual miseries.
items.title: Artha and Paramártha

items.qualifiers: biological basis for mental concentration and morality
items.quote: Mental expression is brought about through the vrttis, and the predominance of the vrttis depends on different glands of the body. There are many glands in the body and from each there is a secretion of a particular hormone. If there is any defect in the secretion of hormones or any defect in a gland, certain vrttis become excited.
items.statement: Psychic propensities (vrttis) are excited or regulated by hormonal secretions from bodily glands, and asanas rectify glandular defects to help control these propensities for meditation.
items.title: Ásanas

items.qualifiers: exemptions apply to postures such as padmásana, siddhásana, viirásana, etc.
items.quote: Practise ásanas only while breath is flowing through the left nostril or both nostrils; do not practise ásanas when the breath flows only through the right nostril.
items.statement: Ásanas must be practised only when breath is flowing through the left nostril (Id́á) or both nostrils (Suśumná), and never when flowing solely through the right nostril, with exemptions for specific postures.
items.title: Ásanas

items.qualifiers: depends on diet, environmental catalytic agents, and physical activity
items.quote: The lymphatic glands supply raw material – lymph – to the factories – the glands – and the surplus lymph goes to the brain and provides food for the nerve cells in the cranium. When lymph comes in contact with an activated gland, hormones are created.
items.statement: The lymphatic glands supply raw lymph as a foundational hormone to the endocrine glands, while surplus lymph nourishes cranial nerve cells; green vegetation rich in chlorophyll accelerates lymph production, fostering higher intellectual development.
items.title: Aspects of Bio-Psychology

items.qualifiers: even sentient food cannot fully offset negative environments
items.quote: Positive psychic and positive physical environments are positive catalytic agents, and negative psychic and negative physical environments are negative catalytic agents. Even if the food one eats is sentient, but the environment is negative, it is detrimental to mental progress.
items.statement: Positive psychic and physical environments serve as positive catalytic agents that enhance lymph and hormone creation, whereas negative environments act as negative catalytic agents.
items.title: Aspects of Bio-Psychology

items.qualifiers: only singular eśańá toward the Cosmic Nucleus achieves liberation
items.quote: Where there is no Esana, there is annihilation of existence. Hence the existence of Esana is essential. It is said above that when a man runs after varieties, he gets none. Sometimes a man thinks to be a Minister, sometimes a Secretary, sometimes a poet. There are thousand and one desires. Because of this Esana is not made fully.
items.statement: Eśańá (desire or pursuit of pabulum) is essential for living existence; when directed towards worldly multiplicity it leads to exhaustion, but when channeled exclusively toward Parama Puruśa as singular devotion (Bhakti), it accelerates Pratisaiṋcara and leads to the merger of existence into Shivatva.
items.title: Astitva and Shivatva

items.qualifiers: saiṋcara contains only prota yoga; pratisaiṋcara contains both ota and prota yoga
items.quote: Association of Puruśottama with the Cosmic Mind, whereby He functions as the witnessing entity, is called prota yoga; association of Puruśottama with the unit minds separately and individually, whereby He functions as the witnessing entity for each individual unit mind, is called ota yoga. His association with the unit minds in collectivity is also termed prota yoga. Thus in saiṋcara there is only prota yoga but in pratisaiṋcara both prota yoga and ota yoga are there.
items.statement: Prota yoga refers to Puruśottama's witnessing association with the Cosmic Mind and with unit minds collectively, while ota yoga refers to His individual witnessing association with each unit mind in Pratisaiṋcara.
items.title: Átman, Paramátman and Sádhaná

items.qualifiers: belongs to the devotional sentiment of Tantra
items.quote: They get merged in Puruśottama who aspire for Him as the ultimate destiny, but those who aim at mokśa, where sádhaná is the complete surrender of self into That (Nirguńa Brahma, the Objectless Consciousness), get out of this Brahma Cakra by a tangential touch. At this point of tangential touch is the abode of Táraka Brahma (who resides within the scope of both Nirguńa and Saguńa Brahma).
items.statement: Táraka Brahma is located at the tangential point of contact with Brahma Cakra, capable of fulfilling the functions of both Nirguńa Brahma and Saguńa Brahma, and represents a devotional reality rather than a philosophical figure.
items.title: Átman, Paramátman and Sádhaná

items.qualifiers: etymological and philosophical distinction of eating states
items.quote: Ashana is derived from ash (ashnute) plus the suffix lyut́. Ashana means “to eat”. Anashana means “not to eat” in the sense of not being able to eat. Áhára also means “to eat” but áhára means “to eat something that has been carefully selected”. Thus anáhára means “not eating carefully selected items” – filling the stomach with worthless edibles. Hence anáhára and anashana are not identical. The meaning of upavása is completely opposite. Upa means “near”. Upavása means “to stay in close proximity”. Most of the year people are busy with matter. If one fixes a specific day to suspend one’s worldly activities and remain near God or live near God then it is called upavása. When all other worldly activities have been suspended, then on that day one should also refrain from eating. Therefore eating is discontinued on that day. Thus these three words, anashana, anáhára and upavása are quite different from each other.
items.statement: Anashana means involuntary inability to eat; anáhára means eating unselected, worthless food; and upavása means consciously suspending worldly activities to stay in close proximity to God while refraining from food.
items.title: Auṋka to Akśa (Discourse 3)

items.qualifiers: moral categorization of commission versus omission
items.quote: Among Pátaka, there are two classes, two branches. One is Pápa, the other is Pratyaváya. Pápa means to do the “don’ts” of life. Don’t steal. If you steal, it will be Pápa because you are doing the “don’ts” of life. Pratyaváya means not to do the “dos” of life. You should help a man in distress. You should help the suffering humanity. These are the dos of life. If you do not do them, you are doing Pratyaváya. Pápa plus Pratyaváya is Pátaka. There are two kinds of Pátaka.
items.statement: Within vice (pátaka), pápa consists of performing prohibited actions ('don'ts' of life), whereas pratyaváya consists of failing to perform obligatory duties ('dos' of life).
items.title: Auto-Suggestion and Outer Suggestion

items.qualifiers: subject to formal initiation in sannyása and governance under the Avadhúta Board with purodhá pramukha approval
items.quote: If it is not possible for anyone to discharge his/her family responsibilities because he/she is completely preoccupied with the propagation of dharma and social service, and if such a person takes formal initiation in sannyása, he/she will be called an avadhúta/iká.
items.statement: An avadhúta/iká is defined as a person who takes formal initiation in sannyása because family responsibilities cannot be discharged due to complete dedication to the propagation of dharma and social service.
items.title: Avadhúta/iká and Avadhúta Board

items.quote: Avidyá Tantrics make use of this sort of process. With the help of their sense organs and ectoplasms they create positive hallucinations. In Sanskrit this science is called rákśasii vidyá. (Rákśasa does not refer to any monstrous type of animal, but to a particular group of humans. ( 2 ) ) With the help of your mental eyes and your psychic power you can create an image visible to the eyes of an ordinary person. You can actually suspend the power of vision of another person so that he sees the object you want him to see. This is called rákśasii máyá.
items.statement: In Avidyá Tantra, creating positive hallucinations using sense organs and psychic power to suspend another's power of vision is called rákśasii vidyá or rákśasii máyá.
items.title: Avidyá – Excerpt A

items.qualifiers: distinguishes between Iishvarakot́i and Brahmakot́i sádhakas
items.quote: Iishvarakot́i sádhakas, through special efforts, can master some negative and positive powers, and may apply them to certain human beings, places, or ideas. But a Brahmakot́i sádhaka can apply those powers throughout the entire universe at one time, through his prota yoga. Moreover, with the help of ota yoga, he can apply his power to an individual place or person if he so wishes.
items.statement: Iishvarakot́i spiritual aspirants master localized occult powers, whereas Brahmakot́i aspirants apply their powers universally through prota yoga or individually via ota yoga.
items.title: Avidyá – Excerpt B

items.qualifiers: fundamental distinction between branches of Tantra
items.quote: The difference between the two is that Avidyá Tantra invariably leads one towards crudification, and ultimately annihilation; whereas Vidyá Tantra leads one from crude to subtle, and invigorates the human life, mind and soul – in fact the whole existence – with exuberant joy.
items.statement: Avidyá Tantra leads to crudification and ultimate conversion into inert matter, while Vidyá Tantra leads from the crude to the subtle and invigorates existence.
items.title: Avidyá – Excerpt C

items.qualifiers: applies to literal and non-literal study
items.quote: Now, there may be defects in both literal and non-literal study; thus knowledge acquired through study cannot be accepted as absolute, nor should it be. There are two kinds of defect. What is the first? Defect due to ignorance. And the second is defect due to change in tempor [time].
items.statement: Knowledge acquired through study suffers from two fundamental non-transcendental defects: defect due to ignorance and defect due to changes across time.
items.title: Awakened Conscience (Discourse 9)

items.quote: In the first stage you study; in the second you analyse the positive and negative sides; and in the third stage you arrive at “blissful or non-blissful, auxiliary or non-auxiliary.” ( 2 ) When you complete this whole process of logical reasoning, the outcome is your “awakened conscience”. This state of awakened conscience is what is called “rationalistic mentality.”
items.statement: Awakened conscience or rationalistic mentality is the final discriminatory decision on whether a logical conclusion promotes human and spiritual welfare.
items.title: Awakened Conscience (Discourse 9)

items.qualifiers: speaker's qualification on traditional scriptural views
items.quote: Though procrastination is a very serious defect according to the scriptures, personally, I do not totally accept this view. In my opinion, the capacity to delay noble deeds is a vice, but the capacity to delay sinful deeds is a virtue. If I waste time and postpone good deeds until tomorrow, it is extremely bad. But if I postpone bad deeds until tomorrow, it is good. While delaying something bad, one’s mind may change and one may decide not to do it after all. Hence, procrastination in the case of bad deeds is a virtue.
items.statement: Procrastination is harmful when applied to noble deeds, but serves as a virtue when delaying harmful or wicked actions.
items.title: Bad Habits Which Should Be Given Up

items.quote: “Bandhu”, “suhrd”, “mitram” and “sakhá” – these are almost synonymous but their meanings are not quite the same. “Bandhu” is one who cannot bear separation, cannot live away. The bondage is so strong that they cannot live away. For this reason they are called “bandhu”. It has not any correct English synonym and so I am compelled to use the word “bandhu”. Those who go together because they have no differences of opinion are called “suhrd”.
items.statement: Classical Sanskrit terms for companionship carry precise definitions: bandhu is one who cannot bear separation, suhrd agrees without differences, mitram is an occupational colleague, and sakhá shares unified vital feeling.
items.title: Bandhu, Suhrd, Mitram and Sakhá

items.qualifiers: general economic rule with current exceptions like Japan
items.quote: The lessons of history suggest that no country should invest huge amounts of money in industries which rely on supplies of raw materials from other countries. At present Japan is an exception to this rule. However, if the people in those countries which supply raw materials to Japan become politically conscious and start developing industries based on their own raw materials, Japan will face great difficulty.
items.statement: A nation should avoid investing heavily in industries that depend on raw materials imported from other countries.
items.title: Bangladesh

items.qualifiers: health and climatic conditions permitting for additional sandhyas
items.quote: Bathing at midnight is prohibited. One must not take a bath in the midnight sandhyá. Everyone must bathe in any one of the other three sandhyás. Taking into consideration one’s health and the climatic conditions, one may also bathe in one or both of the remaining two sandhyás.
items.statement: Bathing must be executed following a sequential order of water application and is prohibited during the midnight sandhyá.
items.title: Bathing Procedure and Pitr Yajiṋa

items.qualifiers: evaluates medium subtlety relative to inner human emotion
items.quote: Human beings cannot express in the form of spoken language even one per- cent of what they feel deep inside; they cannot express in writing everything that they can express in spoken language; and they cannot express through drawings everything that they can express in writing. This is why I said elsewhere that the art of painting is a subtler art - because here even higher expressions remain confined within a few lines of drawing. It is like a violin, which has no frets, amid musical instruments studded with frets.
items.statement: Painting is considered a subtler art than spoken or written language because higher, ineffable expressions remain condensed within lines without acoustic mediation.
items.title: Ráŕh – 24.

items.quote: Actually he is not a sinner, but if he thinks like this, that “I am a sinner, I am a sinner,” what will happen? – he will actually become a sinner, because it is the characteristic of the human mind that it takes the form of its object. So when a man thinks, “I am a sinner, I am a sinner, O Lord, I am a sinner, O Lord, I am a sinner,” then actually he will become a sinner. So such a psychology is fundamentally defective. You must never think that you are a sinner.
items.statement: Internalizing a sinner's psychology causes a person to actually become a sinner because the human mind inevitably takes the form of its ideational object.
items.title: Be Free from All Complexes

items.quote: “Japa” is of three types. One is called “mánasika”; that is, you are repeating it within your mind, you are the only entity that hears. The second is the kind of japa where you open your lips, but it is only you who hears. The third is “vacanika”; that is, with the help of your vocal chord, you are creating a sound. This japa is the worst, and the best is mánasika.
items.statement: Japa is classified into three forms: mánasika (internal mental repetition), lip-movement without audible sound, and vácanika (vocal utterance), of which mánasika is the best and vácanika the worst.
items.title: “Be a Ship to Us, Lord”

items.quote: Consequently, Shalibáhana rejected the lunar calendar system and 1387 years ago introduced a simple new system of calendar which is followed even today in Orissa, Assam, Bangladesh, and by the revenue collectors of North India.
items.statement: King Shalibáhana reformed the ancient Indian lunar calendar 1,387 years ago to align agricultural seasons and tax collections with the solar year starting in Agraháyań.
items.title: Bengali New Year

items.qualifiers: contrasting human dharma with animal or sectarian paths
items.quote: What is the meaning of this shloka? If one’s dharma is difficult to follow and others’ dharma is seemingly very easy to follow, it is still preferable to die while following one’s own dharma. Any other dharma may be very dangerous. Many people wrongly interpret “dharma” as being Hindu Dharma, Vaishnavite Dharma, Shaivite Dharma, etc. But actually “dharma” means mánava dharma [“human dharma”].
items.statement: In the Gita's injunction on svadharma, dharma represents Bhágavata dharma (human dharma comprising vistára, rasa, and sevá), rather than specific communal or religious dogmas.
items.title: “Better to Die . . .” – 1 / It Is Better to Die While Following Bhágavata Dharma

items.qualifiers: applies to physical and psychic strata
items.quote: And here lies the speciality of human beings. But I will not say that it is the speciality of human beings, because in psychic spheres the pleasure you get is nothing but a sort of positive projection of your mind. It creates nothing concrete, nothing lasting. And whenever this sort of positive projection takes place, there comes another projection, a negative projection, just to bring the mind back to normalcy. That is, the psychic pleasure that you get is counteracted or neutralized by a negative projection – by the pain you get due to a negative projection. Plus and minus make it zero. So I said there cannot be any development or any progress in physical or psychic spheres.
items.statement: Purely psychic pleasures cannot yield permanent progress because every positive projection creates an equal and opposite negative projection that neutralizes it.
items.title: Beyond Temporary Experience

items.quote: He is deva. What is deva? The word comes from the root “div”, which means “the Supreme vibrational entity” or “the Supreme vibratory entity” – that which vibrates everything. He Himself is vibration personified, and He by His nature vibrates everything. He is the Supreme motivation. Wherever there is vibration, it is deva.
items.statement: The word deva is derived from the root 'div', designating the Supreme vibrational entity that motivates and vibrates all existence.
items.title: Beyond the Periphery

items.quote: Shiva proclaimed, “You are all mine. Whatever hill you live on you are still my own. I will think well of you. I will think about your collective welfare. I will work for your collective well-being. Come one and all to me safely and fearlessly and tell me your needs. I will help you. Átmagotraḿ parityajya Shivagotraḿ pravishatu [‘Leave your own gotra and enter Shivagotra’].”
items.statement: Lord Shiva abolished clan-based gotras by initiating male and female practitioners equally into kápálika sádhaná under the designations Bhaerava and Bhaeravii in the common family of Shivagotra.
items.title: Bhaerava and Bhaeravii

items.quote: Bhágavata dharma is dependent on three factors: vistara (expansion), rasa (flow) and sevá (service). The literal meaning of the word vistára is expansion, that is, to direct the mind toward the vast Cosmic Entity. This psychic movement towards the vast Cosmic Entity is not dependent on external factors.
items.statement: Bhágavata dharma is founded on three pillars: vistára (psychic expansion), rasa (attunement with the Cosmic flow), and sevá (unilateral selfless service).
items.title: Bhágavata Dharma

items.quote: When you offer something to a person and expect to receive something in return, it is a sort of commercial transaction. But when you have no desire to receive anything in return for services rendered it is called true service, and here lies the basic difference between true service and commercial transactions.
items.statement: Commercial transactions involve reciprocal exchange, whereas true spiritual service is strictly unilateral without expecting anything in return.
items.title: Bhágavata Dharma

items.quote: The term setu connotes bridge. Its function is to connect two objects. Devotion is that bridge which connects jiiva (unit) with Shiva (Cosmic Consciousness). At first one has to know about this setu. He has to dissect and analyse minutely its every aspect, taking also the help of books. This is what is called the Sádhaná of knowledge, i.e., Jiṋána Sadhaná. The endeavour to move towards this Setu is called the Sádhaná of action, i.e., Karma Sádhaná.
items.statement: Devotion acts as a bridge (setu) that connects the unit consciousness (jiiva) with Cosmic Consciousness (Shiva) by subjectivizing objectivity.
items.title: Bhakti-Rúpa Setu (Devotion Acts Like a Bridge)

items.quote: Why is the approach of bhakti the best? The approach of jiṋána is through analysis and synthesis, passing along the systaltic route of movement, and there is pause and speed. During the phase of pause there is every chance of degeneration. And what happens in the approach of karma? Wherever one gets diverted from the goal of life, from the culminating point of one’s march, one becomes degenerated. Vanity may develop both in the case of jiṋána and in the case of karma. But the path of bhakti is harmless.
items.statement: Bhakti is superior to jiṋána and karma because it does not involve pause-phase degeneration or detachment from a personal spiritual goal.
items.title: Bhakti Is the Best

items.quote: Now, the attraction of a particular created being for another finite object is called káma, and one’s attraction for the Infinite Entity is called prema.
items.statement: Attraction directed toward finite entities is káma, whereas attraction focused upon the Infinite Entity is prema.
items.title: Bhakti, Mukti and Parama Puruśa

items.quote: There are three classifications within aparábhakti. When a so-called devotee (aparábhakti means they are not devotees, they are so-called devotees) says, “O Parama Puruśa, I am Your devotee,” and then says, “X is my enemy. Please kill him, please kill him!” this type of bhakti is called támasika bhakti. Actually it is not bhakti. When someone says, “O Parama Puruśa, I am Your devotee, but You know, I am not getting any employment, please arrange for my employment,” he is not trying to harm anybody, but he wants physical development or physical elevation, his [physical] betterment. His bhakti, his so-called bhakti, is known as rájasika bhakti. And that is also aparábhakti, and aparábhakti is not bhakti. And suppose someone says, “O Parama Puruśa, I am Your devotee, and You know, I want mukti, I want mukti,” and Parama Puruśa asks, “O my boy, why do you want mukti?” “Oh, I don’t find any charm in this world, because I lost my digestive power. Either give me back my digestive power or give me mukti.” This is sáttvikii bhakti. Actually sáttvikii bhakti is not bhakti; aparábhakti is not at all bhakti.
items.statement: Aparábhakti is categorized into támasika (seeking harm to others), rájasika (seeking personal material gain), and sáttvikii (seeking individual liberation due to worldly dissatisfaction).
items.title: Bhakti, Mukti and Parama Puruśa

items.quote: The two varieties of Anurakti exist only on account of the introverting or extroversial actions of the mind; that is extroversion denotes Aparánurakti, while introversion denotes Paránurakti. The externalizing forces subordinate a person to the sense organs and render him or her crude. Such a person is divested of his or her spiritual force. Paránurakti on the other hand releases a person from the grips of the Indriyas and through sublime meditations establishes him or her in the finer sublimated senses, in the infinite blessedness beyond the bounds of the Universe.
items.statement: Extroverted mental flow toward finite objects is aparánurakti (ásakti), while introverted flow directed toward Infinite Consciousness is paránurakti (bhakti).
items.title: Bhaktitattva

items.qualifiers: applies to lower four cakras up to anáhata
items.quote: During samádhi the vibration created in different parts of a sádhaka’s body are not controlled by the unit mind but by the Cosmic Mind. There is a feeling of indescribable bliss throughout the body which causes the sádhaka to shiver continuously. Bháva samádhi can be experienced in any of the four lower cakras. But as soon as the mind rises above the anáhata cakra a higher samádhi is experienced.
items.statement: Bháva samádhi occurs across the four lower cakras when psychic propensities are unified and physical/psychic vibrations become directly controlled by the Cosmic Mind.
items.title: Bháva Samádhi

items.quote: “Tadekaḿ smarámah”. What is smrti? “Anubhútivisayásampramośah smrtih”. While you conceive something or feel something with the help of your sensory organs, what does happen? The ectoplasmic structure of your mind takes the shape of that external object. Now when you by your interial force recreate that thing after some time within your mind without the help of any external object then this process of re-creation is known as “smrti”.
items.statement: Smrti (memory) is the internal cognitive process of recreating the ectoplasmic form of an object previously experienced by the sensory organs without external assistance.
items.title: Bhavámbodhipotam

items.qualifiers: mandatory qualifications for election in AMPS organizational structure
items.quote: The sadvipras (those who are well-established in Sixteen Points ( 1 ) ) of a bhukti must elect one bhukti pradhána from among themselves. The bhukti pradhána may or may not be an ácárya/á or a táttvika, but must be an educated family person. They will hold this post for three years, after which a fresh election will be held.
items.statement: The bhukti pradhána must be an educated family person elected from among the sadvipras of the bhukti for a term of three years.
items.title: Bhukti Pradhána

items.quote: Thus the only logical exposition is to say that the bhútas are not any new stuff but only the crudified forms of Cosmic citta, which get manifested at different stages of the saiṋcara process when the intermolecular and interatomic spaces decrease and chemical affinity increases due to the external pressure of static Prakrti.
items.statement: The physical bhútas emerge from the gradual crudification of Cosmic citta driven by static Prakrti, decreasing interatomic spaces while increasing chemical affinity.
items.title: Bhútatattva, Tanmátratattva and Indriyatattva

items.quote: This process of jad́asphot́a, as a result of which the crudest factor, solid, gets converted into certain subtler factors, may be termed “negative saiṋcara”: the solid factor can never, as a result of negative saiṋcara or jad́asphot́a, be transformed into a factor subtler than the subtlest physical factor, that is, the ethereal factor, because were it converted into the next subtler factor, citta, it would mean the withdrawal of the thought-waves of the Macrocosm.
items.statement: Negative saiṋcara through jad́asphot́a causes solid physical structures to explode under intense internal pressure and convert back into constituent subtler factors, up to ether.
items.title: Bhútatattva, Tanmátratattva and Indriyatattva

items.quote: The lymphatic glands supply raw material – lymph – to the factories – the glands – and the surplus lymph goes to the brain and provides food for the nerve cells in the cranium. When lymph comes in contact with an activated gland, hormones are created.
items.statement: Lymph is the primary hormonal raw material converted by glands into specific hormones, with surplus lymph nourishing cranial nerve cells.
items.title: Bio-Psychology

items.quote: The complexity of their cells increased and their bodies gradually became smaller, and eventually their mental power also increased. That is, the physical body first became very big, and after attaining a particular shape, the structure became complicated or complex; and from that moment, in the next stage or phase, as they moved along the path of introversion towards the Supreme Desideratum, their physical body went on diminishing in size and their psychic body was strengthened – their intellect increased. This is the adjustment or equilibrium or equipoise between biological structures and psychic metamorphosis.
items.statement: During pratisaiṋcara, living organisms undergo an increase in cellular complexity and mental development while physical body sizes tend to diminish.
items.title: Biological Transformation Associated with Psychic Metamorphosis and Vice Versa

items.quote: According to Shrii Prabhat Ranjan Sarkar, two “destructive tendencies” are predominant in the human mind: one is “intra-humanistic”, that is, the exploitation or oppression of fellow human beings; and the other is “inter-creature”, that is, the torture of animals, plants and other living beings. The inevitable result is the “catastrophic ruin of human life as well”.
items.statement: Human psychic destructive tendencies are classified into intra-humanistic (oppressing fellow humans) and inter-creature (torturing animals, plants, and other living entities).
items.title: Publisher's Note

items.quote: A birthday celebration should begin with collective Iishvara Prańidhána. Then the birthday person should receive blessings and the auspicious tilaka mark [sandal paste, kumkum, etc.] from the elders; accept salutations, garlands and sandal paste from the juniors; and then accept presents and food.
items.statement: A birthday celebration must begin with collective Iishvara Prańidhána before receiving blessings and tilaka from elders or salutations from juniors.
items.title: Birthday Ceremony

items.quote: Bhaga is a collection of six attributes: aeshvarya, viirya, yasha, shrii, jiṋána and vaerágya.
items.statement: Bhaga is defined as a collection of six specific attributes: occult power (aeshvarya), stamina (viirya), reputation (yasha), activating charm (shrii), spiritual knowledge (jiṋána), and renunciation or remaining unassailed by external attractions (vaerágya).
items.title: Blind Mind and Conscience

items.quote: There are ten organs – ten agents of the blind mind – and each and every organ can function in ten directions. Ten times ten is equal to one hundred. The agents of the mind can function in one hundred directions. So the blind mind has one hundred agents. Dhritarastra had one hundred sons – Duryodhana, Dushasana – one hundred in number; one hundred agents of the depraved mind, the blind mind, the polluted mind.
items.statement: The one hundred Kauravas represent the one hundred functional directions of the ten sensory and motor organs under the blind mind, while the five Pandavas represent the five stages of spiritual elevation through the lower chakras.
items.title: Blind Mind and Conscience

items.quote: When planning is prepared for the all-round growth of a single block exclusively, it is called “intra-block planning”.
items.statement: Intra-block planning deals with developmental schemes exclusively prepared for a single block, whereas inter-block planning involves economic ventures and cooperation among adjoining blocks to address problems traversing administrative boundaries.
items.title: Block-Level Planning

items.quote: In all cases, the maximum time limit for short-term planning should be six months, and the maximum time limit for long-term planning should be three years.
items.statement: Short-term planning must have a maximum time limit of six months, while long-term planning must have a maximum limit of three years.
items.title: Block-Level Planning

items.quote: This surplus protein decreases the alkaline portion of the blood and increases the acidic portion. Over-acidity of the blood weakens the blood-producing and blood-purifying organs such as the liver, kidneys, etc., and as a result the veins and arteries also get hardened and weak.
items.statement: Consuming surplus protein without physical labour decreases blood alkalinity and increases acidity, weakening purifying organs and hardening vessels, which forces the heart to over-exert and risks internal hemorrhaging.
items.title: Blood Pressure Diseases

items.quote: What is the way to counteract this socio-sentiment? The only way to eliminate it is to develop proto-spiritualistic mentality. The basis of this proto-spiritualistic mentality is sama-samája tattva [the principle of social equality].
items.statement: Rationalistic mentality serves as the primary weapon against geo-sentiment, whereas proto-spiritualistic mentality based on the principle of social equality (sama-samája tattva) counteracts socio-sentiment.
items.title: Bondages and Solutions (Discourse 2)

items.quote: Now this avidyá shakti, or Avidyámáyá, centrifugal force, has got a two-fold expression, two different expressions. One is called vikśepa shakti and the other is called ávarańii shakti.
items.statement: Avidyámáyá manifests through vikśepa shakti (repulsive force drifting entities away) and ávarańii shakti (covering force creating ignorance), whereas Vidyámáyá expresses through samvit shakti (spiritual awakening) and hládinii shakti (movement along the spiritual path).
items.title: Brahma Cakra

items.quote: For this reason I say that the present Cosmic Citta is limited, but the Cosmic mind-stuff is infinite and will continue throughout eternity.
items.statement: While the present quinquelemental Cosmic Citta is finite and shaped under Tamoguńa, the totality of Cosmic mind-stuff across eternity is infinite.
items.title: Brahma Krpáhi Kevalam

items.quote: The complexion of Niila Sarasvatii is blue. Developing a golden colour, she became Prajiṋá Páramitá, and then becoming all white, she turned into the Puranic goddess Sarasvatii.
items.statement: The Buddhist deity Niila Sarasvatii worshipped in Tibet was historically transformed into Prajiṋá Páramitá by adopting a golden color, and eventually evolved into the all-white Puranic deity Sarasvatii.
items.title: Buddhist Tantra, Jain Tantra and Hindu Tantra

items.qualifiers: so long as the economic reason exists
items.quote: Superstition is not the only reason behind the dowry system but it has also the economic background. Neither speeches nor removal of superstition will solve this knotty problem, so long as the economic reason exists.
items.statement: The dowry system cannot be solved solely through speeches or eradicating superstition because it is fundamentally driven by the economic liability assigned to females who lack opportunities to earn a livelihood.
items.title: Building a Healthy Society – Excerpt A

items.qualifiers: for three generations, ascending or descending
items.quote: The guardians should not allow matrimony between persons connected with each other either on the paternal or the maternal side for three generations, ascending or descending.
items.statement: In arranged marriages, guardians must not allow matrimony between persons connected on either paternal or maternal sides for three generations.
items.title: Building a Healthy Society – Excerpt H

items.quote: In case she remarries, she will forfeit the right to that property. In this case, the property will revert to the nearest relation of her father-in-law.
items.statement: A widow inherits the entire property of her husband and equal shares of in-laws' property with siblings-in-law without transfer rights, but forfeits the property to her husband's nearest relations if she remarries.
items.title: Building a Healthy Society – Excerpt H

items.quote: According to PROUT, capitalist exploitation is perpetuated in three spheres – the physical sphere, which we are well aware of, and the intellectual and spiritual spheres.
items.statement: Capitalist exploitation operates across three distinct arenas: the physical sphere, the intellectual sphere (elitist retention of knowledge), and the spiritual sphere (isolating spiritual practice in caves without serving society).
items.title: Capitalism in Three Spheres

items.quote: Here it is derived from “yuj” and means “transitional period”. On analysis of history we notice that as one epoch ends another begins: the kśatriya age is followed by the vipra age, the vipra age is followed by the vaeshya age and so on. The intervening period between the two epochs is called a yuga.
items.statement: A yuga is linguistically and historically defined not as mythological golden or iron ages, but as the transitional intervening period between two social epochs.
items.title: “Caraeveti Caraeveti” – “Move On, Move On”

items.quote: When the pulsations of mental feeling can not maintain parallelism with the pulsations of expressions of our nerves, then that propensity or those propensities or that controlling propensity is called kliśt́á-vrtti or klesha. When, they maintain that parallelism it is called or they are called akliśt́á-vrtti.
items.statement: Kliśt́á-vrtti or klesha occurs when the pulsations of mental feeling fail to maintain parallelism with the pulsations of nerve expressions, whereas akliśt́á-vrtti occurs when parallelism is maintained.
items.title: Cardinal Attributions of God

items.quote: Even the learned persons and the jiṋániis, the scholars know that this is this and that is that – or what is what and which is which. Even knowing everything they are entrapped by certain propensities. This particular nature of weakness is called abhinivesha.
items.statement: Abhinivesha is that form of avidyá in which scholars and wise individuals remain entrapped by irrational or harmful habits despite knowing their detrimental nature.
items.title: Cardinal Attributions of God

items.quote: Self-realization is the only knowledge. All other types of knowledge are simply the umbra and penumbra of knowledge,” because they do not contribute to any real understanding of objects.
items.statement: Direct knowledge or true knowledge occurs when knower, knowledge, and object merge in self-realization; all other intellectual operations are merely reflections and refractions that constitute shadows of knowledge.
items.title: The Cardinal Spirit of Action and the Supreme Stance of Devotion (Karma-Sannyása and Parábhakti)

items.quote: Accordingly, to some, the southern branch of Indo-Aryan music is Carnatic music, while others say it is Kodańd́a music or Deccan music.
items.statement: Carnatic music, also referred to as Deccan or Kodańd́a music, represents the southern branch of Indo-Aryan music originating in ancient Kodańd́abhumi.
items.title: Carnatic Music

items.quote: That which is mastered by continued arduous practice is called dhrupada .
items.statement: Dhrupada is defined as a musical method or fixed-scale style mastered through continued arduous practice, whose rigid confinement in specific notes necessitated the development of kheyál to provide melodic freedom.
items.title: Case and Case-Endings – 2 (Discourse 13)

items.quote: The ablative-indicating indeclinable theke comes from the old Burmese word táikiyá. The Burmese word táikiyá became táikyá in the southern Chittagong dialect and from this comes the modern Bengali thákiyá or theke.
items.statement: The Bengali ablative indeclinable 'theke' originates from the old Burmese word 'táikiyá', which transitioned via the southern Chittagong Arakanese-influenced dialect.
items.title: Case and Case-Endings – 3 (Discourse 14)

items.quote: The three types of locatives were created on the basis of these three – the locative of time, the locative of idea and the locative of base.
items.statement: Panini established three distinct bases for the locative case (adhikarańa): the locative of time (káládhikarańa), the locative of idea (bhávádhikarańa), and the locative of base (ádhárádhikarańa).
items.title: Case and Case-Endings – 4 (Discourse 15)

items.quote: A bháryá was not allowed any of the religious or social rights of her husband. But as the marriage was recognized, her children were entitled to the religious and social rights of their father. A bháryá was married only to perpetuate the lineage, not to give the woman dignity.
items.statement: Post-Shiva patriarchal society categorized marital relationships for women into distinct classes: patnii (equal social and religious rights), jáyá (social rights only), bháryá (no rights, meant purely for bearing male children), and kalatra (complete denial of paternal rights).
items.title: Casteism and the Decline of Women's Status – Excerpt D

items.qualifiers: principally the task of the causal mind
items.quote: The revival of experiences of past lives is what we call “extra-cerebral memory”, and is principally the task of the causal mind.
items.statement: Extra-cerebral memory refers to the revival of past-life experiences stored in the causal mind that functions independently of the new physical brain, usually remaining active up to age five.
items.title: Cerebral and Extra-Cerebral Memory

items.quote: If one still remembers one’s past life after that it becomes difficult to survive, because two minds will try to function in one body – the mind of this life and that of the previous one. A single body cannot tolerate the clashes of two minds, hence psycho-physical parallelism is lost leading to eventual death.
items.statement: If extra-cerebral memory persists beyond age twelve, psycho-physical parallelism is broken and death ensues due to the strain of two conflicting minds attempting to function within one physical body.
items.title: Cerebral and Extra-Cerebral Memory

items.quote: Due to excessive clash, some crude matter is pulverized, and cittáńu (ectoplasmic particles), or mind-stuff, is evolved.
items.statement: Due to excessive friction and clash within crude matter, solid matter is pulverized into mind-stuff (cittáńu), demonstrating that mind evolves out of matter in pratisaiṋcara.
items.title: Chapter 1

items.quote: When the mahat merges into the Átman, it is called nirguńásthiti (state of objectlessness) or nirvikalpa samádhi (the trance of indeterminate absorption, or total suspension, of the mind)].
items.statement: Savikalpa samádhi occurs when the unit citta and aham merge into the Macrocosmic Mahat, whereas nirvikalpa samádhi occurs when the Mahat merges into the objectless Átman.
items.title: Chapter 1

items.quote: Puruśottama is linked to each entity individually and to all entities collectively.
items.statement: Puruśottama is associated with each unit entity individually through ota yoga, and with all entities in their collective totality through prota yoga.
items.title: Chapter 2

items.quote: Long sleep in the causal mind is death.
items.statement: Death is defined as long sleep in the causal mind caused by vibrational disparity in psycho-physical parallelism.
items.title: Chapter 3

items.quote: If Shambhúliuṋga be the fundamental positivity, then the kulakuńd́alinii, lying at Svayambhúliuṋga, we may call the force of fundamental negativity.
items.statement: In the evolutionary process of the primordial triangle, Shambhúliuṋga is the root point of fundamental positivity, while Svayambhúliuṋga at the nadir of crudification contains kulakuńd́alinii as the force of fundamental negativity.
items.title: Chapter 4

items.quote: Accelerating the movement of the social cycle by the application of force is called “evolution”.
items.statement: Kránti is the acceleration of the social cycle through force, viplava is acceleration through tremendous force within a short time, vikránti is reversing the cycle through force, and prativiplava is reversing the cycle rapidly through tremendous force.
items.title: Chapter 5

items.qualifiers: After meeting the minimum requirements of all
items.quote: The surplus wealth should be distributed among meritorious people according to the degree of their merit.
items.statement: Society must guarantee the minimum requirements to all according to the age, and distribute surplus wealth among meritorious people according to the degree of their merit.
items.title: Chapter 5

items.quote: Culture is the expression of the intellectual stratum whereas civilization is the expression of the physical aspects of life.
items.statement: Culture represents the collective expression of the intellectual stratum of human life, whereas civilization denotes the subtle sense of refinement in physical expressions and conduct.
items.title: Civilization, Science and Spiritual Progress

items.quote: This bamboo flute was the first musical instrument created by nature. In the beginning, the same bamboo would be used as weapon as well as flute.
items.statement: The bamboo flute was humanity's first nature-derived musical instrument, evolving from hollow sticks originally carried as defensive weapons.
items.title: Classifications of Flute

items.quote: The physical bodies of human beings (mánava) are made of the quinquelemental factors: kśiti, ap, tejas, marut and vyoma. The physical bodies of danavas are made of ap, tejas, marut and vyoma – from four factors. And those of devatás are made of tejas, marut and vyoma and that is why their structures are not visible.
items.statement: Human bodies (mánava) consist of all five fundamental factors, dánava structures consist of four factors (omitting solid/kśiti), and devatá structures (deva yoni) consist of only three subtle factors (tejas, marut, and vyoma), rendering them invisible.
items.title: Cognitive Faculty – the Supreme Element

items.qualifiers: Subtle philosophical analysis of Puruśa/Witnessing Entity
items.quote: Citi Shakti has five qualities: shuddhá (absolutely pure), anantá (infinite), aparińámii (unchangeable), apratisaḿkramá (non-extroversive), and darshita viśayá (witness of the reflected object).
items.statement: Citi Shakti possesses five distinct qualities: absolute purity, infinitude, immutability, non-extroversiveness, and being the witness of the reflected object.
items.title: Cognitive Force and Psychic Practice

items.quote: Here ananta does not mean an object which has no finitude or end ; it means an entity which has no witness. The Supreme Entity can never come within the periphery of the mind for He has no witness.
items.statement: Infinitude (ananta) in relation to Citi Shakti specifically denotes an entity that has no witness rather than merely lacking a terminating end.
items.title: Cognitive Force and Psychic Practice

items.quote: The knowledge of the differentiation between átman (unit Cognitive Faculty) and buddhitattva (existential-I which results from mukhyá akliśt́ávrtti is called vivekakhyáti (viveka means discrimination; khyáti means ensconsement) or viśayaka samápatti (viśayaka means microcosmic object; samápatti means ultimate dissolution). When viveka khyáti or viśayaka saḿapatti become permanent it is called dharmamegha samádhi.
items.statement: Dharmamegha samádhi is attained when permanent discrimination between the unit cognitive faculty and existential-I is established.
items.title: Cognitive Force and Psychic Practice

items.quote: The voting rights should be vested in educated persons who have political consciousness and awareness of people’s problems. Age should not be a bar to voting right.
items.statement: Voting rights in a reformed democracy should be granted based on education and political consciousness rather than age.
items.title: Compartmentalized Democracy

items.qualifiers: Includes executive secretariat, cabinet/legislature, judiciary, and audit branch
items.quote: All the four branches mentioned above should be given the scope to function independently. Thus there will be four compartments. No compartment will function under another.]]
items.statement: A functional democracy requires four independent branches or compartments supervised by a benevolent dictatorship of a board of Sadvipras.
items.title: Compartmentalized Democracy

items.quote: The word briihi means “that in which is hidden the potential for an abundance of food”. Take paddy, for example. From paddy we get uncooked rice, cooked rice, puffed rice, beaten rice, khai [a variety of puffed rice], muŕki [parched rice coated with molasses], and so on. Thus another name for paddy is briihi (briihi → riihi → risi → ráis [rice]). The Modern English word “rice” comes from vriihi.
items.statement: The term briihi, which is the root of the word bahuvriihi and the etymological ancestor of the English word 'rice', means that which contains the potential for an abundance of food.
items.title: Compound Words (Discourse 18)

items.qualifiers: Occurs only in dead or dying celestial bodies
items.quote: Consequently a stage will come when there will be little interatomic space within the solid body. Now if static Prakrti exerts more pressure, [the equipoise of the component elements gets lost and] there will be a tremendous reaction within the physical body (affecting both the interial and exterial forces) resulting in structural dissociation. This is called jad́asphot́a.
items.statement: Jad́asphot́a refers to the material explosion and structural dissociation of a physical body occurring under extreme static pressure.
items.title: Concept of Guńábhivyakti and Jad́asphot́a

items.qualifiers: During the saiṋcara process of crudification
items.quote: Thus we find that the stronger the bondage, the cruder the thing becomes with the origination of more attributes. Due to external static pressure, the number of attributional peculiarities increases, but not the attributional capability.
items.statement: In the process of elemental crudification, attributional expression increases in variety and diversity while total attributional capacity remains constant.
items.title: Concept of Guńábhivyakti and Jad́asphot́a

items.quote: There are four main forms of consciousness – the waking state, the dream state, the deep sleep state, and turiiya [state of absorption of the self into Pure Consciousness]. Actually, in the turiiya form of consciousness, the Supreme Being exists in His own form or own nature, like milk remaining milk and not becoming curd or butter. Hence this is the controlling form of the other three forms.
items.statement: Consciousness manifests in four primary states: waking, dreaming, deep sleep, and turiiya, where turiiya serves as the pure, controlling state of the others.
items.title: Consciousness

items.quote: Of the different systems of production – the cooperative system, private enterprise, the sharecropping system and the commune system – the last one is the worst. The sharecropping system is slightly better than the commune system, and better still is private enterprise, but the best system is the cooperative system of production.
items.statement: Among production systems, the commune system ranks worst, followed in ascending order of quality by sharecropping, private enterprise, and the cooperative system.
items.title: Cooperative Production – Excerpt A

items.qualifiers: Applicable to khesári pulse cultivated in India
items.quote: These poisonous alkaloids reside between the skin and the outer portion of the pulse.
