They can be easily eliminated if the pulse is soaked in water overnight and the following morning the outer skin is removed by rubbing the pulses together. The inner portion of the pulse can be safely eaten by both cattle and human beings.
items.statement: The toxic alkaloids in khesári pulse that cause paralysis can be eliminated by soaking overnight and peeling away the outer skin.
items.title: Cooperative Production – Excerpt B

items.qualifiers: Fundamental distinction in PROUT socio-economic philosophy
items.quote: Where this cooperation is between free human beings, each with equal rights and mutual respect for each other, and each working for the welfare of the other, it is called “coordinated cooperation”. Where people do something individually or collectively, but keep themselves under other people’s supervision, then it is called “subordinated cooperation”.
items.statement: Cooperation is divided into coordinated cooperation, where free individuals interact with equal rights and mutual respect, and subordinated cooperation, which operates under hierarchical supervision.
items.title: Cooperatives

items.quote: PROUT advocates the reorganization of all agricultural land according to a phase-wise plan. In the first phase all uneconomic landholdings should be taken over by cooperative management for the benefit of both those who previously owned the land and agricultural labourers who work in the cooperative. In the second phase all landowners should be requested to join the cooperative system. In the third phase there should be rational distribution of land and redetermination of ownership. Finally, in the fourth phase there will be no conflict over the ownership of land.
items.statement: Agricultural land reorganization under PROUT proceeds through four developmental phases from cooperative management of uneconomic holdings to collective welfare consciousness.
items.title: Cooperatives

items.quote: During the last Gorakhpur dharmamahá cakra [spiritual congregation], ( 1 ) I said that three factors are indispensable for microcosmic progress: physical clash, psychic clash and the attraction of the Great.
items.statement: Microcosmic evolution and progress are driven by three indispensable forces: physical clash, psychic clash, and the attraction of the Great.
items.title: Cosmic Attraction and Spiritual Cult

items.quote: When this attraction is for finite objects, it is called káma [“physical longing”], and when it surges towards the Cosmic Entity, it is called prema [“divine love”]. Of course, káma is nothing but a limited form of prema .
items.statement: Attraction directed toward finite objects constitutes káma (physical longing), whereas attraction directed toward the Cosmic Entity constitutes prema (divine love).
items.title: Cosmic Attraction and Spiritual Cult

items.quote: Hence, after singing songs which are predominantly high-pitched, the singer should sip a mixture of powdered black pepper and warm ghee.
items.statement: Singers of predominantly high-pitched songs should consume powdered black pepper with warm ghee to counteract potential vocal disorders and constipation.
items.title: The Cosmic Ideation and Unit Ideation of Rágas and Rágińiis

items.qualifiers: Subtle microvita functioning within human minds and inferences
items.quote: These yakśas are one of the seven types of devayonis (the others are gandharva, kinnara, vidyádhara, videhaliina, prakrtiliina and siddha) which are the collective names of different categories of microvita.
items.statement: Devayonis are subtle microvita categorized into seven collective groups: yakśa, gandharva, kinnara, vidyádhara, prakrtiliina, videhaliina, and siddha.
items.title: Crude and Subtle Microvita

items.quote: In the final stage of sádhaná, the pure spiritual phase, none of these can help the spiritual aspirant; even positive and negative microvita cannot function above the psycho-spiritual level, beyond the pituitary gland. No vibration is of any help. In such circumstances, finally you will have to depend on the grace of the supreme and nothing else.
items.statement: Positive and negative microvita cannot function beyond the pituitary gland into the pure spiritual phase, where progress depends solely on divine grace.
items.title: Cult, Inference and Propensity

items.quote: Biija means “seed”. Wherever a seed is sown, it [sprouts into] a plant; but where the seed is burnt, a plant is not produced. A sádhaka becomes dagdhabiija when he or she has no more pain or pleasure of his or her own. One who has surrendered in toto and has not kept in hand even a single paisa of it, is alone dagdhabiija.
items.statement: A dagdhabiija is a spiritual practitioner whose mental reactive momenta have been completely burnt up through total surrender, leaving them free of personal pain and pleasure.
items.title: Dagdhabiija

items.qualifiers: Classical structural definition of táńd́ava postures
items.quote: The knees must cross the navel. When they cross the navel it is called Brahma táńd́ava . When they cross the anáhata [mid-point of the chest] it is called Viśńu táńd́ava . When they cross this portion [indicates the throat], it is called Rudra táńd́ava .
items.statement: Táńd́ava dance is classified into three levels based on knee elevation: Brahma táńd́ava (crossing the navel), Viśńu táńd́ava (crossing the mid-chest), and Rudra táńd́ava (crossing the throat).
items.title: Dance, Mudrá and Tantra

items.quote: A middle course was invented, and in Oriental music it is called tála . Oriental music is based on tála. Tála means – the first sound of táńd́ava is tá, and the first sound of lalita is la – tá plus la .
items.statement: The musical concept tála represents the middle course synthesized from the first syllables of táńd́ava ('tá') and lalita ('la').
items.title: Dance, Mudrá and Tantra

items.quote: Kaośikii : The two hands upraised and folded together represent, “Now I am trying to establish a link with Parama Puruśa .” Both hands bending to the right indicate, “I know the right way to request You.” The bending of the body should be at a 45-degree angular projection. The leftward movement represents, “I know how to fulfil Your demands.” The movement of bending in front suggests complete surrender. The backward bending represents, “I am ready to face all troubles that may come.” The last tá, tá represents, “O Lord, I repeat Your rhythm.”
items.statement: The Kaośikii dance embodies specific mudraic ideations across its movements, from linking with Parama Puruśa to total surrender and readiness to face obstacles.
items.title: Dances and the Path of Vidyá

items.quote: When the sádhaka clearly feels the thrill of divine existence around him at the time of sádhaná, the state of bliss as experienced by the sádhaka is described as dashá. When the sádhaka feels the existence of the divine world around him, as also the source from which the divine existence comes, the state of bliss the sádhaka experiences at the time of sádhaná is bháva. Again, when the sádhaka feels the closest proximity of Parama Puruśa, even within his embrace, that bháva is called mahábháva.
items.statement: In devotional ecstasy, dashá is the felt thrill of divine existence, bháva includes sensing the divine source, and mahábháva is the direct tactual experience of close divine proximity.
items.title: Dasha, Bháva and Mahábháva

items.quote: The first principle of decentralized economy is that all the resources in a socio-economic unit should be controlled by the local people.
items.statement: Decentralized economy operates on five core principles: local resource control, production for consumption, cooperative organization, local employment, and removal of non-local goods from local markets.
items.title: Decentralized Economy – 1

items.quote: Local people are those who have merged their individual socio-economic interests with the socio-economic interests of the socio-economic unit they live in. Clearly, this concept of local people has nothing to do with physical complexion, race, caste, creed, language or birth place.
items.statement: Local people in a socio-economic unit are defined strictly by whether their individual economic interests are merged with the collective interest of the unit, independent of birthplace or race.
items.title: Decentralized Economy – 1

items.qualifiers: Structural contrast between capitalism and PROUT
items.quote: Capitalism will never support decentralization, because capitalist production exists to maximize profits. Centralization means industry for profit, while decentralization means industry for consumption. PROUT’s approach, which will be supported by all rational people, is production for consumption.
items.statement: Capitalism inherently requires centralized production to maximize profit, whereas PROUT requires decentralization because production is organized for consumption.
items.title: Decentralized Economy – 2

items.qualifiers: Psychological law of ideation applied to political ideology
items.quote: If one meditates on materialistic ideas the mind will become crude and materialistic. If the mind always meditates on the commune system, will it become subtle or crude? It will surely become crude because in the communist system there is want of humanity and want of morality. The very theory of communism makes the mind crude.
items.statement: Materialistic philosophies like communism inevitably crudify the human mind because the mind assumes the characteristics of the crude objects it ideates upon.
items.title: Defects of Communism – Excerpt C

items.quote: The Licchaviis of Vaishali abolished the monarchy and established the first republic about 2500 years ago. The representatives of the people were known as Licchaviis, and they formed an executive body known as Mahalicchaviis through elections. The Mahalicchaviis controlled the power in Vaishali that was previously controlled by the monarchy.
items.statement: The Licchaviis of Vaishali established the world's first republic roughly 2,500 years ago by replacing the monarchy with an elected executive body called the Mahalicchaviis.
items.title: Democracy and Group-Governed States

items.qualifiers: Linguistic taxonomy based on acoustic derivation
items.quote: Among the established languages of the world, mainly four can be considered as the root languages. They are Vedic, Latin, Hebrew and old Chinese. If one examines the derivation of the vocabulary of these languages one will find that their method or process is identical.
items.statement: The four root languages that establish foundational vocabularies among world languages are Vedic, Latin, Hebrew, and old Chinese.
items.title: Derivation, Emanation and Distortion (Discourse 19)

items.quote: There are 49 propensitics. Collect them and awaken the 50th, the “Para” vrtti. When this will be awakened, you will enter the realm of pure cognition, which is called “Brahmadhámá” or the abode of the Supreme.
items.statement: Human propensities number 49 and must be channelized rather than suppressed to awaken the 50th propensity (Pará vrtti) leading to pure cognition.
items.title: Desideratum of Human Life

items.quote: That is why, in Ananda Marga Oṋḿkára is not a mantra (an incantation of invocation) for chanting but for hearing. Hearing or surrendering to this Oṋḿkára, which is the direct concomitant of the Brahmic nucleus, the Puruśottama, is to attain Him, and attaining Him means there is nothing else to be desired.
items.statement: In Ananda Marga practice, Oṋḿkára is not a mantra meant for vocal chanting, but an acoustic sound intended to be heard through inner listening.
items.title: Desire and Detachment

items.quote: Socio-economic units should be formed throughout the world on the basis of the same economic problems, uniform economic potentialities, ethnic similarities, common sentimental legacy and similar geographical features. The whole of India and the entire world can be reorganized into socio-economic units based on these factors. These units should not merely be geographical areas but self-sufficient socio-economic groupifications. The fundamental basis of these groupifications is social, cultural and economic, and not religious or linguistic.
items.statement: Socio-economic units should be demarcated on the basis of uniform economic potential, geographic features, and common sentimental legacy, rather than religion or language.
items.title: Developmental Planning

items.quote: In pure economic terms developmental programmes are those programmes which directly increase national wealth and indirectly support this increase. Programmes which only increase national wealth indirectly, not directly, cannot be regarded as developmental programmes until the minimum requirements of the people are guaranteed.
items.statement: Developmental programmes are strictly defined in pure economics as expenditures that directly increase national wealth or indirectly support that direct increase.
items.title: Developmental Programmes

items.qualifiers: Philosophical law of causation propounded originally by Maharshi Kanada
items.quote: At the same time you should remember that wherever there is effect, there must be the cause, but wherever there is cause there may or may not be an effect.
items.statement: While every effect must have a preceding cause, the presence of a cause does not guarantee the emergence of an effect.
items.title: Devotees Moving around the Cosmic Nucleus

items.quote: When joy surpasses the capacity of the mind it becomes immeasurable. If sorrow becomes too intense to bear, one loses one’s equipoise and may even become senseless. When sorrow becomes this acute, it, too, can no longer be measured. So, unbearable sorrow and overwhelming joy are both beyond the scope of measurement. A person overwhelmed with joy may become senseless or may dance joyfully. That intense, immeasurable joy which leads one to infinity, is called “ánanda”.
items.statement: Ánanda is defined philosophically as infinite happiness that surpasses the measuring capacity of the mind.
items.title: Devotion Is the Life-Force of a Devotee

items.qualifiers: Ethical and spiritual classification of sins
items.quote: So pátaka is atonable, but atipátaka is not atonable; and mahápátaka, you know, is the worst type of [ati]pátaka. If one wants to atone for mahápátaka, one will have to sacrifice one’s life for the cause of the entire universe.
items.statement: Moral violations (pápa) are classified into atonable pátaka, unatonable atipátaka, and recurring-harm mahápátaka.
items.title: Devotion: The Only Way to Salvation

items.quote: I have said earlier and repeat today that Parama Puruśa cannot do two things: first, He cannot hate anybody; and second, He cannot create someone like Himself. One who loves Him will merge in Him, will become one with Him. Parama Puruśa always remains a singular Entity –
items.statement: Parama Puruśa cannot perform two specific actions: hating anyone and creating another entity identical to Himself.
items.title: Devotion and the Realm of Intellectuality

items.quote: When this devotional cult ( 3 ) does not remain confined to a mere practice, but instead is elevated to a devotional sentiment, a devotional mission, to the realm of devotional ideation – when the underlying spirit of humanism is extended to everything, animate and inanimate, in this universe – I have designated this as “Neohumanism”. This Neohumanism will elevate humanism to universalism, the cult of love for all created beings of this universe.
items.statement: Neohumanism is the elevation of humanism to universalism through the extension of devotional sentiment to all animate and inanimate entities in the universe.
items.title: Devotional Sentiment and Neohumanism (Discourse 1)

items.qualifiers: Allegorical interpretation of the Mahabharata / Giitá
items.quote: Now, Páńd́upakśiiya means five phases of internal development, five phases of exaltation, starting from the supreme negativity, the kulakuńd́alinii, and proceeding towards the supreme positivity, the controlling point of the pineal gland.
items.statement: Allegorically in the Giitá, Dharmakśetra represents the human physical body, Kurukśetra represents the active world of work, the five Pandavas represent stages of internal psycho-spiritual elevation, and the one hundred Kauravas represent the blind mind's propensities moving through ten directions across ten organs.
items.title: Dharmakśetra and Kurukśetra

items.quote: The basic dharma of humans is Bhágavata dharma, which has four supporting legs – vistára [the principle of expansion], rasa [the principle of total surrender to Parama Puruśa], sevá [selfless service to Parama Puruśa and His creation], and tadsthiti [the final ensconcement in Parama Puruśa]. Bhágavata dharma stands on these four legs.
items.statement: Bhágavata dharma is the fundamental human dharma supported by four pillars: vistára (expansion), rasa (surrender), sevá (selfless service), and tadsthiti (final ensconcement in the Supreme).
items.title: Dharmakśetra – the Human Body

items.qualifiers: within the allegorical framework of the Giitá
items.quote: When the resultant force arising out of this war, this conflict between vice and virtue, is directed towards human well-being – this very resultant force is then called viveka (conscience, the power of discrimination). The power to discriminate, to judge, between good and bad is the conscience.
items.statement: In the allegorical interpretation of the Giitá, Dhritarastra represents the blind mind and Sanjaya represents conscience or the power of discrimination (viveka).
items.title: Dhritarastra and Sanjaya

items.qualifiers: conditional upon direction of energy utilization
items.quote: When this principle, this energy, this power – the dormant power hidden within – is properly utilized for a good purpose, a human being attains godhood. That is possible by arousing and pushing the latent power upwards. When, on the other hand, it is directed downwards, a human becomes a demon.
items.statement: When internal bodily energy (tejastattva) is guided upward towards higher cakras, it leads to godhood, whereas directing it downward makes a human demonic.
items.title: Dhritarastra and Sanjaya

items.quote: That which is mastered by continued arduous practice is called dhrupada . The Sanskrit language has been bound by the composition of grammar. For this reason, the Sanskrit language is called dhrupadii language.
items.statement: Dhrupada refers to that which is mastered through continuous arduous practice, applicable to rule-bound languages and fixed-scale musical styles.
items.title: Dhrupadii Style of Music

items.qualifiers: contrast between rule-bound prestige and flexible vitality
items.quote: When saḿgiita (the combined name for instrumental music, vocal music and dance) is not bound fast by the scale, that is, when the singer enjoys sufficient freedom in their vocals, when the dancers can direct their steps to some extent according to their own wishes, when the musicians enjoy a certain freedom with the metre while playing, then this kind of saḿgiita , that is, dance, vocal and instrumental music, can be called folk song, folk music and folk dance.
items.statement: Folk music is characterized by freedom from strict scales and metres, but when it becomes bound by rigid rules, it ascends to the level of dhrupadii.
items.title: Dhrupadii Style of Music

items.qualifiers: universal to physical and physiological movements
items.quote: All the movements taking place in us in life – movements in nerves, veins, arteries, the brain – are always systaltic. That is, speed is followed by pause, which again is followed by speed. The movement is not continuous.
items.statement: Human movement and bodily processes are inherently systaltic, composed of alternating speed and pause, making pause an intrinsic recurring micro-death.
items.title: Dhruva and Adhruva

items.quote: So we have the affliction of birth, the affliction of life, the affliction of death; when people recognize the affliction, yet are unwilling to part from it, that attachment is the last half coil. These three-and-a-half coils constitute the mrtyupásha. Pásha means “that which binds”.
items.statement: The mrtyupásha (death noose) consists of three-and-a-half coils: birth affliction, life suffering, death suffering, and the half-coil of lingering attachment.
items.title: Dhruva and Adhruva

items.quote: The debility of the mańipura cakra ( 1 ) is the main cause of diabetes. Amongst the pancreatic juices, one secretion helps in the digestion of food, and another separates the sugar content from non-vegetarian and starchy types of food.
items.statement: The fundamental cause of diabetes is debility of the mańipura cakra, impairing the pancreatic secretions and the liver's capacity to store sugar.
items.title: Diabetes

items.quote: Diabetes with sugar in the urine is called somaroga or madhumeha . Diabetes without sugar is called mútrátisára or udakameha .
items.statement: Diabetes with sugar present in the urine is termed somaroga or madhumeha, whereas diabetes without sugar in the urine is termed mútrátisára or udakameha.
items.title: Diabetes

items.quote: Democracy cannot succeed unless 51% of the population rigidly follow principles of morality. Where corrupt and immoral persons are in the majority, leaders will inevitably be elected among these immoral people.
items.statement: Democracy cannot function successfully unless at least 51 percent of the population strictly adheres to moral principles, mass education is established, and socio-economic consciousness exists.
items.title: Dialectical Materialism and Democracy

items.qualifiers: except heavy industries and essential government offices
items.quote: With the exception of heavy industries and essential government offices, all industry should be shifted to the vil lages. To stop overcrowding in the cities this is the only feasible approach.
items.statement: To prevent urban congestion and crime, industrial decentralization should be implemented by shifting all industries except heavy industry and essential government offices to mechanized cottage units in villages.
items.title: Dialectical Materialism and Democracy

items.qualifiers: general rule for body exposure to heat and sunlight
items.quote: One should always remember, “Expose the stomach to fire and the back to sun;” i.e., if you need to warm yourself at a fire, keep the stomach towards the fire, never the back.
items.statement: During sun-bathing (átapa snána), diseased body parts are exposed while healthy parts are shaded, following the principle of exposing the stomach to fire and the back to the sun.
items.title: Different Yoga Practices

items.qualifiers: in the mythological resolution between Shiva and Rama
items.quote: “We suggest you accept the following interpretation,” said the human beings, “Ramaeva iishvarah iti Rameshvarah; that is, Rama himself is a lord, so he’s Rameshvarah.”
items.statement: The compound 'Rámeshvarah' admits three distinct syntactic interpretations: Rama's lord, one whose lord is Rama, or Rama himself as lord.
items.title: Differing Interpretations

items.qualifiers: two distinct historical-spiritual phases of diikśá
items.quote: The first phase is known as Vaedikii diikśá, and the second phase is known as Tántrikii diikśá. In Vaedikii diikśá, the aspirant requests the Supreme Entity, Parama Puruśa, to show him or her the path. It is not a cult; it is just requesting the Supreme Father to let him or her know the secrets of success in the stratum of spirituality.
items.statement: Vaedikii diikśá consists of prayer requesting guidance onto the path of spirituality, whereas Tántrikii diikśá is a practical cult of psychic expansion involving diipanii, mantrágháta, and mantra caetanya.
items.title: Diikśá and Initiation

items.quote: Mantrágháta means, as I have already told you, that each and every mantra has the support of an acoustic root: and when that acoustic root strikes at the root of the coiled serpentine, it is aroused. This is called mantrágháta. After that this roused coiled serpentine moves with the force, or the stamina, it gets from the mantra. It moves towards the supreme positivity, and this movement is called mantra caetanya.
items.statement: Mantrágháta is the arousal of the coiled serpentine by striking its root with the acoustic root of a mantra, while mantra caetanya is its subsequent directed movement towards supreme positivity.
items.title: Diikśá and Initiation

items.quote: Rudimental factors cannot be created by human beings, hence ownership lies with the Cosmic Entity and not with individuals. We can only use these factors. We are like the members of a joint family under the Dáyabhága ( 1 ) system of law sermonized by Shrii Jiimutabahana Bhattacharya.
items.statement: Individual ownership of fundamental natural resources is invalid because humans cannot create rudimental factors; all mundane assets represent common cosmic patrimony.
items.title: Discourses on Prout

items.quote: Thus: (1) small businesses should be left to individuals; (2) big industries should be owned by the immediate government; and (3) the industries in between the big and small industries should be run on a cooperative basis. ( 11 )
items.statement: Industrial organization under PROUT requires key large-scale industries to be managed by the immediate government, middle industries by cooperatives, and small businesses by private enterprise.
items.title: Discourses on Prout

items.qualifiers: contingent upon a consumption-based economic system
items.quote: The question of unemployment arises only in the capitalistic framework where industry is for profit. In the collective economic structure, where industry stands for consumption and not for profit, the question of unemployment does not arise. Here the number of labourers will not be lessened; rather the working hours will be reduced and the remaining hours will be used in mental and spiritual pursuits.
items.statement: In a collective economic structure oriented towards consumption rather than capitalistic profit, rationalization and technological mechanization do not create unemployment.
items.title: Discourses on Prout

items.qualifiers: universal prerequisite is solely the human framework and practice
items.quote: When a unit being obtains a human body as a result of efforts from life to life, they become fit for attaining liberation with the help of this kind of self-knowledge. Hence herein lies the proof that one who has obtained a human body is suitable for attaining liberation or salvation. Here the question of discrimination of rights does not arise, nor does the question of caste.
items.statement: Every individual possessing a human structure possesses the complete right and capacity to attain liberation and salvation through self-knowledge, regardless of caste, gender, or academic scholarship.
items.title: Discrimination in Rights

items.qualifiers: classification of pretayonis as negative microvita
items.quote: These pretayonis are divided into several categories – durmukha, kabandha, madhyakapála, mahákapála, brahmadaetya or brahmapisháca, ákáshiipreta, and pisháca.
items.statement: Disembodied minds with defective mentalities become pretayonis of seven categories: durmukha, kabandha, madhyakapála, mahákapála, brahmadaetya/brahmapisháca, ákáshiipreta, and pisháca, which function as negative microvita.
items.title: Disembodied Souls and Microvita – Excerpt A

items.qualifiers: tanmátric preference based on subtlety and crudity
items.quote: Negative microvita prefer the smell tanmátrá more than the sound tanmátrá, and in the same way positive microvita prefer the sound tanmátrá more than the smell tanmátrá.
items.statement: Negative microvita prefer the cruder smell tanmátra over the sound tanmátra, whereas positive microvita prefer the subtler sound tanmátra over the smell tanmátra.
items.title: Disembodied Souls and Microvita – Excerpt A

items.quote: The seven varieties of devayoni are yakśa, kinnara, gandharva, vidyádhara, prakrtiliina, videhaliina and siddha.
items.statement: Devayonis (positive microvita) consist of three fundamental factors (ethereal, aerial, luminous) and comprise seven categories: yakśa, kinnara, gandharva, vidyádhara, prakrtiliina, videhaliina, and siddha.
items.title: Disembodied Souls and Microvita – Excerpt B

items.quote: The powers which are confined to Parama Puruśa alone are known as “vibhuti garimá”, not “garimá” alone. Garimá means “one of the occult powers of áśt́a aeshvarya”.
items.statement: Occult powers exclusive to Parama Puruśa alone are termed vibhuti garimá, distinct from individual occult powers acquired through penance or grace.
items.title: Disembodied Souls and Microvita – Excerpt B

items.quote: (5) The disposal of the dead body and its financial responsibility belong to the society. It is not proper to give any burden to the bereaved family.
items.statement: The financial responsibility and execution of dead body disposal belong entirely to the collective society, and should place no burden on the bereaved family.
items.title: Disposal of the Dead Body

items.quote: It is worth noticing that we call this natural change “emanation” instead of “distortion” because distortion refers to a special form of change or a corrupted form of change. In Sanskrit grammar it is called vivarttana.
items.statement: Natural language evolution through regular phonetic shifts is termed utsárańa (emanation), whereas irregular, corrupt, or truncated phonological alterations are classified as vivarttana (distortion).
items.title: Distortion (Discourse 21)

items.quote: If one constantly thinks, “I’m a sinner, I’m a sinner”, one loses one’s inherent mental strength. Such thoughts are to be avoided. What humans should think is, “Whatever I may be, good or bad, I belong to Paramátma, so why should my mind be weakened by hesitation, confusion or an inferiority complex?”
items.statement: An inferiority complex is a harmful expression of fear that destroys mental strength, and spiritual aspirants should replace it with the awareness that all beings belong to Parama Puruśa.
items.title: Do Not Entertain Any Inferiority Complex

items.qualifiers: Tantric definition of mudrańam and association
items.quote: The Tantrik practice of Mudrá Sadhana means to associate with good human beings in order to attain liberation.
items.statement: Mudrá Sadhana in Tantra signifies the deliberate renunciation and desertion of evil company (asatsauṋgamudrańam) to facilitate liberation.
items.title: Do Virtuous Deeds Day and Night

items.quote: The two types of pápa are pátaka and pratyaváya. If one does something which should not be done, such as stealing, telling lies, etc, it is called “pátaka”. It is an action which harms others. If one fails to do that which should be done, such as not feeding the poor or not serving the sick, it is called “pratyaváya”.
items.statement: Pápa (sin) is classified into pátaka (commission) and pratyaváya (omission), with pátaka further subdivided into compensable pátaka, uncompensable atipátaka, and recurring-harm mahapátaka.
items.title: Do Virtuous Deeds Day and Night – 1

items.quote: When the process of incantation is perfectly attuned to the respiration, it will continue effortlessly in a wakeful, dream or sleep stage. A person in that situation is said to have attained “ajapá siddhi”.
items.statement: Mastering the synchronisation of incantation with the respiratory cycle creates continuous, effortless 24-hour mantra repetition known as ajapá siddhi.
items.title: Do Virtuous Deeds Day and Night – 1

items.quote: “A” means “coming” and “gati” means “mobility”. When all mobility terminates in Parama Puruśa, it is called “sharańágati”. When sharańágati occurs, one is said to have accomplished the final attainment.
items.statement: Sharańágati is defined as complete, hundred-percent psychic dependence on Parama Puruśa where all individual movement and mobility terminates in Him.
items.title: Do Virtuous Deeds Day and Night – 2

items.qualifiers: definition in the psychic and intellectual realm
items.quote: Similarly, in the psychic realm, if there is an idea, that idea may be big, but if that idea is surrounded by boundary lines, and no microcosm is allowed to go beyond those boundary lines, that idea is called dogma. Dogma seals the future of the human intellect.
items.statement: A dogma is any idea that is enclosed by rigid boundary lines beyond which the microcosm is forbidden to venture, paralyzing the future of human intellect.
items.title: Dogma – No More

items.quote: Human thought-waves and human knowledge may be directed towards two objects. One is the objective psychic stance, and the other is the objecto-subjective spiritual stance.
items.statement: Human thought movement operates either as an objective psychic stance (enlarging ectoplasmic structure and brain cells) or an objecto-subjective spiritual stance (pinnacling mental propensities for supreme surrender).
items.title: Dogma and Human Intellect

items.quote: This personal relationship between human beings and their creator, Parama Puruśa, is called “ota yoga”. Through ota yoga, Parama Puruśa is individually associated with all unit human beings: no one is alone, no one is helpless.
items.statement: Ota yoga refers to Parama Puruśa's direct, individual relationship with every unit entity, while prota yoga represents His pervasive association with the entire cosmic collective.
items.title: Don't Be Afraid

items.quote: In the human mind there are one thousand propensities. The pineal gland is therefore called “sahasrára cakra” ( 1 ) , because it controls the movement of one thousand propensities. Actually there are fifty propensities in the human mind, an all fifty are working internally and externally. So, how many expressions are there? 50 x 2 = 100. And there are ten direction: púrva, peschima, uttar, dákśińa, úrdha, adhah – the six dik, or disha – and iishán, agni, naerta, vayu – the four corners, or anudisha – so six pradisha and four anudhisha equals ten directions. One hundred propensities working in ten directions becomes one thousand: that’s why it is called “sahasrára cakra”.
items.statement: The sahasrára cakra controls one thousand propensity manifestations, derived from 50 fundamental propensities expressed internally and externally across 10 directions.
items.title: Don't Be Misguided

items.qualifiers: classification of Ananda Marga marriage practice
items.quote: Now, the marriage system of Ananda Marga is a gandharva form of marriage as described by Manu, but it is solemnized publicly. That is to say, an Ananda Marga marriage is a socially-organized, socially-recognized marriage.
items.statement: The marriage system in Ananda Marga is a publicly solemnized gandharva marriage that is socially organized and legally recognized under Hindu marriage law.
items.title: Dowry and Marriage – Excerpt F

items.qualifiers: psychological distinction between ordinary and supramental dreams
items.quote: The surging vibrational flow which comes out of the fountain-head of the unconscious mind and vibrates the subconscious mind is also a sort of dream. Such dreams are not devoid of significance because their cause is the omniscient causal mind. This may be called “supramental vision”.
items.statement: Confused dreams result from restless nerve cells and physical disturbance, while supramental dreams originate from the omniscient causal (unconscious) mind transmitting premonitions to the subconscious.
items.title: Dream, Telepathic Vision and Clairvoyance

items.qualifiers: applies across individual and collective psychic processing
items.quote: When people listen to something, that idea is not assimilated immediately. It only gets assimilated when the mind is in a state of pause. The subsequent expression takes place in the state of speed.
items.statement: Sensory and psychic inputs cannot be assimilated during active movement; assimilation occurs strictly during states of pause, while subsequent expression occurs in states of speed.
items.title: Dynamicity and Staticity

items.qualifiers: etiological and biological explanation of dysentery symptoms
items.quote: Under those circumstances, the different fluid-secreting glands of the body engage in secreting more fluids in an effort to rectify the internal disorder. When these extra fluids come into contact with the undigested food and other contaminated matter, they turn into mucus. So in a case of dysentery the stool is full of mucus. The mucus is no disease by itself but is a natural system of healing the disease.
items.statement: The presence of mucus in dysenteric stool is not a disease in itself, but a physiological healing reaction produced by secreting glands to counteract decomposing matter.
items.title: Dysentery

items.quote: Chewing food brings an adequate quantity of saliva into the mouth. No sooner does the food mixed with saliva enter the stomach than the liver and the pancreas are enabled to start secreting their bile and digestive fluids. So unless food is chewed well, the liver can never function properly.
items.statement: Failure to thoroughly chew food deprives starchy nutrients of adequate salivary mixing, preventing the timely secretion of liver and pancreatic digestive juices.
items.title: Dyspepsia (Indigestion)

items.quote: It is desirable to take food or to defecate when the main flow of breath is through the right nostril. Even after food, it is desirable if the flow of breath mainly through the right nostril continues for some time. Because that is the time when the digestive glands start secreting a sufficient quantity of fluids to help digestion.
items.statement: To optimize digestive gland secretions, it is desirable to eat meals and defecate when the main respiratory breath flow is active through the right nostril.
items.title: Dyspepsia (Indigestion)

items.qualifiers: Use until the disease is completely cured
items.quote: Take a few mature, fresh leaves of white ákanda and slowly fry them in pure cow’s ghee as parat́há is fried. Then extract juice from these fried leaves, add warm ghee to it and pour three drops of that mixture into the affected ear three times daily – in the morning, evening and before bed. Continue using the medicine till the disease is completely cured. This remedy is very useful in diseases like mumps and pus-forming diseases of the ears.
items.statement: Juice extracted from mature, fresh white ákanda leaves fried in pure cow's ghee, combined with warm ghee and dropped into the ear three times daily, serves as a remedy for mumps and pus-forming ear diseases.
items.title: Ear-Aches, Mumps, Etc.

items.quote: The humidity and heat in the climate together bring down the level of activity of the local inhabitants, and make them somewhat averse to physical labour.
items.statement: A dry climate increases the working capacity and physical industriousness of inhabitants, whereas humidity and heat reduce activity levels and foster an aversion to physical labour.
items.title: East Wet Theory

items.qualifiers: Pertains specifically to floating populations unable to adapt
items.quote: The psychological defect of a floating population is this – the people fail to accept a new locality as their own home, so they cannot forget the land they left behind. This is the reason why the speed of their socio-economic integration and progress is slower than that of the local people.
items.statement: The psychological defect of a floating population is that failing to accept a new locality as home impairs and slows their socio-economic integration.
items.title: East Wet Theory

items.quote: Economic decentralization means production for consumption, not production for profit.
items.statement: Economic decentralization is defined as production carried out for consumption rather than for profit.
items.title: Economic Democracy

items.quote: The first requirement for economic democracy is that the minimum requirements of a particular age – including food, clothing, housing, education and medical treatment – must be guaranteed to all.
items.statement: Economic democracy rests on four core requirements: guaranteeing the minimum requirements of life, guaranteeing increasing purchasing capacity, placing all economic decision-making in the hands of local people, and strictly preventing outsiders from interfering in the local economy.
items.title: Economic Democracy

items.qualifiers: Subject only to slight, cyclical periodic adjustments
items.quote: However, if a country discontinues trade related to direct or indirect economic transactions and commences barter trade instead with other countries, it will not suffer much from such an economic depression.
items.statement: If a country conducts barter trade with other nations rather than direct or indirect monetary/bullion transactions, it will not suffer substantially from worldwide economic depressions.
items.title: Economic Depressions

items.qualifiers: Applies to both individual and state capitalism
items.quote: There are two main causes for economic depressions – first, the concentration of wealth, and secondly, blockages in the rolling of money.
items.statement: The fundamental causes of economic depressions are the concentration of the value of wealth and blockages in the rolling and circulation of money.
items.title: Economic Dynamics

items.qualifiers: Expands beyond traditional purely economic definitions to include psychic and spiritual exploitation
items.quote: According to PROUT, economic exploitation involves the unrestricted plunder of the physical and psychic labour of a particular community together with the natural resources in their local area.
items.statement: Under PROUT, economic exploitation is the unrestricted plunder of both physical and psychic labour alongside local natural resources.
items.title: Economic Exploitation of Bengal

items.qualifiers: Typically initiated by imperialist or fascist powers
items.quote: Where psychic exploitation is used to further economic exploitation, it is called “psycho-economic exploitation”.
items.statement: Psycho-economic exploitation occurs when psychic exploitation is deliberately used to facilitate and perpetuate economic exploitation.
items.title: Economic Exploitation of Bengal

items.qualifiers: True in individual spiritual life, impossible for the collective body
items.quote: When individual animation is suspended in Cosmic animation, or when individual aspiration is suspended in Cosmic aspiration, the result is absolute peace. Absolute peace in the collective body means the suspension of the universe, which is an impossibility.
items.statement: Absolute peace cannot exist in the collective body in the relative universe; absolute peace only occurs when individual animation and aspiration are suspended in Cosmic animation and aspiration.
items.title: Economic Self-Reliance – Excerpt A

items.quote: To counteract this threat, a powerful popular sentiment should be immediately generated for the liberation of intellect. For this, the first requisite factor is that the intellectuals in society must keep their intellects pure and unblemished. They will have to adjust to the level of the common people, casting aside their inertness and prejudicial notions. They should assist the masses in their development and extend their support to all anti-exploitation movements.
items.statement: To counter psycho-economic exploitation, intellectuals must maintain unblemished intellects, adjust to the level of the common people, discard prejudices, and actively support anti-exploitation movements.
items.title: Economic Self-Reliance – Excerpt F

items.qualifiers: Applied across social, economic, and political spheres
items.quote: To enjoy a right and to enjoy the right of management are not the same thing. Since human beings are mostly followers and not leaders, the right of management should be vested in a select few.
items.statement: Every individual possesses the inborn right to enjoy common universal patrimony, but the right of management must be vested exclusively in a select few intellectual-cum-intuitional workers.
items.title: Economic Self-Reliance – Excerpt G

items.qualifiers: Irrigation must preferably rely on surface water
items.quote: Nowadays boro is being cultivated with the help of deep tube wells, but this system of irrigation is not scientific. The same amount of water which is brought to the surface does not seep back down into the water-table because much of the water dries up due to the hot sunshine or is absorbed by the trees and plants. Hence, the water-table is rapidly declining.
items.statement: Continuous deep tube well irrigation leads to a severe lowering of the water table because extracted water evaporates or is absorbed rather than seeping back into the underground water table.
items.title: Economic Self-Sufficiency for Bengal

items.qualifiers: Often triggered by weakness resulting from suppressed dysentery
items.quote: When the chyle, blood, flesh and fat, these four elements, all become disturbed, eczema appears. That is why this disease is worse and more harmful than leucoderma, or white leprosy.
items.statement: Eczema is caused by a disturbance in four physical elements—chyle, blood, flesh, and fat—which weakens the body's immune defenses and enables eczema germs to colonize.
items.title: Eczema

items.quote: Whatever students learn from their parents and teachers out of fear fades into oblivion as soon as the agencies of fear disappear. The reason is that their learning and their fear were inseparably associated, so with the disappearance of fear, the knowledge that they had acquired in the course of their education also disappears from the more developed parts of their minds.
items.statement: Education imparted through fear and intimidation fails to produce lasting knowledge because learning associated with fear is forgotten as soon as the source of fear disappears.
items.title: Education

items.qualifiers: Necessary to ensure media serves social education instead of party propaganda or profit
items.quote: If we have even the slightest intention of using cinema for the benefit of society, it has to be placed in the hands of non-governmental cultural bodies and not in the hands of business persons or the government.
items.statement: To prevent political and commercial exploitation of mass media, radio broadcasting networks and cinema should be administered by independent boards of non-political, cultured educators.
items.title: Education

items.qualifiers: Distinguishes human capacity from animal instinct
items.quote: But human beings have another characteristic, another inborn instinct, and that is to expand their psychic arena also. So unlike other animals, human beings have the opportunity to divert their physical longings into spiritual longings, into spiritual aspirations. Other animals do not have this opportunity. But because of this psychic characteristic human beings exploit others on the psychic level as well as on the physical level, and this exploitation on the psychic level is even more dangerous than on the physical one.
items.statement: Unlike animals, humans possess an innate instinct to expand their psychic arena, which allows physical longings to be sublimated into spiritual aspirations but also makes psychic exploitation far more dangerous than physical subjugation.
items.title: Education and Neohumanism

items.quote: Prior to Lord Shiva, there was no institution of marriage in human society. As fathers and mothers were not bound by the ties of duty, the innocent children suffered tremendous hardship. The mothers had to bear a great burden as they had to shoulder the entire responsibility of rearing the children. The result was that the women’s progress in different spheres of life was thwarted. Shiva, through the application of logic and strength, forced husbands and wives into a social bond. That was the first time social marriage took place in this world.
items.statement: Prior to Lord Shiva, the social institution of marriage did not exist in human society, leaving mothers with the entire burden of child-rearing until Shiva established formal marital bonds.
items.title: Eka to Ekáuṋga (Discourse 12)

items.quote: Patnii : A patnii enjoyed equal religious and social rights as her husband. ( 5 ) Her children were entitled to all religious and social rights as their inheritance.
items.statement: In post-Shiva patriarchal society, the social status of wives was classified into four distinct levels: Patnii, Jáyá, Bháryá, and Kalatra, each conferring diminishing social and religious rights.
items.title: Eka to Ekáuṋga (Discourse 12)

items.qualifiers: Operates when the physical body dies while meditating on mundane or intellectual objects
items.quote: There are other categories like this such as yakśa, gandharvá, kinnara, vidyádhara, vidhehaliina and siddha which have been categorized according to the degree of ectoplasmic crudity or subtlety.
items.statement: Entities that ideate on crude or non-spiritual goals become disembodied minds operating through luminous, aerial, and ethereal factors after death, categorized into seven types of devayoni based on ectoplasmic crudity or subtlety.
items.title: Ekendriya – 1

items.qualifiers: Only the third stage yields permanent and absolute knowledge
items.quote: This is the process of acquiring knowledge, a process divided into three stages: ava-átmasthiiksárańa, upa-átmasthiikarańa, and samyak-átmasthiikárańa.
items.statement: The psychic assimilation of external projections (knowledge) progresses through three distinct stages: ava-átmasthiikarańa (superficial assimilation), upa-átmasthiikarańa (entering the psychic stratum), and samyak-átmasthiikarańa (complete spiritual ideation in Parama Puruśa).
items.title: Ekendriya – 2

items.qualifiers: The third stage in pratyáhára sádhaná
items.quote: The real spirit of ekendriya is this: the mind, having discarded all physical objects, ideas and dogmas, embraces the Supreme One as its supreme and only goal.
items.statement: Ekendriya is the stage where the mind discards all mundane objects, intellectual doctrines, and dogmas to direct its entire flow exclusively toward the Supreme Entity.
items.title: Ekendriya – 3

items.qualifiers: A relative factor that ceases when the rotating entity or mind ceases
items.quote: Time is a mental measurement of the motivity of action.
items.statement: Time is defined as the mental measurement of the motivity of action.
items.title: Ekendriya – 4

items.qualifiers: Mind acts as an indriya without physical apertures
items.quote: That which is directly related to the quinquelemental world and simultaneously related to the psychic world is called “indriya”.
items.statement: An indriya is that which is simultaneously related to the quinquelemental physical world and the psychic world, with the mind functioning as the eleventh, subtler indriya that operates without an external gateway.
items.title: Ekendriya – 5

items.qualifiers: Governed by the rhythm and pause of respiration in práńáyáma
items.quote: The indriyas are the controller of the body, the mind the controller of the indriyas, and the vital energy the controller of the mind. That’s why on the path of spiritual practice, and particularly in the practice of astáuṋga yoga (the eight fold path consisting of yama, niyama, ásana, práńáyáma, pratyáhára, dhárańá, dhyána, and samádhi) práńáyáma plays a very significant role.
items.statement: The indriyas control the body, the mind controls the indriyas, and the vital energy (práńa) controls the mind through the rhythm of the respiratory system.
items.title: Ekendriya – 6

items.qualifiers: Hierarchical progression from material/sensory absorption to supreme realization
items.quote: According to spiritual science the samádhi attained when the entire mind is pin-pointed on Parama Puruśa is called prajiṋá samádhi.
items.statement: Samádhi can occur on multiple levels: kśitibhaetik samádhi on fundamental physical factors, tanmátrik samádhi on inferences, samádhi on indriyas, and prajiṋá samádhi when the entire mind is pinpointed on Parama Puruśa.
items.title: Ekendriya – 7

items.qualifiers: Differentiates stages of spiritual realization below and at supreme attainment
items.quote: Iishvarakoti sádhakas, through special efforts, can master some negative and positive powers, and may apply them on certain human beings, places, or ideas. But a brahmakoti sádhaka can apply those powers on the entire universe at the same time, through his prota-yoga. Moreover, with the help of ota-yoga, he can also apply his power on an individual place or person if he so wishes.
items.statement: An Iishvarakoti sádhaka can apply occult powers to specific individuals, places, or ideas within space, whereas a Brahmakoti sádhaka applies powers to the entire universe simultaneously through prota-yoga and to specific entities through ota-yoga.
items.title: Ekendriya – 8

items.quote: The original stringed instrument is the ektárá . This ektárá [one stringed musical instrument] was invented during prehistoric times to bring resonance to the sound of the string. Shiva improved upon this ektárá and made the viiń or viińá . This viiń or viińá is the first musical instrument so devised as to maintain unison with surasaptaka or musical octave.
items.statement: The ektárá was the original prehistoric stringed instrument, which Lord Shiva refined into the viińá to achieve unison with the musical octave (surasaptaka).
items.title: Ektárá – One-Stringed Musical Instrument

items.qualifiers: Predisposed by constipation, excess pitta, over-acidity, malnutrition, or excessive seminal discharge
items.quote: When these microbes enter the shukrabahá náŕii and get a chance to settle there, they obstruct the flow of shukra and cause the vessels to swell. This swelling of the shukrabahá náŕii takes the form of elephantiasis.
items.statement: Elephantiasis occurs when microbes breed in contaminated or debilitated blood and lodge in the shukrabahá náŕii vessels, obstructing the flow of shukra and causing swelling.
items.title: Elephantiasis

items.qualifiers: Temporary preferential system until minimum requirements are guaranteed
items.quote: Thus, the criteria for receiving preferential services and education should not be birth affiliation but a person’s economic condition.
items.statement: As a temporary measure before PROUT is established, job and education reservations should be granted based strictly on economic backwardness rather than caste or birth affiliation.
items.title: Elevating Backward Classes

items.qualifiers: Moves in crests and troughs across physical, linguistic, and biological domains
items.quote: If something is produced from something and gradually moves forward towards greater manifestation it is called utsárańa. At the root of emanation is cause or causal factor, which is in a dormant condition at the outset.
items.statement: Emanation (utsárańa) is defined as the process wherein something is produced from a dormant causal seed and moves forward in a contractive-expansive systaltic flow toward greater manifestation.
items.title: Emanation (Discourse 20)

items.quote: The Operative Principle is a binding faculty only and the style of functioning of the binding faculty is called “svabháva” – “nature” in English. Some people who do not have sufficient knowledge – deep knowledge of science – may say that it is all natural. But the fact is that nature is simply the style of the Operative Principle, not an independent entity.
items.statement: Nature (svabháva) is not an independent entity, but is merely the functional style of the Operative Principle, which draws its functional stamina from energy created by the Cognitive Faculty.
items.title: Energy and Cognition

items.qualifiers: Driven by the evolution of collective psychology and technology
items.quote: That is, the importance of physical strength has dwindled, and the importance of intellectual strength has increased. So the physical advantages that were used by the male-dominated society to drive the steamroller of oppression over women, today just will not do.
items.statement: The historical oppression of women rooted in male physical superiority is becoming obsolete because modern society increasingly prioritizes intellectual power over physical strength.
items.title: Equal Rights for Men and Women

items.qualifiers: Glandular differences are limited strictly to lower crude vrttis
items.quote: But in the spiritual, supra-mental and psycho-spiritual spheres, there are no differences between men and women. Rather, women can attain the highest spiritual experiences that men can attain. There is no logic whatsoever to justify depriving women unnecessarily or making their path of progress thorny.
items.statement: While physical and glandular differences between men and women affect certain crude propensities, there is zero distinction in the supra-mental and psycho-spiritual spheres, where both are equally entitled to highest spiritual realization.
items.title: Equality in the Psycho-Spiritual Sphere

items.qualifiers: Physical spatial separation remains, but internal psychic separation dissolves
items.quote: The same saḿskáras cannot live in two separate entities – they want to be fused in one. So if one’s individual saḿskáras could be withdrawn and then infused into two separate structures, they will certainly become one.
items.statement: Identical saḿskáras cannot exist in two separate entities; if identical saḿskáras are infused into two individuals, their separate psychic identities fuse into one single soul and mind.
items.title: Equalization of Saḿskáras

items.qualifiers: Distinguished via the narrative of Shiva explaining Ravana's crime
items.quote: Ravana disguised himself as a saint to carry off a housewife. As a result no housewife will henceforth believe a saint. Suppose a genuine saint comes to a family house and begs for alms. The housewife may well fear that he is a thief in the guise of a saint, like Ravana. Ravana has committed a crime which will have its effect on society in future. Moreover, the effect of Ravana’s evil deed will be a recurrent one. For this reason Ravana is not an atipátakii but a mahápátakii.
items.statement: An atipátaka is an offence causing individual harm for which there is no social atonement, whereas a mahápátaka is a crime whose evil deceitful impact causes recurrent, long-term damage across society.
items.title: Even the Greatest Sinners

items.qualifiers: Derived from root verbs bhar (to feed) and tan (to expand)
items.quote: So bhárata means “he who feeds you and helps you in your all-round expansion, all-round development”.
items.statement: Bháratavarśa etymologically denotes the land that feeds its inhabitants and supports their all-round physical, mental, and spiritual expansion.
items.title: Every Word Is Meaningful

items.qualifiers: Apparent philosophical paradox resolved by relative versus absolute stance
items.quote: Anejat, not ejat – not moving, that is, fixed. Why is He fixed, why is He stationary? Because He is above the periphery of time, space and person. There is neither any time, nor any space, nor any person. So can there be any movement, can there be any speed, not to speak of velocity? There cannot be.
items.statement: Parama Puruśa is described as anejat (non-moving) because He is beyond time, space, and person, yet simultaneously faster than the mind because the Macrocosm inherently surpasses all microcosmic movement.
items.title: Everybody Obeys Him

items.qualifiers: Core law of psychic ideation and projection
items.quote: So the mind has this potentiality – it takes the form of its object. If you say, “I am a sinner, I am a sinner,” you will be a sinner. Even if you are not a sinner but you always think, “I am a sinner, I am a sinner, I am a sinner,” you will be a sinner because that sinning becomes your mental object.
items.statement: The mind inherently assumes the form of its ideational object, meaning that dwelling on a sin complex makes one a sinner, whereas ideating on being a child of Parama Puruśa purifies and elevates the individual.
items.title: Everything Comes from Something

items.qualifiers: Inherent to Supreme Consciousness, attainable through realization
items.quote: This power of entering inside objects is known as antaryámitva. There are no secrets before the Supreme Consciousness – He can enter everywhere, inside every object, inside every mind.
items.statement: Antaryámitva is the subtle yogic power to enter inside physical or mental objects to know everything about them and exercise control over them.
items.title: Everything Is Vibrational

items.quote: And when this vrtti, this psychic urge, or this psychic mobility, is towards the crude, it is called pravrtti; and when it is towards the subtle it is called nivrtti.
items.statement: Psychic urge or mobility directed towards the crude is termed pravrtti, whereas when directed towards the subtle it is called nivrtti.
items.title: Existential Flow and Its Culminating Point

items.quote: These are the eight external bondages, or imposed bondages. One must fight against these imposed bondages, one must wage war against these bondages. And then there are the six ripu. Ripu means “internal enemies” – not imposed saḿskáras, imposed bondage, but inborn bondage.
items.statement: Bondages are classified into eight external, imposed bondages called pasha and six inborn internal bondages called ripu.
items.title: Existential Flow and Its Culminating Point

items.quote: Ayurveda considers the body to be composed of seven elements, or materials, derived one from the other in the following order: rasa, or chyle (the fluid essence of digested food), blood, flesh, fat, bone marrow, and shukra (for a definition of shukra, please see the Bengali Glossary). The body functions on the basis of three factors, or principles: váyu, pitta and kapha (please see the Bengali Glossary).
items.statement: Ayurveda considers the human body to be composed of seven successive elements and governed by three functional principles: vayu, pitta, and kapha.
items.title: Explanatory Notes

items.quote: As I mentioned earlier, the first reason for this waste of human potentiality is ignorance about the right path, and the second reason is lethargy. There is a third reason. Sometimes, even if people are aware of the right path and are not at all lethargic – even if one is a genius – they cannot express their full potentialities as they are subjected to unusual intellectual or social pressure.
items.statement: Waste of human potentiality occurs due to ignorance of the right path, lethargy, and external socio-intellectual pressure checking natural expression.
items.title: Exploitation – No More

items.quote: When this exploitation is perpetrated by the application of brute force, it is politico-economic exploitation; but when it is done not through brute force but through the application of cunning intellectual strategy, it is primarily psycho-economic exploitation.
items.statement: Politico-economic exploitation is executed through brute physical force, whereas psycho-economic exploitation operates through cunning intellectual strategy.
items.title: Exploitation and Pseudo-Culture (Discourse 7)

items.quote: As you know, the mind has a natural tendency to degrade itself; it flows more easily downwards than upwards. So if some people, by virtue of their wealth, impose vulgar cinemas and dramas on others, this will break the latters’ spines and they will become paralysed. And those paralysed, spineless people will thenceforth never be able to stand unitedly against cultural or any other kind of exploitation.
items.statement: Cultural exploitation works by imposing vulgar art and pseudo-culture onto populations to paralyze their psychic capacity and destroy their ability to resist.
items.title: Exploitation and Pseudo-Culture (Discourse 7)

items.quote: Remember that a genius has inborn talents, but who is a technician? Technicians are those who have ordinary qualities, but by dint of application (Sádhaná) and effort they have converted these into outstanding skills. This is the basic difference between a genius and a technician.
items.statement: A genius possesses inborn talent, whereas a technician begins with ordinary qualities and refines them into outstanding skills through sustained effort and practice.
items.title: Expression and Symbolization

items.quote: These mental symbols will one day have to be given expression as physical symbols. As long as these physical symbols do not get expressed, you will be carrying the load of those mental symbols from one life to another. This is the reason why people take rebirths until such time when all their mental symbols get converted into physical expressions.
items.statement: Rebirth occurs because unexpressed latent mental symbols must eventually find physical expression unless converted into psycho-spiritual waves.
items.title: Expression and Symbolization

items.quote: What you store in your brain through the medium of the nerve cells is your cerebral memory. But in the case of non-cerebral memory your nerve cells will not come forward to assist you. They cannot help you because no memory of your past episodes remains stored in your present nerve cells to enable you to remember them.
items.statement: Cerebral memory relies on physical nerve cells in the brain, whereas non-cerebral memory pertains to past-life episodes whose impressions travel with the mind and unrequited samskaras.
items.title: Extra-Cerebral Memory

items.qualifiers: only in three types of cases
items.quote: Such things only happen in three types of cases: first, in those who have a very well-developed personality; secondly, in those who have commanded their own death or who have died with full consciousness; and thirdly, in those who died through accidents. In these three cases, the episodes of the previous life remain visible and clear in the mind.
items.statement: Clear, vivid non-cerebral memories of a past life occur exclusively in three cases: developed personalities, those who commanded their own death, and those who died by accident.
items.title: Extra-Cerebral Memory

items.quote: Economic holdings are those where the market price of the produce will exceed the cost of production including capital, labour and machinery. Lands which produce economically viable agricultural wealth – that is, where output exceeds input – are called “economic holdings”.
items.statement: Economic holdings are lands where output value exceeds production costs, whereas uneconomic holdings produce less market value than input costs.
items.title: Farmers Cooperatives

items.quote: As I have already said, agricultural land should be brought under cooperative management, but the cooperative system should be introduced in two stages. In the first phase of the socialization of land, PROUT will not raise the demand for land ceilings, but the sale of agricultural land will be prohibited and uneconomic landholdings will be brought under cooperative management.
items.statement: According to PROUT, the cooperative system must be introduced in stages, starting with uneconomic holdings and later expanding to economic holdings and full net profit distribution to laborers.
items.title: Farmers Cooperatives

items.quote: In all types of menstrual trouble – dysmenorrhoea, leucorrhoea or any other female disease – a woman should not practise ásanas or mudrás during her menstrual period. Instead, she should perform práńáyáma only.
items.statement: During the menstrual period, women suffering from female diseases should suspend asana and mudra practices, performing pranayama only.
items.title: Female Diseases

items.quote: However, there is a difference between the terms “suzerainty” and “supremacy”. “Suzerainty” applies when the smaller kings accepted the authority of the powerful kings but did not pay them taxes. Today Australia accepts the suzerainty of the English monarchy, but it does not accept English supremacy because it does not pay taxes to the British government.
items.statement: Suzerainty involves accepting the authority of a dominant monarch without paying taxes, whereas supremacy entails full subordination including tax payments.
items.title: Feudalism and the Zamindary System

items.quote: The difference between these systems was that in the zamindary system if the zamindar failed to pay the required tax he was sent to jail, and he was only released when the tax was paid. In the jágirdari system, if the tax collector failed to pay the required tax his land was confiscated.
items.statement: In the zamindary system, non-payment of tax resulted in imprisonment until paid, whereas in the jagirdari system, default resulted in confiscation of land.
items.title: Feudalism and the Zamindary System

items.quote: Dogma is a psychic structure – all ideas are psychic structures – but there must be some flexibility regarding its boundary line.
items.statement: Dogma is defined as a psychic structure or idea characterized by rigidity and an inflexible boundary line that limits thought.
items.title: Fight Against All Dogmas – Excerpt B

items.quote: The cult that liberates the spiritual aspirant by helping him in expanding his mind and spirit is Tantra, “liberation through expansion”. Unless and until the mind becomes great, one cannot get liberation, one cannot attain spiritual salvation. That’s why the spiritual cult is called Tantra.
items.statement: Tantra is defined by the root 'tan' (to expand) and 'tra' (liberator), meaning spiritual liberation attained through mental and spiritual expansion.
items.title: Fighting at Each and Every Step

items.quote: The characteristic of the static principle is to bind whatever is subtle within the limitations of forms and lines, thus bringing it within the periphery of sense perception, and within the scope of human conception. Thus, due to the static influence of Prakrti, the abstract is brought into the initial stage of matter (ether).
items.statement: Static Prakrti functions to bind abstract and subtle consciousness into finite forms, names, and sensory-perceptible material objects.
items.title: Form and Formless

items.quote: When there is dominance of saḿyojanii shakti in one’s latent saḿskáras, the disembodied soul attains a female body for its outward expression, and conversely where there is a dominance of vibhájanii shakti, it attains a male body. Where there is an approximate balance between the two the disembodied soul attains the body of a hermaphrodite.
items.statement: The balance between the psychic forces of attraction (samyojanii) and being attracted (vibhajanii) determines whether a disembodied soul takes a female, male, or hermaphroditic body.
items.title: Form and Formless

items.quote: The minimum number of members on a board will be three, and the maximum, seven. The members may or may not be highly educated, but must have a developed sense of responsibility. A person cannot be a member of more than one board.
items.statement: Every board within AMPS from central to village level must comprise a minimum of three and a maximum of seven members, and no person may sit on multiple boards.
items.title: Formation of Boards

items.quote: And in the final stage, that is, when one attains the stage of devatá, then what one thinks, one says; and what one says, one does. There is no difference amongst thinking, saying, and doing. And that is the best stage of human structure or human existence.
items.statement: Human evolution progresses across three spiritual stages—pashu, viira, and devata—distinguished by the degree of harmony among thought, speech, and action.
items.title: From Animality to Divinity

items.quote: So the conception of God and Satan is defective. If we accept the existence of Satan, it means there are two Gods, one God positive and the other God negative – that is, Satan – and that Satan challenges the authority of Parama Puruśa . That cannot be. So there is no Satan. Everywhere is the rule of Parama Puruśa . Nowhere is the rule of Satan.
items.statement: A dualistic concept of God and Satan is fundamentally invalid because Parama Purusa is singular and omnipresent, with no separate opposing force.
items.title: From the Physical Stratum to the Apex

items.quote: And the spokes – there are innumerable spokes – what are these spokes? The spokes are various vibrations, various vibrational sounds, various vibrational lights. So these spokes, these vibrations, these innumerable vibrations, are called deva. Deva means “divine vibration”; deva means “divine effulgence”. And “Mahádeva” means “Supreme Deva”; that is, this hub, this hub of the wheel, this nave of the wheel, this nucleus of this Cosmological order, is Mahádeva.
items.statement: The Cosmological wheel's vibrations and light emissions are called deva, while its central hub or supreme causal factor is Mahadeva.
items.title: Further Names of the Supreme

items.quote: It is a common error to say that that mantra is the “Gáyattrii Mantra”; because gáyattrii is not the name of a mantra, it is the name of a chanda. In the Vedas, there are seven recognized chandas, that is, seven recognized rhythms. Those rhythms are gáyattrii, uśńiik, triśt́up, anuśt́up, jagati, brhatii and paunkti.
items.statement: Gayattrii is properly the name of a Vedic poetic meter composed of three lines of eight syllables each, rather than the name of the mantra itself, which is the Savitr Rk.
items.title: Gáyattrii Rhythm and the “Gáyattrii Mantra”

items.quote: So the entire functional business of the Supreme Self is represented by three sounds, a, u and ma – a-u-mmm. Hence the activated Consciousness is represented by the sound oooṋm. ( 24 ) And this oṋm now is called prańava.
items.statement: The cosmic sound Pranava (Onm) represents creation, preservation, and dissolution through the acoustic roots 'a', 'u', and 'ma'.
items.title: Gáyattrii Rhythm and the “Gáyattrii Mantra”

items.quote: The other day I said that in practical life, fascism is born from such a mentality – and also imperialism, capitalism, oligarchy and bureaucracy. Thus you can easily understand how dangerous this mentality is, and how detrimental to the progress of humanity.
items.statement: When economic and social ideologies are founded on geo-sentiment, they abandon rationality and foster imperialism, fascism, and group conflict.
items.title: Geo-Sentiment (Discourse 3)

items.quote: The four major races are the Austrics, Aryans, Mongolians and Negroids. The differences among these races and sub-races can be easily discerned by two factors: the skull index and the nose index.
items.statement: The four primary human races (Austrics, Aryans, Mongolians, Negroids) are physically distinguished based on the skull index and the nose index.
items.title: Geology and Human Civilization

items.quote: A Tantric, certainly not a Vidyá Tantric, but an Avidyá Tantric, with the help of a certain portion of their own ectoplasmic stuff, sits tight in an ásana [meditation posture], and, with the help of their ectoplasmic stuff, creates an ectoplasmic body for a detached mind (known as preta in Sanskrit).
items.statement: Apparent hauntings or visible disembodied spirits are caused when an avidya tantric or a fearful person transfers ectoplasmic stuff to a detached mind, producing a temporary solid form or positive hallucination.
items.title: Ghosts and Evil Spirits

items.quote: These beings are called devayonis. They are of seven types – yakśa, rakśa, kinnara, gandharva, vidyádhara, siddha and Prakrtiliina.
items.statement: Devayonis are seven non-quinquelemental post-physical entities (yaksa, raksa, kinnara, vidyadhara, gandharva, siddha, and Prakrtiliina) formed when spiritual aspirants retain subtle desires at death.
items.title: Ghosts and Evil Spirits

items.quote: By performing ásanas [postures for physico-psychic well-being] regularly, human beings can control the propensities attached to each cakra, and hence the thoughts which arise in their minds and their behaviour. This is because ásanas have a profound effect on the glands and sub-glands. How? All ásanas have either a pressurizing or depressurizing effect on the glands and sub-glands.
items.statement: Asanas regulate human thoughts and propensities by exerting pressurizing or depressurizing effects upon the glands and sub-glands associated with the cakras.
items.title: Glands and Sub-Glands

items.quote: If this hair is removed, then the lymphatic glands tend to overheat, causing over-secretion, and this in turn decreases the function of the thyroid and parathyroid glands. There is an inverse relation between the lymphatic glands and the thyroid and parathyroid glands: if one is more active then the other is less developed and it becomes weak.
items.statement: There is an inverse relationship between the lymphatic glands and the thyroid and parathyroid glands; removing joint hair overheats lymphatic glands and weakens thyroid function.
items.title: Glands and Sub-Glands

items.quote: Therefore gonorrhoea patients should observe naeśt́hika Brahmacarya [strict abstinence from sexual intercourse] for a long period of time, to avoid having blind or deformed offspring. Even after achieving a complete cure from the disease, strict continence must be maintained for at least three years.
items.statement: Patients cured of gonorrhoea must maintain strict abstinence from sexual intercourse for at least three years to prevent relapse and deformed offspring.
items.title: Gonorrhoea

items.quote: “Isms” that separate man from man are all encouraged and patronized by the vaeshyas. Casteism, provincialism, nationalism, racism, are nurtured chiefly with the money of the vaeshyas, who finance the disintegration and division of the human race, so that the people may not in any way raise their voice against the rapacious vaeshyas.
items.statement: Divisive 'isms' such as casteism, racism, and nationalism are actively funded and preserved by vaeshyas to divide humanity and subjugate ksatriyan brawn and vipran intellect.
items.title: Great Universe Fillers – Excerpt A

items.quote: The scientists who only worship the creation, and the hermits who ever remain in constant consternation of destruction – both tread the wrong path, which is not the path of salvation. One who moves judiciously, accommodating both of them, alone attains salvation.
items.statement: Both those who solely pursue the glamour of creation and those obsessed with the fear of its destruction are on the wrong path, whereas true salvation requires looking upon both with equanimity.
items.title: Great Universe Fillers – Excerpt C

items.qualifiers: Prescriptive definition of true society and social dharma
items.quote: The marching together of all in unison is termed society. Instead of despising those who have lagged behind, help them to advance. This alone will be your social dharma.
items.statement: Society (samája) is defined by its innate spirit of moving and marching together in unison, helping those who have lagged behind rather than despising them.
