items.title: Great Universe Fillers – Excerpt C

items.qualifiers: Distinguishing internal and external spiritual association
items.quote: So satsauṋga means “the company of Parama Puruśa”. But a second meaning is also there. This term is also used to describe the company of good people. The first is internal, the second external.
items.statement: The term satsauṋga has two meanings: internal satsauṋga, which is company with Parama Puruśa attained via love and faithful sadhana, and external satsauṋga, which is seeking out the company of good spiritual seekers.
items.title: Guhá and Satsaunga

items.quote: This bursting out of the forces through one of the vertical points signifies the state of disequilibrium in the triangle of forces, and the point through which the unbalanced forces burst out is called kámabiija. This imbalance or lack of balance is [called] guńakśobha in Tantra. From this point of bursting out, the creation starts, and Prakrti starts exerting influence on Puruśa.
items.statement: Creational evolution begins when the triangle of forces (Guńayantraka) loses equipoise due to homomorphic evolution (svarúpa parińáma) and bursts out through a vertex called kámabiija.
items.title: Guńayantraka and Svarúpa Parińáma

items.quote: “Kr” means to help one in one’s progress even when one does not deserve it. So if one deserves it, that is, if one has the qualification to get oneself fully developed and fully exalted, then in that case there is no necessity of krpá, there is no necessity of help from Táraka Brahma. But when one does not deserve it, when one has not got the qualification for development, and still one is helped, that sort of help is called “krpa”.
items.statement: Krpá (grace) is defined as offering assistance towards one's progress specifically when the person does not possess the requisite merit or qualification.
items.title: Guru Krpáhi Kevalam

items.qualifiers: Philosophical qualification of the Guru concept
items.quote: His secret is known to Him only, and He expresses Himself through a framework, a form. Now generally people say that the form is Guru, but the form is not Guru, Guru is expressing Himself through that form.
items.statement: The physical form itself is not the Guru; rather, Brahma expresses Himself through that specific physical framework.
items.title: Guru Pújá

items.quote: In olden times, an educational institution enrolling about a hundred students was called a “Pathshála”, that with 100-1000 students was called a “Catuspáthii”, and an institution of 1000-5000 students was called a “Mahá-catuspáthii”, Vidyapeetha or “Seat of learning”. Pupils of ancient Semitic and Middle Asia whose branches are the Ottoman Turks, Arabs and Jews used to call it “Academy”. Institutions with 5000-500,000 students were called Gurukul.
items.statement: Ancient Indian educational institutions were classified by enrollment capacity: Pathshála (around 100), Catuspáthii (100–1,000), Mahá-catuspáthii/Vidyapeetha (1,000–5,000), and Gurukul (5,000–500,000).
items.title: Gurukul: History and Planning

items.quote: Their advanced students, lecturers, teachers and students of higher classes who could sit under that huge umbrella were known as chatras. Hence it is clear that those who would sit under the chatra or umbrella of the kulapati were specially known as chatra+an=chatra chat +rak=chatra.
items.statement: The word chatra historically designated advanced students and teachers permitted to sit under the large umbrella (chatra) of the kulapati, whereas primary students who did not sit under it were termed vidyarthi.
items.title: Gurukul in a Historical Perspective

items.quote: It is not possible to achieve a permanent cure by removing the developed piles through surgery or through stopping the bleeding by any method, because if the root causes are not eliminated, the disease may attack again at any moment, or the contaminated gas and blood in the body may cause some other disease. Therefore, though it may not be improper to employ some temporary expedient to stop severe bleeding at the critical stage, the liver has to be restored in order to obtain a permanent cure.
items.statement: Surgery or stopping bleeding alone cannot permanently cure piles because the condition is fundamentally rooted in liver dysfunction and constipation affecting the entire system.
items.title: Haemorrhoids (Piles)

items.quote: [There are seven requirements for success in any mission. The first is firm determination: “I must succeed.” The second is reverence. The third is guru pújá, or constant remembrance of one’s spiritual master. The fourth is equanimity of mind. The fifth is control of the senses. The sixth is a balanced diet. The seventh There is no seventh requirement.]
items.statement: Shiva outlines six requisite factors for success in any mission: firm determination, reverence (shraddhá), guru pújá, equanimity of mind, control of the senses, and a balanced diet (with no seventh factor).
items.title: Hara's Seven Secrets

items.qualifiers: Scriptural concept of collective devotional environment
items.quote: The sweet spiritual environment created by the kiirtana is called Hariparimańd́ala in the scriptures. Hari resides at its nucleus.
items.statement: Hariparimańd́ala is the blissful spiritual environment generated by collective kiirtana where Hari shifts His nucleus to become the focal point of ideation.
items.title: Hari Pari Mańd́ala

items.qualifiers: Contrasting unit psychology with Supreme Consciousness
items.quote: Elevated beings – uttama puruśa – on the other hand, do not accept anything from anyone. But Parama Puruśa is entirely different from these two groups. He makes no discrimination whatever and accepts all that is offered to Him by any of His children.
items.statement: Unlike ordinary people who select what to accept or elevated beings who accept nothing, Parama Puruśa makes no discrimination and accepts everything offered by His children.
items.title: He Is Everywhere

items.qualifiers: Practical philosophical guideline for action in the world
items.quote: In my opinion, the best way is objective adjustment through subjective approach. If you do not feel that all objects and entities are a part of you, you cannot develop any love and affection for His creation. The balance between your unit being and the external world will be impaired and your movement towards Parama Puruśa will be hindered. Remember that the love you develop for this worldly creation must always be channelized towards Parama Puruśa.
items.statement: Spiritual seekers should practice objective adjustment through a subjective approach, channelizing worldly affection towards the Supreme Owner rather than developing attachment to mundane objects.
items.title: He Makes the Dumb Speak

items.qualifiers: Philosophical distinction between human and animal psychology
items.quote: Each and every living being is guided by certain instincts. Plants have instincts, animals also have instincts, but human instincts are fewer in number than human psychic propensities. That is, in the case of humans, propensities are stronger than instincts; and here lies the fundamental difference between an animal and a man.
items.statement: Human beings are distinguished from animals by having psychic propensities that outnumber and dominate over raw instincts, leading to a natural desire for subtler expressions.
items.title: He Thinks and We Perceive

items.quote: According to the scriptural meaning, diikśá is derived from “dii” and “kśa”. Dii is the first letter of the word “diipajiṋána” (light of knowledge) and kśa is the first letter of “kśayam” (exhaustion of saḿskaras).
items.statement: Diikśá is defined etymologically from dii (diipajiṋána, the light of knowledge) and kśa (pápakśayam, the exhaustion of accumulated saḿskáras).
items.title: He Who Steals Others' Sins Is Called Hari

items.qualifiers: Law of karmic reaction across spacetime
items.quote: If an action’s reaction is immediate, it will be equal and opposite. But if the reaction occurs after a change in time, place or person, its magnitude will increase. Some people suffer the reaction immediately, some after two years, some after one hundred years, and some after twenty lifetimes. The more the delay, the greater the reaction. That is, some “interest” will have to be added to the reaction of the original action. This is the natural law.
items.statement: Reactions to actions are equal and opposite only if time, place, and person remain unchanged; any delay adds an increasing magnitude of reaction analogous to interest on a loan.
items.title: He Who Steals Others' Sins Is Called Hari

items.qualifiers: Dietary and physiological cause of cardiovascular weakness
items.quote: Persons above thirty-five or forty years of age who consume an excessive quantity of non-vegetarian food out of greed may also suffer from heart disease; because non-vegetarian food increases the acidity of the blood, and this compels the heart to overwork in order to purify the blood; and the heart becomes weak.
items.statement: Excessive intake of non-vegetarian food or intoxicants increases blood acidity, which places severe strain on the heart and glandular system to purify the blood.
items.title: Heart Disease

items.quote: Too much non-vegetarian and fatty food aggravates the acidity of the blood. As a result, different hormone-secreting glands become weak, and the partially-digested food starts decaying inside the body, creating a foul and poisonous gas which, in turn, puts pressure and strain on the stool-filled intestine and forces its dislodgement. Therefore failure of the liver to digest all the food properly is the main cause of hernia.
items.statement: The primary cause of hernia is failure of the liver to digest food properly, which creates toxic gas and pressure from undigested food and stool that forces the intestine through the abdominal wall.
items.title: Hernia

items.quote: Wherever there is aesthetics, there is bound to be heterogeneity, and the ultimate goal of this clash is to be established in the realm of the Supreme Homogeneity, the state of Absolute Bliss – in the midst of heterogeneity. But that state of Supreme Bliss does not come within the scope of aesthetics; it comes within the scope of supra-aesthetics, that is, in the world of the absolute above the domain of relativity.
items.statement: Aesthetics operates within the realm of heterogeneity and the clash of the three binding principles, whereas Absolute Bliss belongs to supra-aesthetics in the realm of Supreme Homogeneity.
items.title: Heterogeneity in Aesthetics

items.qualifiers: Acoustic and psycho-spiritual framework of language and cakras
items.quote: So for all the Cosmic expressions, there are fifty pencils of vibration – not fifty vibrations, but fifty pencils of vibration. And if we analyse properly, we get about one thousand vibrations. And that is why the pineal gland, the controlling body or controlling structure of those one thousand vibrations in the human body, is called “sahasrara cakra”, that is, “controlling one thousand vibrations”. But those one thousand vibrations come within fifty pencils of vibration, and those fifty pencils have sound, they have colour.
items.statement: Cosmic expressions consist of fifty pencils of vibration containing around one thousand sub-vibrations controlled by the sahasrára cakra, corresponding directly to the fifty letters of the Sanskrit alphabet.
items.title: His Reflections Are Everywhere

items.qualifiers: Historiographical definition according to Sanskrit tradition
items.quote: “The type of itivrtta which has the possibility of fulfilling physical longings, psychic longings, psycho-spiritual longings and spiritual longings, and which also imparts moral education, should be called itihása .”
items.statement: Itihása is distinct from itikathá (mere chronological history) and puráńa (moral myths without historical basis); itihása specifically denotes historical narrative possessing educative and moral value that fulfills the four human longings.
items.title: History and Superstition

items.quote: In philosophical Saḿskrta “súkśma” means the entity or entities that can not be perceived by sense-organs without the help of any other medium. And “átisúkśma” means those entities which can not be conceived by the mind.
items.statement: In philosophical Sanskrit, súkśma refers to entities that cannot be perceived by the sense organs without an external medium, while átisúkśma refers to entities that cannot be conceived by the mind.
items.title: How Does Jiiva Become Shiva

items.quote: Vaerágya is commonly understood to mean retiring from the world and leading a life of strict self-denial by practising excessive austerity. Vaerágya does not mean this. It does not make one a recluse. It only means to attempt to understand the proper use of things and to use them correctly (of course without working under the control of the crude objects of mind only).
items.statement: Vaerágya does not mean austere renunciation or becoming a recluse; it means understanding the proper, non-attached use of objects without becoming a slave to them.
items.title: How Should Human Beings Live In This World?

items.quote: The entity which is instrumental for the withdrawal of everything is called “Hara” and the entity responsible for the creation of unit beings is called “Hari”. This is the fundamental difference between Hari and Hara.
items.statement: The functional difference between Hari and Hara is that Hari creates and sustains unit beings, whereas Hara withdraws entities into Himself to re-project them in newer forms.
items.title: How Should a Devotee Behave?

items.quote: Self-sufficient socio-economic zones should be established throughout the world to smoothly eliminate social disparity and increase collective wealth. The formation of states on political grounds should be carefully avoided. In one political unit there may be several socio-economic zones which can live unitedly together with their respective problems.
items.statement: Lasting human unity requires establishing self-sufficient socio-economic zones based on economic potentialities and natural problems rather than dividing territories along political or linguistic borders.
items.title: How to Unite Human Society

items.quote: In the case of falsehood [as the noumenal entity], sin and crime coincide. In all other [cases] there are two different entities. ( 1 ) That which is not supported by the law of the land is called crime, and that which is not supported by cardinal human principles is sin.
items.statement: Crime is that which violates the mutable law of the land, whereas sin is that which violates universal cardinal human principles; the two coincide in falsehood as the noumenal cause.
items.title: Human Expressions and Human Movements

items.quote: The correct interpretation is, “Yoga means ‘unification’.” Unification by whom, with whom? Saḿyoga yoga ityukto jiivátma Paramátmanah. “Unification of the unit self with the Cosmic Self is yoga.” When your little “I” becomes one with your great “I”, that state is the state of yoga.
items.statement: Yoga is not mere thoughtlessness or suspension of propensities (which are negative states), but the positive unification of the unit self (jiivátma) with the Cosmic Self (Paramátman).
items.title: Human Life and Its Goal

items.quote: Pulsation means the combination of pause and speed. Where the stage of pause is experienced in the intellectual sphere, this pause is what we call intellectual liberation. The stage of mind when it becomes free from doubts and problems for a while is the state of pause or intellectual liberation. Psychic force created due to clashes in the intellectual sphere strikes the causal mind and powders it down. This finally re sults in the conversion of the causal mind into consciousness (self).
items.statement: Intellectual liberation is defined as the temporary state of pause in the pulsative movement of the mind when it becomes free from doubts and problems, striking and converting the causal mind into consciousness.
items.title: Human Progress

items.quote: At first the colour and physiognomical differences between the scattered Homo Sapiens were not very prominent. But with the passage of time, as they passed their lives over long periods amidst diverse geophysical conditions, differences in their physical structures became more and more apparent. Thus the apparent diversity in the human world today is the product of natural conditions.
items.statement: Physical differences in human features and melanin content are evolutionary adaptations to climate and solar radiation, deriving entirely from a common ancestral lineage.
items.title: Human Society Is One and Indivisible – 1

items.quote: “The concerted effort to bridge the gap between the first expression of morality and establishment in universal humanism is called ‘social progress’. And the collective body of those who are engaged in the concerted effort to conquer this gap, I call ‘society’.”
items.statement: Social progress is defined as the concerted effort to bridge the gap between morality's initial expression and establishment in universal humanism, and society is the collective body engaged in that effort.
items.title: Glossary

items.quote: In other words, the endeavour to make the controlling point of the “I” feeling coincide with some other subjectivated form is called meditation.
items.statement: Meditation is defined as the effort to make the controlling point of the 'I' feeling coincide with a subjectivated form.
items.title: Ideation and Meditation

items.quote: When the unit mind is established in psycho-spiritual parallelism, it is called “idea”, while the psychic conception of psycho-spiritual parallelism is called “ideology”. When idea maintains adjustment with the glands and sub-glands, it is called “ideation”.
items.statement: Idea is unit mind established in psycho-spiritual parallelism, ideology is its psychic conception, and ideation is idea maintaining adjustment with the glands and sub-glands.
items.title: Ideation and Meditation

items.quote: The sahasrára cakra is the psychological name and the Guru cakra is the physical name. The sahasrára cakra has no corporal structure. Its spiritual location is on the outer portion of the cranium (the point is called Brahmarandhra). The Guru cakra is just inside the cranium and is the controlling point of all the controlling points of all the brain cells on the physical, psychic and spiritual planes.
items.statement: The sahasrára cakra is the psychological name without corporal structure located at the Brahmarandhra, whereas the Guru cakra is its physical counterpart located inside the cranium acting as the common controlling point of all brain cells.
items.title: Ideation and Meditation

items.quote: Suppose there are two opposing ideas. The initial idea is tarka and the opposing idea is vimarsha. These two will produce a resultant which is called viveka or “conscience”. This entire procedure is called vicára. When one moves along the path of viveka, that movement is called “rationality”.
items.statement: The collision of two opposing ideas (tarka and vimarsha) yields a resultant called conscience (viveka), and progressing along this straight path avoiding unnecessary curvatures is rationality.
items.title: Ideation and Meditation

items.quote: The simplest formula is “action minus jiṋánam [knowledge] is equal to devotion” – “karma minus jiṋánam is equal to bhakti.”
items.statement: Devotion in the practical field functions according to the formula that selfless action minus intellectual knowledge equals resultant devotion.
items.title: I Will Not Discourage Jiṋánam

items.quote: But when the elephant is not present, but by dint of your psychic power you are again creating that elephant in your objective portion of mind, that second creation, rather re-creation (not “recreation”, “re-creation”) of the elephant, is called memory.
items.statement: Memory (smrti) is the psychic re-creation of an object in the objective portion of the mind when the external object itself is absent.
items.title: Ideological Flow and the Eight-fold Path

items.quote: In this phase or process of concentration, first of all, the figure of that flower will disappear. In the second phase the colour of the flower will disappear. And finally, the existence of the seer will merge into the existence, into the theoretical existence, of that flower. This suspension of mind into its object is known as samádhi.
items.statement: Samádhi is the sequential suspension of the mind into its object, moving from the disappearance of form, then colour, to the complete merger of the seer into the object's theoretical existence.
items.title: Ideological Flow and the Eight-fold Path

items.quote: Ideology is an impersonal element. To go toward “Iśt́a,” we need only love; whereas to follow an ideology we need courage and efforts.
items.statement: Ideology is an impersonal ideal requiring effort and courage, whereas Iśt́a is a personal goal pursued purely through love.
items.title: Ideology, Goal and Devotion

items.quote: The collective name of these six attributes, the eight occult powers [aeshvarya], viirya, yashah, shrii, jiṋána, and vaerágya, is bhaga.
items.statement: Bhaga consists of a collection of six attributes: aeshvarya (the eight occult powers), viirya, yasha, shrii, jiṋána, and vaerágya.
items.title: Iigal to Iikśańaka/ Iikśańika/ Iikśańiká (Discourse 8)

items.quote: [That Entity who remains unassailed by klesha (afflictions), by the bondages of karma, by vipáka [reactions] and áshaya (saḿskáras) is called Iishvara.]
items.statement: Iishvara is the specific Puruśa entity who remains entirely unassailed by afflictions (klesha), action (karma), reactions (vipáka), and mental imprints (áshaya/saḿskáras).
items.title: Iigal to Iikśańaka/ Iikśańika/ Iikśańiká (Discourse 8)

items.quote: It is improper to use the word shrii with a word that has the nádabindu, pronounced iishvara, attached to it, that is, while living we say Shrii Shubhamanas Sarkar and after death we say Iishvara Shubhamanas Sarkar, not Iishvara Shrii Shubhamanas Sarkar.
items.statement: The nádabindu mark (৺) used before the name of a deceased person is read as iishvara (equivalent to 'late'), and using the honorific shrii with it is improper.
items.title: Iigal to Iikśańaka/ Iikśańika/ Iikśańiká (Discourse 8)

items.quote: The fundamental difference between icchá and eśańá is that icchá is limited to one’s internal world but when that icchá is associated with the effort to give it a practical shape or an actional expression then it is called eśańá.
items.statement: Icchá is a desire confined entirely to the internal psychic world, whereas eśańá is desire conjoined with practical effort and actional expression.
items.title: Ik to Indura (Discourse 6)

items.quote: That portion of history in which there is morality and in which the four vargas, dharma, artha, káma, and mokśa, attain fruition is called itihása.
items.statement: Itihása is specifically that portion of historical narrative which contains moral instruction and wherein the four human pursuits (dharma, artha, káma, and mokśa) achieve fruition.
items.title: Ik to Indura (Discourse 6)

items.quote: Time can best be defined as the mental measurement of the motivity of action.
items.statement: Time is the mental measurement of the motivity of action.
items.title: In Adoration of the Supreme

items.quote: There are two types of actions: pratyayamúlaka (original actions) and saḿskáramúlaka (non-original or reactive actions). Human beings have the freedom to perform original actions as they think fit, whereas in non-original actions they are mechanically guided by the mutative force of Prakrti, who creates a congenial environment for the expression of their reactive momenta.
items.statement: Actions are divided into pratyayamúlaka (original actions performed with volitional freedom) and saḿskáramúlaka (non-original reactive actions where one is mechanically guided by Prakrti).
items.title: In Adoration of the Supreme

items.quote: In the Puranic Age, the commonly accepted practice was that the controlling deities derived from Post-Shiva Tantra were designated as “Dakśińá Shakti”, and those derived from Vajráyána Buddhism were designated as “Vámá Shakti”.
items.statement: In the synthesis of Tantric deities, deities originating from Post-Shiva Tantra are classified as Dakśińá Shakti, while those derived from Vajrayána Buddhism are designated as Vámá Shakti.
items.title: In the Glory of Shiva – Excerpt A

items.quote: Thus all the actional expressions of Prakrti [the Operative Principle] are performed only on the vast body of Supreme Consciousness. If Shakti takes one step away from the body of Shiva, it may be harmful. So Ardha-Náriishvara Shiva is a symbolic form of this creation by Shiva and Shakti.
items.statement: Ardha-Náriishvara Shiva symbolizes the philosophical necessity that blind creative energy (Shakti) must operate under the witnessing guidance and control of Supreme Consciousness (Shiva).
items.title: In the Glory of Shiva – Excerpt B

items.quote: In those days of matrilineal order, people introduced the system of mother worship, and from that emerged the custom of cańd́ii pújá, the worship of cańd́iká shakti, the power of the group-mother.
items.statement: Cańd́ii pújá originated as the worship of the authority of the clan-mother (gotramátá) during the prehistoric matrilineal order, which subsequently spawned virgin worship (kumárii pújá) to appease future clan-mothers.
items.title: In the Glory of Shiva – Excerpt C

items.quote: We must remember that actual progress can be made only in the spiritual stratum. There cannot be any progress in the physical stratum, or the physico-psychic stratum, or even in the psychic stratum. Whatever is known as progress is actually change of place and nothing more.
items.statement: True progress is only possible in the spiritual stratum; changes in the physical, physico-psychic, or psychic strata represent merely a change of place.
items.title: Incantation and Human Progress

items.quote: The average of rhythms of all rhythms – the rhythm of body, mind and soul, and the individual organs etc., of the body – is called individual rhythm.
items.statement: Individual rhythm is the average of all the rhythmic vibrations of an entity's body, mind, soul, and individual organs.
items.title: Individual Rhythm and Universal Rhythm

items.quote: Through spiritual practices the riches of the unconscious mind are brought down into the subconscious mind. The spiritual aspirant then understands everything; he discovers the secret signs of knowledge.
items.statement: Unconscious knowledge descends into the subconscious mind when deep mental one-pointedness is attained through spiritual practice or intense longing followed by deep sleep.
items.title: Indukamala to Iyatta (Discourse 7)

items.quote: While discussing Neohumanism, I said that study and rationalistic mentality are required to counteract geo-sentiment, and a proto-spiritualistic psychic structure is required to resist socio-sentiment.
items.statement: Geo-sentiment is counteracted by study and rationalistic mentality, whereas socio-sentiment is resisted by a proto-spiritualistic psychic structure utilizing sama-samája tattva.
items.title: Inner Asset

items.quote: When the psychic flow emanates from the feeling of unit corporality and moves along the maze of human corporal relationship and again comes back to its starting point, then that certain psychic flow is known as “instinct”.
items.statement: Instinct is defined as the psychic flow that emanates from the feeling of unit corporality, travels through human corporal relations, and loops back to its point of origin.
items.title: Instinct and Devotion

items.quote: When this instinct is converted into love for the Supreme, that metamorphosed instinct, that transmuted instinct, is known as “devotion”.
items.statement: Devotion is instinct that has undergone metamorphosis and transmutation into love for the Supreme Entity.
items.title: Instinct and Devotion

items.quote: When due to ignorance, microcosms think that there is something more besides Paramártha it is called the non-integral outlook. Conversely, when they feel in the core of their hearts that there is nothing within or without except Paramártha, and that whatever exists is nothing but His imagination, that is called the integral outlook.
items.statement: An integral outlook recognizes that nothing exists within or without except Paramártha, whereas a non-integral outlook arises when ignorance leads one to perceive something separate from Paramártha.
items.title: Integral and Non-Integral Outlook

items.quote: As a principle, subterranean water should not be used for irrigation purposes. Subterranean water should not be disturbed, otherwise the level of the water-table will drop, leading to an acute shortage of water. The best system is to collect surface water.
items.statement: Subterranean groundwater reserves should not be disturbed for irrigation because it depresses the water table; surface water conservation should be utilized instead.
items.title: Integrated Farming

items.quote: Náráyańa means the ayana of nára, the ayana of the Operative Principle, the ayana of the Paramá Prakrti. Who is the ayana, who is the shelter of Nára? Parama Puruśa is the shelter of Paramá Prakrti. So Náráyańa means Parama Puruśa – the Cosmic Consciousness, the Cognitive Faculty.
items.statement: Náráyańa means the shelter (ayana) of the Cosmic Operative Principle (Nára/Paramá Prakrti), which is Parama Puruśa.
items.title: Interpretation of “Ráma” and “Náráyańa”

items.quote: It will have to first retract from citta to ahaḿtattva, then from ahaḿtattva to mahattattva; and finally the metamorphosed projection as mahattattva will have to be withdrawn into unit consciousness for emancipation from the hold of Prakrti.
items.statement: In the inward path of sádhaná, consciousness must retract sequentially by absorbing citta into ahaḿtattva, ahaḿtattva into mahattattva, and finally dissolving mahattattva into pure unit consciousness.
items.title: Intuitional Practice and Its Necessity

items.quote: Hence any use of supernatural power brings one under the control of Avidyámáyá, which inevitably leads to a fall and to degradation.
items.statement: The display or application of supernatural powers obtained through intuitional practice constitutes a regression that subjects the practitioner back to the bondage of Avidyámáyá and Prakrti.
items.title: Intuitional Practice and Its Necessity

items.quote: The science of rhythm ( tála ) was formed out of tá , the first letter of the táńd́ava dance of Shiva and la , the first letter of the lalita dance of Párvatii.
items.statement: The science of musical rhythm (tála) was formulated from the first syllable 'tá' of Shiva's táńd́ava dance and 'la' from Párvatii's lalita dance.
items.title: Invention of Various Musical Instruments

items.quote: When the movement of a particular time, space and person maintains parallelism of similar movement related to a particular physical and mental wave, the resultant is called an "ism".
items.statement: An ism is established when there is correlated physical and psychic parallelism among time, space, and person.
items.title: Ism and Human Progress

items.quote: Now, so far as this expressed world is concerned, we may divide dharma into three broad categories.
items.statement: Dharma is categorized into three broad divisions: vastu dharma (governing inanimate and physical properties), jaeva dharma (governing instinctual maintenance of living beings), and Bhágavata Dharma (human spiritual dharma).
items.title: Jaeva Dharma and Bhágavata Dharma

items.quote: So vistára, rasa and sevá – these are the three essentialities for Bhágavata Dharma. Bhágavata Dharma is a must for every human being.
items.statement: Bhágavata Dharma is founded upon three essential pillars: vistára (psychic expansion), rasa (Cosmic flow), and sevá (selfless unilateral service).
items.title: Jaeva Dharma and Bhágavata Dharma

items.quote: The reflected flowers are jiivátmá, and the original flower is Pratyagátmá. Here the special name for Parama Puruśa is Pratyagátmá. The Entity that witnesses its reflected counterparts is Pratyak, pratyak+átmá=Pratyagátmá.
items.statement: Jiivátmá is the reflected counterpart of Paramátmá in the unit mental mirror, whereas Pratyagátmá is the original Witnessing Entity that witnesses all reflected counterparts.
items.title: Jiivátmá and Pratyagátmá

items.quote: When we fail to find a link between the preceding form and the succeeding form, then we say that the preceding form has undergone death.
items.statement: Death is the state reached when an observer fails to establish a continuous link between a preceding form and its succeeding form.
items.title: June-July 1970

items.quote: The mind has fifty propensities or [modes] of mental expression. These may be expressed internally [mentally] and externally [physically]. And this expression may be in ten directions – through the five sensory and five motor organs. Thus the total expressions of the mind are 50 x 2 x 10 = 1000. The sahasrára cakra controls these thousand expressions, and hence it has been called the thousand-petalled lotus.
items.statement: The sahasrára cakra controls one thousand modes of mental expression derived from fifty propensities expressed internally and externally across ten sensory and motor directions.
items.title: June-July 1970

items.quote: I therefore think that the term “penal system” should be deleted from social terminology. If and when somebody, whether a judge or an ordinary person, takes any type of action against another, it should be corrective, not punitive.
items.statement: Judicial systems should abolish purely punitive penal measures in favour of corrective measures to avoid cultivating vindictiveness and harming the wrongly accused.
items.title: Justice

items.quote: For the purpose of analysing the types of crime committed by a criminal, and whether his or her offences were committed voluntarily or at the instigation of others, criminals may be classified into the following five categories.
items.statement: Criminals are classified into five distinct categories: criminals by nature, criminals out of habit, criminals due to environment, criminals due to poverty, and criminals out of momentary weakness.
items.title: Justice

items.quote: I define immorality as that which, in order to further the personal interest of an individual or group, aims to exploit another individual or group or the rest of society, or aims to deprive them of the right to self-preservation. Behaviour based on such immoral intentions is a crime.
items.statement: Immorality is defined as any act intended to exploit an individual, group, or society, or deprive them of the right to self-preservation to advance selfish interests.
items.title: Justice

items.quote: The difference between kaola and Mahákaola is, the kaola raises his or her coiled serpentine, kulakuńd́alinii, through his or her sádhaná, and establishes the union [of] the fundamental negativity and the fundamental positivity; where in the case of the Mahákaola, the Mahákaola has the power to raise the kulakuńd́alinii of others also.
items.statement: In Tantra, a kaola raises their own kulakundalinii through spiritual practice, whereas a Mahakaola possesses the unique ability to raise the kulakundalinii of other aspirants as well.
items.title: Kaola and Mahákaola

items.quote: The point where the parabolic and the elliptical figures touch each other – that tangential point – is Táraka Brahma so far as the Cosmological order is concerned.
items.statement: Táraka Brahma is the tangential point where parabolic and elliptical movements touch in the cosmological order, taking physical form to guide people in Tantra and yoga.
items.title: Kaola and Mahákaola

items.qualifiers: qualified by 'As far as one can determine'
items.quote: As far as one can determine, He first instructed a non-Aryan, Karkat́ii Rákśasii by name. (Many arrogant Aryans called non-Aryans by derisive names such as dánava [devil], daetya [devil] or rákśasa [demon].) In all of India, Karkat́ii Rákśasii alone could confidently treat cholera and cancer.
items.statement: Lord Shiva first instructed his school of medicine (Vaedyak Shástra) to a non-Aryan woman named Karkatii Raksasii, who was uniquely capable of treating cholera and cancer.
items.title: Karkat́ii Rákśasii – Excerpt A

items.quote: What is knowledge? It is the understanding, with sharpened intellect, of what is permanent and what is temporary. Besides this, one has to analyse that out of the permanent which one is true and which one is false.
items.statement: Knowledge is defined as the understanding, achieved through sharpened intellect, of what is permanent versus temporary, separating substantial truth from dross.
items.title: Karma Is Brahma

items.quote: In case of a conflict between spiritual morality and simple morality, the first is destined to win, and the physical and psychological reason for the victory of spiritual morality is this: that spiritual morality is a dynamic force, and as it is a dynamic force, it has an inherent capacity to strike at the enemy.
items.statement: Spiritual morality is a dynamic force with an inherent capacity to strike against adversity, which naturally overcomes static simple morality during conflict.
items.title: Karna and Draopadi

items.qualifiers: under conditions of serious disproportion in gender ratios
items.quote: That’s why I have said that if there is a serious disproportion in the numbers of males and females in society (for instance, if the number of females exceeds the number of males), a man should be permitted to marry more than one woman just to maintain social purity. Conversely, if it so happens that the number of males exceeds the number of females, a woman will have to accept more than one husband, in order to maintain social purity.
items.statement: Under exceptional demographic imbalances resulting from war or catastrophe, polygyny or polyandry may be sanctioned as social provisions to preserve social purity.
items.title: Karna and Draopadi

items.quote: Kálii, when adorned with that garland of skulls, is called Kauṋkálamálinii, and the samádhi in which sádhakas identify themselves with Paramá Prakrti (symbolized by Kauṋkálamálinii) and experience indescribable joy, is described as Kauṋkálamálinii samádhi.
items.statement: Kaunkalamalinii samadhi is the spiritual absorption where sadhakas identify completely with Parama Prakrti and experience immense bliss along with severe somatic nervous pressure.
items.title: Kaunkálamálinii Samádhi

items.quote: In Saḿskrit, the entire literature is divided into four groups. One is kávya, the second is itikathá, the third is itihása and the fourth is puráńa.
items.statement: Sanskrit literature is categorized into four distinct groups: kavya (lucid aesthetic story), itikatha (factual chronicle), itihasa (educative factual history), and purana (educative myth/legend).
items.title: Keep Company with the Virtuous

items.quote: So this term durjana is a relative term. “Tyája durjana saḿsargaḿ” – you should avoid the company of a man who is durjana for you, that is, whose resultant demerit is more than your resultant merit.
items.statement: Durjana and sadhu are relative relational designations determined by whether an individual's net balance of merit and demerit can uplift or degrade another specific person.
items.title: Keep Company with the Virtuous

items.quote: The value of money increases with its mobility. That is, the more that money changes hands, the greater its economic value. On the other hand, the more that money is kept immobile in a safe, the more it loses its utility, and thus its economic value decreases. This is the most fundamental principle of economics.
items.statement: The fundamental principle of economics dictates that the value of money increases proportionally with its mobility and decreases with immobility.
items.title: Keep Money Rolling – Excerpt B

items.quote: The Tantric practice of mudrá sádhaná means to associate with good human beings in order to attain liberation.
items.statement: Mudra sadhana in Tantra is defined as the practice of shunning the company of negative persons and associating with virtuous people to attain all-round liberation.
items.title: Keeping Good Company

items.qualifiers: conditional on chronic excess acidity or contamination
items.quote: If such a situation continues for some time, the different waste materials found in the urine (accumulated naturally in the collecting system of the kidneys and in the urinary bladder) become high in proportion to the surplus water found there. And when that urine becomes sedimented, the waste materials start crystallizing.
items.statement: Kidney stones crystallize when high acid or poisonous contamination in the blood impairs heart and kidney function, causing waste solutes in sedimented urine to exceed surplus water.
items.title: Kidney-Stones

items.qualifiers: conditional on being chanted with maximum sincerity
items.quote: In case of natural calamities like flood, famine, drought or epidemic, or man-made calamities, miseries and tortures - if kiirtana is chanted with maximum sincerity, it will bring direct relief in no time.
items.statement: Collective sincere chanting of kiirtana removes both physical and psychic calamities by concentrating collective psycho-physical energies and drawing the direct presence of the Cosmic Entity.
items.title: Kiirtana Dispels Calamities

items.quote: The dhae portion means spiritual touch, the dhin portion means psychic touch, and the tá portion means the physical touch.
items.statement: In Lalita Marmika dance, touching the ground with the toe tip represents spiritual contact and minimal worldly pressure, the ball represents psychic contact, and the heel represents physical contact.
items.title: Kiirtana and Dance / The Psychic Order

items.quote: “Knowing” is a particular psychic projection. Not knowing is also a psychic projection, though of another form. One is positive and the other is negative. But both are psychic projections of the same type.
items.statement: Both knowing and not knowing are dual psychic projections within relative mental boundaries, whereas the transcendental Absolute Entity lies beyond all positive or negative ideational forms.
items.title: Knowing and Not Knowing

items.quote: Physico-psychic knowledge is the subjectivisation of external objectivity which may be physical, psychic or spiritual. In other words, knowledge is not sterile. It consists in the recognition of some objective matter and action done accordingly. Such knowledge, in practice is born out of a clash of instincts.
items.statement: Physico-psychic knowledge is defined as the mental subjectivisation of external objectivity, arising fundamentally from a clash of instincts.
items.title: Knowledge and Human Progress

items.quote: The wise do not take Paramátman as their object exactly, but rather think that they are being witnessed by Him. “Paramátman is not my object; I am the object of Paramátman.” When this feeling is constantly there, always there, in a person, the name of this stage is dhruvasmrti.
items.statement: True spiritual knowledge is attained not by attempting to make the Supreme Entity an object of the mind, but by cultivating the constant awareness that one is perpetually witnessed as an object by Cosmic Subjectivity (dhruvasmrti).
items.title: Knowledge and Progress

items.quote: Generally in poetry and lyrics, letters belonging to ca varga and ta varga are considered to be komala [soft], those of ka varga and pa varga are regarded as medium, and those of t́a varga ( 1 ) are considered hard.
items.statement: In poetic phonetic theory, consonants of the ca and ta vargas are classified as soft (komala), ka and pa vargas as medium, and the ta (cerebral) varga as hard.
items.title: Komalagiiti – Soft-Sounding Songs

items.quote: According to their relative density of crudeness developed through the bondage of the static principle, the five kośas, starting from the initial stage, are hirańmaya kośa, vijiṋánamaya kośa, atimánasa kośa, manomaya kośa and kámamaya kośa.
items.statement: The Cosmic Mind's crudification via the static operative principle is structured into five distinct mental kosas: hiranmaya, vijnanamaya, atimanasa, manomaya, and kamamaya.
items.title: Kośa

items.quote: When people attain progress in the realm of spiritual realization, that progress is divided into six stages – sálokya, sámiipya, sáyujya, sárúpya, sárśt́hi and kaevalya.
items.statement: Progress in spiritual realization evolves across six successive stages: salokya, samiipya, sayujya, sarupya, sarsthi, and kaevalya.
items.title: Krśńa Imparts Six Stages of Realization (Discourse 3)

items.quote: The kulakuńd́alinii rises upward in eight jumps or phases, so with two syllables in a siddha mantra, ( 1 ) the kuńd́alinii will jump four times. But a general, or publicly-given, siddha mantra will make the kulakuńd́alinii jump eight times or in eight phases. That is why such a siddha mantra has eight syllables.
items.statement: A proper publicly-given siddha mantra consists of eight syllables because the rising kundalinii makes eight jumps or phases from the muladhara to the sahasrara cakra.
items.title: Krśńa Unparalleled

items.quote: The school of medicine that depends on the Vedas is called áyurveda, and the Tantra-based school of medicine is called the vaedyaka shástra.
items.statement: The Vaedyaka Shastra is the Tantra-based school of medicine taught by Lord Shiva to Dhanvantari, distinct from the Veda-dependent Ayurveda Shastra.
items.title: Krśńa and Prapattiváda – 1 (Discourse 4)

items.qualifiers: conditional on temporal, spatial, or personal variance
items.quote: Regarding karma, it is said that for each and every action there is an equal and opposite reaction, provided the three fundamental relative factors, namely, the temporal factor, the spatial factor and the personal factor, remain unchanged, remain unassailed; otherwise, there will be a change in the reaction.
items.statement: The reaction to an action will not be equal and opposite if the three relative factors of time, space, and person undergo transformation between the action and its fruition.
items.title: Krśńa and Prapattiváda – 2 (Discourse 5)

items.quote: Now, for Kárańa Brahma the acoustic root, the biija mantra, is oṋm, and for Kárya Brahma, the created universe, the acoustic root is ka. That is why ka is the first letter of our consonants.
items.statement: The acoustic root of the causal entity (Karana Brahma) is 'om', whereas the acoustic root of the expressed creation (Karya Brahma) is 'ka', which forms the basis of the root 'klrm'.
items.title: Krśńa, the Nucleus of the Universe

items.quote: The quintessence of aesthetic science is to get joy and give joy. When the wavy movement at a certain stage of its progress is turned into linear movement, that is, the movement becomes straightened, then that is no longer aesthetic science, it becomes converted into supra-aesthetic science.
items.statement: Aesthetic science (nandana vijnana) involves mutual finite attraction moving in crests and troughs, whereas supra-aesthetic science (mohana vijnana) is the linear, irresistible spiritual attraction exerted exclusively by the Cosmic Nucleus upon all unit minds.
items.title: Krśńa and Supra-Aesthetic Science (Discourse 27)

items.quote: What originates in the mind and expands to the external world is called ripu [six inherent bondages]. That which originates outside and influences the mind is called pásha , as told earlier. An intelligent person keeps his or her ripu in control and fights the páshas .
items.statement: A person must control internal ripus (which originate internally and express outwardly) while actively opposing external pashas (imposed bondages that originate outside and fetter the mind).
items.title: Ku to Kuiṋjara (Discourse 27)

items.quote: Hence up until the age of thirty-nine the human body is called tanu . In tropical countries the human body after the age of thirty-nine should be called shariira , that whose nature is to become thin or emaciated.
items.statement: In human biology across tropical regions, the physical body is termed 'tanu' up to the age of thirty-nine while expanding, and 'shariira' after thirty-nine as it naturally tends toward emaciation.
items.title: Kukśa to Kuntala (Discourse 30)

items.quote: Upavása is undoubtedly a kind of voluntary abstention. However, at the same time there is to some extent a withdrawal of physical activity and a gradual directing of ones mental propensities towards closer proximity with Parama Puruśa . Upa means “near” and vása means “to stay”. Thus the etymological meaning of the word upavása is “to remain near the Lord”.
items.statement: Voluntary fasting (sveccha-anashana) provides physical rest to bodily organs, while upavasa additionally incorporates mental withdrawal and spiritual ideation toward Parama Purusa.
items.title: Kulya to Kuvela (Discourse 34)

items.quote: In a disembodied state the mind cannot work, because ectoplasmic structure can never function in that state. The stuff of which the mind is composed cannot function once it is detached from the body, because the mind-stuff functions only when the brain is active and the nerve cells are active.
items.statement: Disembodied minds cannot function independently without a living physical body and nervous system; anomalous physical events attributed to spirits occur only when a living person projects their own ectoplasm onto that disembodied seed.
items.title: “Kurvanneveha Karmmáńi”

items.quote: The fish help to keep the water clean and the level constant because their breathing creates water and carbon dioxide. The fish inhale oxygen along with water vapour from the atmosphere as well as dissolved oxygen from the water. They synthesize water which is exhaled into the lake.
items.statement: Developing pisciculture in artificial lakes maintains clean water and constant water volume, as fish respiration synthesizes water exhaled back into the reservoir.
items.title: Lakeside and Riverside Plantations

items.quote: Slope plants should always be planted in symmetrical horizontal lines and never in vertical lines, as this allows the water to flow away and encourages soil erosion.
items.statement: Slope-stabilizing plants must always be planted in horizontal symmetrical rows rather than vertical lines to prevent runoff and soil erosion.
items.title: Lakeside and Riverside Plantations

items.quote: Roughly speaking there are eight conditions that must be fulfilled in order to be considered a language, much like an eight-legged cot. These eight are: 1) own vocabulary, 2) pronouns, 3) verb-endings, 4) case-endings, 5) oral or written literature, 6) style of intonation, 7) psycho-acoustic and inferential acoustic notes, and 8) syntax.
items.statement: A linguistic system must fulfill eight specific criteria to qualify as a distinct language rather than a dialect: vocabulary, pronouns, verb-endings, case-endings, literature, intonation style, psycho-acoustic/inferential notes, and syntax.
items.title: Language and Dialect – 1 (Discourse 7)

items.quote: After the demise of the Vedic language in India seven different Prákrta languages came into existence. They were: Mágadhii, Shaorasenii, Paeshácii, Páshcáttya, Pahlavii or Saendhavii, Málavii and Maháráśt́rii.
items.statement: Following the decline of the Vedic language, seven distinct Prakrta languages emerged in India: Magadhi, Shaorasenii, Paeshacii, Pashcattya, Pahlavii/Saendhavii, Malavii, and Maharastrii.
items.title: Language and Dialect – 1 (Discourse 7)

items.quote: Varied opinions notwithstanding, the seven flames of fire recognized during the Buddhist period of the scientist Nagarjuna are: i) kálii , ii) karálii , iii) lelihána , iv) lolojihvá , v ) sarvalaktá , vi) kharpará , and vii) masiikrśńá .
items.statement: According to ancient Buddhist scientific classification associated with Nagarjuna, seven distinct flames of fire are recognized based on wind speed and unburnt carbon.
items.title: Kálii to Kikhi (Discourse 25)

items.quote: The sensorial measurement of the motivity of action is called kála . If the motivity of this ucchúnyá [unexpressed state of] Prakrti were not there, time would have been flawed by non-existence.
items.statement: Time (kala) is defined as the sensorial measurement of the motivity of action, which requires a measuring mind and relative displacement among entities.
items.title: Káliká to Káliuṋga (Discourse 24)

items.quote: According to the old school of thought, a philosophy that does not believe in any of the three – Vedas, the átmá [soul, spirit] or Paramátmá [Supreme Subjectivity]–is called atheistic. Belief in any of these three absolves one of the charge of atheism.
items.statement: A philosophical school is defined as theistic if it accepts any of three premises—the Vedas, the individual soul (atman), or the Supreme Subjectivity (Paramatman)—and atheistic only if it rejects all three.
items.title: Kámbal to Kárańa (Discourse 22)

items.quote: Only work done by hand is called shilpa [art] or shilpankriyá [an art product]. In other words, shilpa or shilpana means work in which manual skill is required. If you use the word hastashilpa , you commit the fallacy of tautology, because hastashilpa would literally mean “a handicraft made by hand”.
items.statement: In Indian linguistic precision, 'shilpa' or 'shilpana' strictly denotes skilled handicrafts executed by manual hand labour, rendering terms like 'kanthashilpii' (vocal artist) a semantic misnomer.
items.title: Kárpat́ika to Kála (Discourse 23)

items.quote: Literature refers to that art form which is based on letters while sáhitya is something altogether different. Simply being an art form based on letters does not qualify something to be called sáhitya. For it to be sáhitya it must imbibe the thought of welfare. Sáhitya means hitena saha [with welfare]. In other words, if a piece of literature is not motivated by the thought of welfare then it cannot be classified as sáhitya.
items.statement: Literature and sáhitya are not equivalent; literature refers to art based on letters, while sáhitya requires being motivated by the thought of universal welfare.
items.title: Language and Dialect – 2 (Discourse 8

items.quote: The mind must always have an object (viśaya). In scriptures, viśaya is known as “ábhoga.” “Ábhoga” means that object which feeds the mind – that is, mental pabulum. If this pabulum is limited, the mind also becomes limited. If the pabulum is infinite, by making an effort to obtain it, the mind becomes infinite. It depends entirely on the will of human beings which pabulum, limited or unlimited, is made their object.
items.statement: Human beings possess an independent mind capable of choosing bondage or liberation depending on whether they select a limited or infinite mental object (ábhoga).
items.title: Leaving Bondage

items.quote: NO”, because the quadri-dimensional manava dharma (human dharma) is one and the same. It includes: vistara (expansion), rasa (flow), sevá (service) and mokśa (spiritual emancipation).
items.statement: Human dharma (mánava dharma) is quadri-dimensional, comprising vistara, rasa, sevá, and mokśa, and is identical for both householders and renunciates.
items.title: Let History Be Rewritten

items.quote: The third one is Nirakśara Brahma. “Kśarátmanáviishate deva ekah”. There is another Deva who establishes His control both over Kśara and Akśara. He is Nirakśara. The common meaning of nirakśara is illiterate but here nirakśara means “Táraka Brahma” – the tangential point who has got control over both Kśara and Akśara, but not Nirguńa because Nirguńa has got no control over anything. He does not accept anything as His object.
items.statement: Nirakśara Brahma represents Táraka Brahma as the tangential controller over both mutable (Kśara) and non-mutable (Akśara) entities, distinct from Nirguńa Brahma who accepts no object.
items.title: Liberation from Viśńumáyá

items.quote: The loss in the parallelism of physical and mental waves causes death. The physical cause of death is the passing away of the nine (ten minus dhanaiṋjaya) váyus into eternal space. The psychic waves, finding no proper adjustment with the physical waves, also dissociate and pass into eternal space.
items.statement: Physical death occurs when the loss of parallelism between physical and psychic waves causes the dissociation of mental and physical structures, leading the ten vital airs to depart, with dhanaiṋjaya lingering until burning or complete decay.
items.title: Life, Death and Saḿskára

items.quote: Práńáh is the collective name of ten váyus, five internal and five external. The internal váyus are práńa, apána, samána, udána and vyána; and the external váyus are nága, kúrma, krkara, devadatta and dhanaiṋjaya.
items.statement: Práńáh consists of ten distinct vital airs divided into five internal váyus and five external váyus, each governing specific bodily and physiological functions.
items.title: Life, Death and Saḿskára

items.quote: When the underlying spirit of humanism is extended to everything, animate and inanimate, in this universe – I have designated this as Neohumanism. This Neohumanism will elevate humanism to universalism, the cult of love for all created beings of this universe.
items.statement: Neohumanism is defined as the extension of the underlying spirit of humanism to everything, both animate and inanimate, elevating humanism to universalism.
items.title: Light Comes

items.quote: Each and every living entity, whether plant or animal, has two types of value: one, its “utility value” and the other, its “existential value.”
items.statement: Every living entity possesses both an existential value to itself and potentially a utility value to others, but lack of recognized utility does not negate a creature's moral right to exist.
items.title: Light Comes

items.quote: When the causal factor is known to you, it is kriidá, and when the causal factor is not known to you, it is liilá.
items.statement: Liilá refers to creation whose causal factor is unknown to the unit being, whereas kriidá is creation whose causal factor is known.
items.title: Liilá and Kriidá

items.quote: A collective tendency, a tendency to live in groups, that is based on sentiment, is called “socio-sentiment”. Socio-sentiment is a million times more harmful than geo-sentiment, because socio-sentiment leads people much further from proper thinking than does geo-sentiment.
items.statement: Socio-sentiment is defined as a collective tendency to live in groups or communities based on sentiment rather than rationality.
items.title: Living Beings and Their Mentality (Discourse 5)

items.quote: There is a feeling of “I exist” in me – “I exist”. That “I” is the subtlest mind. The feeling that “I exist” is in me, is known to me. That knowing “I” – “I know that I exist” – that knowing “I” (the “I” of “I know”) is the átman, the spirit, the soul.
items.statement: In self-awareness, the subject of 'I exist' represents the subtlest mind (guhá), while the witness 'I know that I exist' represents the átman (soul).
items.title: Longing for the Great

items.quote: This past instruction was – the eight instructions are – samyak darshana, samyak saḿkalpa, samyak vák, samyak ájiiva, samyak vyáyáma, samyak karmánta, samyak smrti, and samyak samádhi . These are the Eight-Fold Path.
items.statement: Buddha's Eight-Fold Path (Aśt́áuṋga Mágga) consists of eight cardinal practices beginning with inner vision (samyak darshana) and culminating in mental suspension (samyak samádhi).
items.title: Lord Buddha's Cardinal Principles

items.quote: Samyak darshana means not only seeing externally with these crude eyes, or rather, with the help of your [[optical]] power only; inner darshana means seeing with your inner ocular force; and this is the difference between “optical” and “ocular”. “Optical” is always physical, and “ocular” is physico-psychic and at the same time psycho-physical.
items.statement: Samyak darshana signifies seeing with inner intuitional vision (ocular force) to discover root causes rather than judging merely by external sensory perception (optical power).
items.title: Lord Buddha's Cardinal Principles

items.quote: The vibrational manifestations emanating from the Supreme Nucleus are known as “Devatás”, and these devatás address that Supreme Nucleus as “Deva”. That Supreme Nucleus is addressed by the term “Deva”. He with His powers vibrates the entire universe, makes the entire universe dance táńd́ava; and He by dint of His occult and supra-occult powers brings back everything unto His lap. This is the definition of “Deva”, and these rays and pencils of rays coming out from the Nucleus are known as “Devatás”.
items.statement: Deva refers to the Supreme Nucleus that vibrates the entire universe and withdraws it into Itself, whereas Devatás are the vibrational manifestations emanating from that Nucleus.
items.title: Lord of All Lords

items.quote: This particular type of yoga where a yogii does not bear love for the Supreme Entity is called “hat́ha yoga” in Saḿskrta. It is dangerous for the human elevation. “Hat́ha” comes from “ha” and “t́ha”. “Ha” represents “súrya nádii or ida nádii” and is the acoustic root of physical force. “Tha” represents “candra nádii or piuṋgalá nádii” and is the acoustic root of the mind. So “hat́ha” implies forcible control of mind by physical force.
items.statement: Hat́ha yoga denotes forcible physical control of the mind without devotion to the Supreme Entity, resulting in psychic stagnation into crude matter.
items.title: Love – the Essential Prerequisite

items.quote: The propensitive equipoise is a characteristic only of the Macrocosmic Entity, since in It lies everything, nothing is beyond or external to It. Hence it remains unassailed. But microcosms have an external world and get assailed therefrom due to incoming vibrations, to have an unbalanced state.
items.statement: Macro-propensitive equipoise is an exclusive attribute of the Macrocosm because everything exists within It, eliminating the need for external mental pabulum.
items.title: Macro-Propensitive Equipoise and Non-Propensitive Desideratum

items.quote: The physical control of any cakra is exercised by the controlling point of that cakra, but its ideational control is exercised by the controlling point of the next higher cakra. For instance, the svadhisthana cakra cannot have full control, both physical and ideational, over all the nerve-cells and nerve-fibres attached to the svadhisthana cakra; rather the ideational aspect of the control remains with the manipura cakra.
items.statement: In the human cakra system, physical control is exercised by a cakra's own controlling point, but ideational control is governed by the controlling point of the next higher cakra.
items.title: Mahásambhúti Krśńa

items.quote: Mantra caetanya is the condition where, with the help of a particular shabda, a person establishes parallelism between his or her external physical vibration and his or her internal ectoplasmic vibration, and then raises this to the spiritual level. ( 3 ) And the culmination of this process in the achievement of the final spiritual goal is called mantra siddhi.
items.statement: Mantra caetanya is the awakening of a mantra by establishing parallelism between unit physical vibration, internal ectoplasmic vibration, and the spiritual level.
items.title: Mantra Caetanya

items.quote: Shravana therefore enables one to cross the vibrational faculty. Manana enables one to cross the primordial faculty. And nididhyásana makes it possible to merge with the Supreme Entity.
items.statement: Crossing the three cosmic faculties back to the Supreme Entity requires three progressive spiritual practices: shravana crosses the vibrational faculty, manana crosses the primordial faculty, and nididhyásana enables merger into the basic principle.
items.title: Mantra Caetanya

items.quote: Similarly, all mantras must have two meanings. One meaning is the mundane significance, and the other is the acoustic root. And wherever either meaning is wanting, the word cannot be treated as a mantra.
items.statement: To qualify as a mantra, a word must possess both a mundane significance and an acoustic root, verified by a Mahákaola.
items.title: Mantra and Incantation

items.quote: Master Units will be the minia ture forms of Ánanda Nagar, and these Master Units will be the main centres for the Ánanda Márgiis. Master Units should be a minimum of five acres. The Saḿskrta name of Master Unit is “Cakranemii” which means “the nucleus of the cakra” (wheel). I want all Master Units to be economically self-sufficient in all respects, because spiritualists should not depend on the wealthy class for money.
items.statement: Master Units (Cakranemii) must be at least five acres in size and serve as economically self-sufficient miniature models of Ananda Marga providing the five fundamental minimum necessities.
items.title: Master Units

items.quote: Energy is a blind force. It has got no conscience – what is to be done or what should not be done, this sort of conscience is lacking in energy. But microvita are not like that; that is, they are not blind forces. They have the support of conscience behind them. This is another fundamental difference between energy and microvita.
items.statement: Matter is the 'known I' in the cosmic arena, whereas microvita and energy exist on the demarcation line between matter and abstract, with microvita carrying the support of conscience while energy is a blind force.
items.title: Matter and Abstract

items.quote: The difference between physical science and logicians’ philosophy is that the former has a considerable benevolent aspect but the latter is dark on both sides. Logicians’ philosophy at times weaves a web of logic around matter and at other times it endeavours to find the relation between thought and matter; and then again at other times it plays blind man’s buff in the blind alley of thoughts.
items.statement: Physical science is inherently analytical and subject to refutation, whereas spiritual philosophy is unitive and synthetic, synthesizing rather than destroying prior realizations.
items.title: Matter and Spirit

items.quote: Instead the correct and psychological approach to Máyá is to channelize it in the direction of the Absolute. For in this expressed world, you cannot overpower Máyá because she has a much greater power.
items.statement: Freedom from Máyá (Mukti) cannot be achieved by suppressing or warring against Máyá, but by channelizing her sentient operative principle toward the ideation of the Absolute.
items.title: Máyá and Mokśa

items.quote: Shakti [the Operative Principle] is not an independent entity. It is dependent on Him.
items.statement: Shakti (the Operative Principle) is dependent on and controlled by Parama Puruśa rather than being an independent entity.
items.title: “Máyámetáḿ Taranti Te” - 2 / The Nectar Beyond Máyá

items.quote: The virtuous who, after death, have retained a few but not all of the five fundamental factors are called apsarás .
items.statement: Apsarás are defined as virtuous entities who, after death, do not possess physical bodies composed of all five fundamental factors but retain only a few.
items.title: Meditative Songs Heard from Afar

items.quote: There are three methods of salutation: (1) sáśt́áuṋga prańáma [prostration], (2) carańa sparsha prańáma [bowing and touching the feet] and (3) namaskára [salutation].
items.statement: Salutation comprises three specific methods: sáśt́áuṋga prańáma (reserved strictly for Márga Guru), carańa sparsha prańáma (touching the feet of highly regarded worldly or spiritual elders), and namaskára (touching the ájiṋá cakra for all persons).
items.title: Methods of Salutation

items.quote: Do not shake hands with anyone, because it is unhygienic, and do not do kurnish [a kind of court salute signifying submission to one’s authority] to anyone, as you are not anyone’s slave. Kurnish is a symbol of slavery, so as a form of salutation it is strictly forbidden.
items.statement: Handshakes are forbidden due to being unhygienic, and kurnish is strictly forbidden because it symbolizes slavery.
items.title: Methods of Salutation

items.qualifiers: defined in context of mental measurement
items.quote: First of all, take the case of the tempus, the Tempus Eternal. What is it? It is a psychic measurement of the motivity of action.
items.statement: Time (tempus eternal) is defined as a psychic measurement of the motivity of action.
items.title: Microcosm and Its Object of Ideation

items.quote: What you call fate is actually the reaction of our past actions. In saḿskrta, it is called saḿskára, in Latin “reactive momenta”.
items.statement: Fate is nothing other than the unserved reactions of past actions (saḿskára or reactive momenta).
items.title: Microcosm and Its Object of Ideation

items.quote: The non-attributional supreme rank of Parama Puruśa is located at the pineal plexus (sahasrára cakra), ten fingers above the pituitary plexus (lunar plexus or ajiṋa cakra, the location of mind as well as kut́astha caetanya).
items.statement: The non-attributional supreme rank of Parama Puruśa at the sahasrára cakra is situated ten fingers above the pituitary plexus (ájiṋá cakra), which represents the controlling seat of the mind and the fundamental factors.
items.title: Microcosm and Macrocosm

items.quote: Of all the, inferences, sound and touch are very subtle and so their receptors, the ears and the skin, are dominated by the sentient principle. The smell and taste tanmátras are very crude and hence their receptors, the tongue and the nose, are dominated by the static principle. The remaining form tanmátra, which is neither crude nor subtle, has the eyes as its receptor and is dominated by the mutative principle. Regarding the motor organs, the vocal cords and the hands are dominated by the sentient principle, the legs by the mutative principle, and the anus and genital organs by the static principle.
items.statement: Receptors for sound and touch (ears and skin) and motor organs like vocal cords and hands are dominated by the sentient principle; eyes and legs are dominated by the mutative principle; and smell, taste, anus, and genital organs are dominated by the static principle.
items.title: Microcosm and Macrocosm

items.quote: Microcosm is multipurposive but its flow is unilateral. On the other hand, Macrocosm is uni-purpose but its flow is multilateral.
items.statement: The microcosm is multipurposive but flows unilaterally (can focus in only one direction at a time), whereas the Macrocosm is unipurposive (universal welfare) but multilateral in flow.
items.title: Microcosm and Macrocosm

items.quote: This expressed universe is Kárya Brahma and the remaining portion is Kárańa Brahma. Kárya Brahma and Kárana Brahma together form Saguna Brahma or attributed Consciousness, or qualified Consciousness.
items.statement: The expressed universe of physical manifestation is Kárya Brahma whose acoustic root is 'ka', while the unmanifest witnessing remainder is Kárańa Brahma; together they constitute Saguńa Brahma.
items.title: Microcosm and Macrocosm

items.quote: Positive microvita equal negative microvita – that is, the sum total of positive microvita equals the sum total of negative microvita. This is so in the entire macrocosm and in individual microcosmic structures.
items.statement: The sum total of positive microvita equals the sum total of negative microvita across both the entire macrocosm and individual microcosmic frameworks.
items.title: Microvita and Cosmology

items.quote: Positive microvita elevate the upgrading propensities, but the field of activity for negative microvita is the Manipur Cakra and below.
items.statement: Microvita are not directly involved in the pure spiritual stratum, and negative microvita are restricted in their activity to the Manipur Cakra and below.
items.title: Microvita and Cosmology

items.quote: A scientist in the microvita age will refuse to accept the carbon atom as the rudimental factor for the emergence of life. To him or her a carbon atom is nothing but billions of microvita getting solidified.
items.statement: Carbon atoms and protoplasmic cells are not rudimental ultimate factors of life, but solidified collective aggregates of billions of microvita.
items.title: The Theory of Microvita and Its Possible Effects on Society – Excerpt A

items.quote: The longevity of all forms of protoplasm is twenty one days. Changes will also occur in this regard.
items.statement: The natural longevity of all forms of protoplasm is twenty-one days.
items.title: The Theory of Microvita and Its Possible Effects on Society – Excerpt B

items.quote: Except for the pineal gland and the upper layers of the pituitary gland, they influence almost each and every atom of the human structure; only the negative microvita cannot influence any portion of the body above the pituitary gland. The positive microvita may function above it but cannot touch the pineal gland.
items.statement: Negative microvita cannot directly influence any part of the human physical or glandular structure above the pituitary gland, nor can positive microvita touch the pineal gland.
items.title: Microvita and Their Influence on Micropsychic and Macropsychic Corporal Structures

items.qualifiers: clear distinction of spiritual vs psychic phenomena
items.quote: A khamúrtti, however, is a thoroughly spiritual vision. Cháyá puruśa is a mere image of a shadow, whereas khamúrtti is an image of bright effulgence.
items.statement: A khamúrtti is an effulgent spiritual vision granting spiritual inspiration, whereas a cháyá puruśa is an optical shadow effect created by light-and-shade used in hypnotism.
items.title: Microvita and Spiritual Attainment

items.quote: A person in the stage of meditation cannot be attacked by negative microvitum, but positive microvitum can work directly in the lunar plexus and it can move, rather it does move, up to the occult plexus (the Guru Cakra). But it cannot go beyond the occult plexus – it cannot touch the macro-propensive plexus.
items.statement: Positive microvita move from the lunar plexus up to the occult plexus (Guru Cakra) but cannot proceed beyond to touch the macro-propensive plexus.
items.title: Microvitum and Its Effect on Human Body and Human Mind

items.quote: So these microvita may be broadly divided into three categories – first, those coming within the scope of [[a microscope]]; secondly, those not coming within the scope of a microscope but coming within the scope of perception as a result of their expression, as a result of their actional vibration; and thirdly, those not coming within the scope of common perception but coming within the scope of a special type of perception which is actually the reflection of conception within the periphery of perception.
items.statement: Microvita are broadly categorized into three density classes: those within the scope of a microscope, those perceptible only via their actional vibrations, and those perceived through a special reflection of conception within perception by developed minds.
items.title: Microvitum, the Mysterious Emanation of Cosmic Factor

items.quote: So far as physicality is concerned, the position of these microvita is just between ectoplasm and electron, but they are neither ectoplasm nor electron.
items.statement: Microvitum is physically situated between ectoplasm and electron, being neither of protoplasmic order nor reliant on carbon molecules.
items.title: Microvitum, the Mysterious Emanation of Cosmic Factor

items.qualifiers: determined by vision while in viirásana
items.quote: If the colour is golden-yellow or earth-yellow, then kśititattva [solid factor] dominates, and if the colour is watery white, then apatattva [liquid factor] dominates. Both these colours are good for physical activities. When the red colour appears there is a domination of tejastattva [luminous factor], and the time is good for physical activity and, to some extent, for mental activity.
items.statement: In viirásana, seeing golden-yellow or watery white reflects solid or liquid factor dominance suited for physical action; red reflects luminous factor for physical and some mental action; blue or green indicates aerial factor suitable for mental and spiritual activity; and snow-white indicates ethereal factor ideal for sádhaná.
items.title: Mind, Memory and Colours

items.quote: It is during the state of pause and potentiality that the citta is able to receive the tanmátras and takes the form of shapes represented by those tanmátras. Unless citta takes the form of incoming tanmátras no perception is possible, because the ego can work only when the citta adopts a form.
items.statement: Práńendriya operates pulsatively; during its pause, the citta can receive tanmátras, whereas during its expansive stage, sympathetic nerve vibration hinders tanmátra perception.
items.title: Mind, Práńendriya and Vrtti

items.quote: A sádhaka, who is a practical psychologist, realizes that instinct is a sentiment affecting the subsidiary glands.
items.statement: Instinct is defined practically by yogic psychology as a sentiment affecting the subsidiary glands (any glands other than the pineal and pituitary).
items.title: Mind, Práńendriya and Vrtti

items.quote: The subsidiary glands control forty-eight vrttis and the pituitary controls two – saḿkalpátmaka, or one leading to parávidyá (knowledge of the Great) and vikalpátmaka, relating to aparávidyá (knowledge of the mundane). The pineal as a structure controls all these fifty vrttis taken internally and externally by all ten indriyas. 50 x 2 x 10 = 1000.
items.statement: The human body possesses 50 crude vrttis controlled internally and externally across the ten indriyas (50 x 2 x 10 = 1000 expressions), whose collective seeds reside in the sahasrára cakra.
items.title: Mind, Práńendriya and Vrtti

items.quote: Reflected portion is called jiivátmá and the original entity whose reflections they are is called Pratyagátma. Now Pratyagatmá is the Paramátmá. Jiivátmá is not the Paramátmá, it is simply a reflection.
items.statement: Jiivátmá is the reflected consciousness on the unit mental plate, whereas Pratyagátma (Paramátmá) is the original unreflected Singular Entity.
items.title: Mind and Cognitive Faculty

items.quote: PROUT’s approach is to guarantee the minimum requirements for all, guarantee maximum amenities for all and guarantee special amenities for people with special capabilities.
