items.statement: PROUT requires guaranteeing ever-increasing minimum requirements to all, maximum amenities to common people as well, and special amenities for people of special calibre to encourage greater service.
items.title: Minimum Requirements and Maximum Amenities

items.quote: The mutative force is a hundred thousand times more powerful than the static force, and the sentient force is a hundred thousand times more powerful than the mutative force; hence you should not be afraid of any force in the universe.
items.statement: The mutative force is a hundred thousand times more powerful than the static force, and the sentient force is a hundred thousand times more powerful than the mutative force.
items.title: Miscellaneous

items.quote: Self-hypnotism is called ávesha. In self-hypnotism all the indriyas come under the control of the mind and act according to the dictates of mind. But samádhi cannot be attained without mind being dissolved.
items.statement: Samádhi cannot be equated with self-hypnotism (ávesha); in self-hypnotism indriyas obey the mind, whereas in samádhi the mind itself dissolves.
items.title: Miscellaneous

items.qualifiers: philosophical evaluation of progress vs movement
items.quote: So I must say that there is movement in the physical sphere but there is no progress in the physical sphere; there is movement in the psychic sphere, but there cannot be any progress in the psychic sphere; but progress and movement both exist in the realm of spirituality – that is, spiritual progress is the progress, and other kinds of progress [do not represent any real gain].
items.statement: Progress does not exist in the physical or psychic spheres because they lack a culminating point; genuine progress exists only in the spiritual movement towards the Cognitive Faculty.
items.title: Mobility and Cognitive Stance

items.quote: The ideological component of the unit mind which provides the initial inspiration for the individual to attain that Cosmic state, is called “morality”. Every aspect of morality sings the song of the Infinite, even in the midst of the finite.
items.statement: Morality is defined as those magnanimous propensities of the ideological component of the unit mind that inspire and lead the individual to attain the Cosmic state.
items.title: Moralism

items.quote: The concerted effort to bridge the gap between the first expression of morality and establishment in universal humanism is called “social progress”. And the collective body of those who are engaged in the concerted effort to conquer this gap, I call “society”.
items.statement: Social progress is defined as the concerted effort to bridge the gap between the initial expression of morality and full establishment in universal humanism.
items.title: Moralism

items.quote: So if a man is a super-moralist, but he doesn’t do any spiritual practice, his downfall is inevitable; that is, his movement towards bhútajiṋánii is inevitable. So wise people must do spiritual practice.
items.statement: If a person strictly adheres to moral principles but neglects spiritual practice, the lack of positive pratisaiṋcara acceleration will inevitably cause negative pratisaiṋcara (downfall towards bhútajiṋána).
items.title: Movement Is the Order of the Day

items.quote: Movement towards perfection, that is, God, is dharma; while movement towards imperfection is adharma. The former is life, the latter is death. A human being’s movement towards animalism is, therefore, death.
items.statement: Dharma is defined as movement towards perfection (God), whereas movement towards imperfection is adharma and spiritual death.
items.title: Movement towards Perfection Is Dharma

items.quote: To communicate ideas through gesture and posture is called “ mudrá ”. In the East, we find that dance is dominated by mudrá , and in the West, we find that it is dominated by rhythm. Indian folk dance and classical dance are also mudrá -dominant. Mudrá is more subtle than rhythm.
items.statement: Mudrá is the communication of ideas through gesture and posture, being more subtle than rhythm.
items.title: Mudrá

items.quote: This search for the Great by the little is called mysticism. The fundamental point of spirituality depends on this mysticism.
items.statement: Mysticism is defined as the never-ending search for the Great by the little, seeking the glamour and grandeur of the Lord.
items.title: Mysticism

items.quote: Pátakas are of three kinds. First, the ordinary kind. These are undesirable acts after which the person [may repent]. For instance, someone takes the money of others. That person’s act will be called pátaka, for he or she can pay back the money and repent of the act.
items.statement: Pátakas (sins) comprise ordinary pátaka (reparable and atoneable), atipátaka (irreparable damage like severing limbs, atoned by complete renunciation in service to humanity), and mahápátaka (recurring damage requiring an invention or contribution of recurring societal benefit).
items.title: Mysticism and Spirituality

items.quote: Your attraction to the Supreme is called devotion [bhakti], whereas attraction to any finite objectivity is called ásakti. Attraction to friends is ásakti, attraction to God is bhakti. In the case of ásakti the object is limited, in the case of bhakti it is unlimited.
items.statement: Attraction to finite objects is ásakti, whereas attraction to the infinite Supreme is bhakti (devotion).
items.title: Mysticism and Spirituality

items.quote: In Sanskrit, yoga means “addition”. For instance, two plus two is equal to four. But for a mystic, for an aspirant of the mystic goal or the mystic desideratum, yoga is not only addition; here yoga means “unification”. What sort of unification? It is just like sugar and water.
items.statement: In ordinary arithmetic yoga means addition where entities retain individual identities (like adding apples), but in mysticism yoga means complete unification without separate identity (like sugar dissolving in water).
items.title: Mysticism and Yoga

items.quote: Now, let us see why the name is more powerful than the named. The shakti, or energy, in the name is kendrita – centralized. It is stambhita – latent. But when a name comes into being, it means a namer has come, and through the name, the named is addressed. In that situation, the latent power in the name gets activated.
items.statement: The name (náma) of the Lord is more powerful than the named (námii) because the potential energy in the name is activated and translated into action through the calling of the devotee.
items.title: Náma and Námii

items.quote: Human longings are trilateral [physical, mental and spiritual], so he will have to come in contact with physical objects, and he will have to ascribe Brahma-hood to those physical objects. And those physical objects are not a creation of the Cognitive Principle or of the Operative Principle, but a creation of both of them. Both of them have jointly created this universe. So while ascribing Brahma-hood, he will have to think of Prakrti also. That’s why a spiritual aspirant is not called Puruśa sádhaka or Prakrti sádhaka; He is called Brahma sádhaka.
items.statement: Spiritual aspirants are called Brahma sádhakas rather than Puruśa or Prakrti sádhakas because they must interact with the physical world while ascribing Brahma-hood to all physical objects to prevent negative introversion.
items.title: Names of the Supreme

items.quote: So first there is “spirituality as a cult”, secondly, “spirituality in essence”, and thirdly, “spirituality as a mission”. All existential phenomena are emanating from the Existential Nucleus. The existential nucleus of a single individual has a direct link with the Cosmological Hub, a direct link with the Existential Nucleus of the Cosmological order. But this path is not psycho-spiritual; according to Neohumanism, the final and supreme goal is to make one’s individual existential nucleus coincide with the Cosmic Existential Nucleus ( nádabindu yoga , in the language of Tantra).
items.statement: The path of Neohumanism comprises three developmental stages: spirituality as a cult (physico-psycho-spiritual practice), spirituality in essence (reorienting humanity's collective mind), and spirituality as a mission (merging the individual existential nucleus into the Cosmic Existential Nucleus via nádabindu yoga).
items.title: Neohumanism Is the Ultimate Shelter (Discourse 11)

items.quote: In the case of niiti, indeed, there are certain dos and don’ts. In Sanskrit these dos are called vidhi, and the don’ts are called niśedha. The collection of dos and don’ts is niiti. But as regards dharma there are no don’ts, everything is do; that is, everything is a conduct which has to be performed.
items.statement: Niiti involves both positive prescriptions (vidhi) and negative prohibitions (niśedha), whereas dharma contains only positive conduct without prohibitions.
items.title: Niiti and Dharma

items.quote: An action devoid of cosmic ideation is kriyá. If we are to live in the world we must perform actions in order to maintain our physical existence. Whatever we do with our physical organs without a spiritual purpose is our kriyá – sleeping, resting, drinking and eating devoid of cosmic ideation are kriyá and not karma. Actions performed with cosmic ideation are termed karma.
items.statement: Actions devoid of cosmic ideation are categorized as kriyá and lead to bondage, whereas actions performed with cosmic ideation are termed karma and lead to liberation.
items.title: Nitya Karma and Naemittik Karma

items.quote: Bodha means experience supported by the intellect. Suppose you saw something wonderful – that was an experience for you. However, no idea of yours is connected to that experience which you had. So this is not bodha, or knowing.
items.statement: Bodha (knowing) is defined specifically as experience supported by the intellect rather than raw perception alone.
items.title: Nityaḿ Shuddhaḿ

items.qualifiers: Applies as long as thought has not converted to physical action
items.quote: I have also told you that I never consider “mental sins” as “sin”, although it is a fact that mind’s sinful thoughts may ultimately take shape as sinful deeds. But so long as the sinful thought is not expressed externally it is neither condemnable nor punishable and should not be called a sin as the person concerned did not cause any harm to the world or any or its people.
items.statement: A sinful thought that remains purely internal without physical manifestation is neither condemnable, punishable, nor considered a sin.
items.title: Nityánanda and Liilánanda

items.quote: According to the shástras [scriptures], the death noose has three-and-a-half rounds: the first round – the pain of birth the second round – the tortures of life the third round – the pang of death the last half round – moha (desire) for birth
items.statement: According to scripture, the noose of death consists of three and a half rounds.
items.title: Nityánitya Viveka

items.quote: He cannot do two things: He cannot hate anybody, and He cannot create another Parama Puruśa!
items.statement: Parama Puruśa cannot hate anyone, nor can He create another Parama Puruśa.
items.title: No One Is Negligible

items.quote: PROUT advocates another type of revolution called “nuclear revolution”. In nuclear revolution, every aspect of collective life – social, economic, political, cultural, psychic and spiritual – is completely transformed.
items.statement: Nuclear revolution refers to the complete transformation of every aspect of collective life, accomplishable exclusively by sadvipras.
items.title: Nuclear Revolution

items.qualifiers: In the context of ending vaeshya exploitation
items.quote: Shúdras can never be the actual revolutionaries because they lack sufficient moral stamina, responsibility and fighting spirit. They are vulnerable to many vices and are not well-established in human values, hence they cannot develop the requisite revolutionary character. The vikśubdha shúdras develop into genuine revolutionaries because they acquire the moral courage and discipline to oppose exploitation.
items.statement: Shúdras cannot lead actual revolutions due to insufficient stamina and fighting spirit; revolution against capitalism is spearheaded by disgruntled workers (vikśubdha shúdras).
items.title: Nuclear Revolution

items.qualifiers: Based on Sanskrit etymology (ut - sú + al)
items.quote: “Ut” means “above” and “sava” means “[[to take]] birth”; so utsava means “an occasion which gives human beings fresh inspiration to live a new life.”
items.statement: An utsava (festival) is etymologically defined as an occasion that provides humans fresh inspiration to live an elevated or new life.
items.title: On Festivals

items.qualifiers: Tantric initiation makes Vedic initiation unnecessary
items.quote: So, as long as a person does not get the path of sadhana, he or she should pray to god for one thing or the other. This prayer is called Vedic initiation. The younger ones learn this Vedic initiation from their elders; in other words, [they learn] “Tell me how should I pray to God.” Thereafter, when one gets the grace of God, one receives Tantric initiation. Mantras like iśt́a mantra constitute part of Tantric initiation.
items.statement: Vedic initiation consists of prayer to God, whereas Tantric initiation provides an actionable iśt́a mantra and supersedes the need for prayer.
items.title: On the Savitr Rk

items.quote: Material, then [[abstract]], then astral. And the hub of your astral existence, the nave of your abstract existence, is your soul, or spirit. And your soul, or your spirit, which is the nave of all your subtler existences, is moving or dancing around Parama Puruśa, knowingly or unknowingly, consciously or unconsciously.
items.statement: Human existence is structured across three hierarchical levels—material, abstract, and astral—with the soul as the central nave.
items.title: One Should Know Everything

items.quote: As there are no proper synonyms for ádhibhaotika, ádhidaeviká and ádhyátmika, I am in favour of using the terms “metaphysical”, “metapsychic,” and “metaspiritual,” respectively. I have said that the spatial, temporal and personal obstacles come within the scope of the metaphysical sphere.
items.statement: The triple bondages (trividha klesha) of progress are mapped to metaphysical (ádhibhaotika), metapsychic (ádhidaevika), and metaspiritual (ádhyátmika) spheres.
items.title: One Who Realizes Brahma Becomes Brahma

items.quote: The human body has a particular rhythm; each and every human body has its peculiar rhythm. And that rhythm is a creation of the person’s reactive momenta. So that rhythm separates him from all other objects of this universe. The reactive momenta of two persons are not the same. So the entitative rhythm of a particular man is purely his. And, just now I said, the Iśt́a mantra is to be used as uttarárańi. The Iśt́a mantra has a particular acoustic rhythm. Each and every mantra has its own acoustic rhythm. So the entitative rhythm of the spiritual aspirant must be in constant touch with the incantative rhythm of his Iśt́a mantra.
items.statement: In spiritual practice, the physical body acts as the lower friction wood (arańi) and the Iśt́a mantra acts as the upper wood (uttarárańi) to generate the spiritual fire that destroys mental impurities.
items.title: One Will Have to Know Oneself

items.quote: So it is said, to Nárada, “I transfer my nucleus to the place where my devotees sing my name.” Why? Because in devotees there is upsurge (Ucchavása) and emotion (Ávega). With the help of that emotion, I radiate vibrations in the universe.
items.statement: Parama Puruśa places His nucleus where devotees perform kiirtana because their emotional upsurge allows His divine vibrations to radiate through the universe.
items.title: Opening, Not Closing, the Heart With Kiirtana

items.qualifiers: Requires interial resultant force and congenial environment
items.quote: If the resultant force, the force that comes into being as a result of both external and internal frictions in the object-body, “happens to be interial in character, a nucleus is formed within the solid factor” in some part of that body, and the powers or energies active in that body are collectively called práńáh, or vital energy. In Sanskrit the word práńáh “is always used in the plural number, because it is a collection of ten váyus, or ten important forces working within… the physical structure.”
items.statement: Vital energy (práńáh) is composed of ten internal forces (váyus) originating from the clash between interial and exterial forces in physical structures.
items.title: Our Concept of Creation and Cosmic Mind

items.quote: In our philosophical treatise, Ánanda Sútram, it has been enunciated, Bháva bhávátiitayoh setuh Tárakabrahma – “The common point bridging together the empirical state of Saguńa and the metempirical state of Nirguńa is called Táraka Brahma.”
items.statement: Táraka Brahma is defined as the common tangential point bridging the empirical Saguńa Brahma and the metempirical Nirguńa Brahma.
items.title: Our Concept of Táraka Brahma

items.quote: Usually a philosophical treatise has four main sections – (1) ontology, (2) metaphysics, (3) ethics, (4) epistemology. But in Ananda Marga philosophy two more sections, in addition to the above-mentioned four, have been added. They are (1) psychology and (2) spiritual cult.
items.statement: Ananda Marga philosophy expands traditional philosophy from four branches to six by adding psychology and spiritual cult.
items.title: Our Philosophical Treatise

items.quote: This battle of sádhaná can be carried out in one of three ways – Dakśińácára sádhaná, Vámácára sádhaná or Madhyamácára sádhaná.
items.statement: Spiritual struggle against Máyá follows three approaches: Dakśińácára (flattery), Vámácára (unfocused fight), and Madhyamácára (fighting towards Brahma as the goal).
items.title: Overcoming Máyá

items.quote: When there is all-round progress in the physical, psychic and spiritual strata, it is known as shubha . When there is progress in two strata, it is termed kalyáńam . When there is progress in one stratum it is called kśemam .
items.statement: In Sanskrit, progress across all three strata (physical, psychic, spiritual) is termed shubha, progress across two strata is kalyáńa, and progress in one stratum is kśema.
items.title: Parama Puruśa – the Primordial Cause

items.quote: What is our style of extending goodwill? We say, Namaskár. That is, “I pay respect to the Supreme Entity residing within you.” You should remember this. “I concentrate all the good feelings of my mind here in the trikut́i [between the eyebrows].”
items.statement: Namaskár means paying respect to the Supreme Entity residing within an individual by concentrating one's good thoughts at the trikut́i and sweetness of sentiment at the chest.
items.title: Parama Puruśa within Everyone

items.qualifiers: permanent rescue is beyond human capability
items.quote: Suppose someone is in danger, and you rescue the person for the time being; that is an act of tráńa. But although you have saved the person today, they may be in danger again the next day. Obviously you have not pulled them out of danger permanently. Such an act of bringing someone out of the woods permanently is not an easy task; it is, in fact, beyond the power of human beings. To save someone permanently is called paritráńa. Only Parama Puruśa can bring about the paritráńa of jiivas [living beings], no one else.
items.statement: Tráńa represents temporary rescue from danger that leaves room for future recurrence, whereas paritráńa denotes permanent salvation that only Parama Puruśa can effect.
items.title: “Paritráńáya Sádhúnám”

items.quote: Aesthetic science implies that psychic waves coming in contact with vibrations of greater frequency attain a greater wavelength, and we may say, Anukúlavedaniiyaḿ sukham [“A congenial mental feeling is called happiness”]. If the reverse occurs, we say, Pratikúlavedaniiyaḿ duhkham [“An uncongenial mental feeling is called sorrow”]. In aesthetic science there is no scope for sorrow; and when the vibrations of happiness become straightened, it leads to ánandam; happiness is transformed into bliss.
items.statement: Aesthetic science (nandana vijiṋána) involves psychic waves straightening and expanding into greater wavelengths upon contacting higher frequency vibrations, culminating in bliss (ánandam).
items.title: Párthasárathi Krśńa and Aesthetic Science (Discourse 26)

items.quote: Parama Puruśa remains associated with His creation through ota yoga and prota yoga. He is connected with each individual separately through His ota yoga, and with all collectively through His prota yoga. Vraja Krśńa is more inclined towards ota yoga than prota yoga, while Párthasárathi Krśńa is more inclined towards prota yoga than ota yoga.
items.statement: Vraja Krśńa associates primarily through individual connection (ota yoga), providing individual joy, whereas Párthasárathi Krśńa is more inclined towards collective association (prota yoga), providing collective joy.
items.title: Párthasárathi Krśńa and Aesthetic Science (Discourse 26)

items.quote: One in whom all the aeshvaryas [occult powers] are manifest is called Iishvara. They are chiefly eight in number – ańimá, mahimá, laghimá, prápti, iishitva, vashitva, prakámya and antaryámitva.
items.statement: An entity is termed Iishvara when fully manifesting the eight occult powers (aeshvaryas): ańimá, mahimá, laghimá, prápti, iishitva, vashitva, prakámya, and antaryámitva.
items.title: Párthasárathi Krśńa and Bhaktitattva (Discourse 23)

items.quote: Dvaeta means the existence of two entities – jiiva and Iishvara, the microcosm and the Macrocosm – but it does not explain where the jiivas originally came from. It cannot be logically accepted that the jiivas spring out of nothingness. Thus the final portion of dvaetádvaetaváda is acceptable, but not its beginning. Logically something which does not contain a beginning cannot possess an end.
items.statement: Dvaetádvaetaváda philosophy is logically flawed in its premise because it asserts a duality at the beginning without explaining how unit beings originated, though its conclusion of final non-dual merger is valid.
items.title: Párthasárathi Krśńa and Dvaetádvaetaváda (Discourse 20)

items.quote: Pápa means “to do that which should not be done”. For instance, stealing is pápa, telling lies is pápa. In addition to pápa, there is another word – pratyaváya. Pratyaváya means “not to do what should be done”. For instance, parents should educate their children. If they do not, they are said to have committed pratyaváya.
items.statement: Pápa is committing prohibited negative actions, whereas pratyaváya is failing to perform obligatory positive duties; both constitute branches of sin (pátaka).
items.title: Párthasárathi Krśńa and Dvaetaváda (Discourse 18)

items.quote: Actually the words pápátmá and puńyátmá [soul affected by sin or by virtue] are both incorrect. The soul never commits a sin, it never becomes sinful, nor does it ever become virtuous. It remains deathless and undecaying in its original state. But it does receive an impression.
items.statement: The human soul never itself becomes sinful or virtuous; it merely receives an external reflection or impression, resembling a clear mirror reflecting a red rose.
items.title: Párthasárathi Krśńa and Dvaetaváda (Discourse 18)

items.quote: Krśńa replied, “It is true that Parama Puruśa could do everything by mere wish. He could do everything without creating this world, without this Cosmos. But the drama of the Kurukśetra war was enacted to teach the common people that ultimately dharma always triumphs over adharma [injustice, unrighteousness]. It was meant for popular education. If Parama Puruśa were to accomplish everything by mere thought-projection, that would be hidden from people’s sight, and people would not learn anything from it.
items.statement: The Kurukshetra war was conceived and dramatized rather than resolved through mere mental wish in order to visibly demonstrate to the common masses that dharma ultimately triumphs over adharma.
items.title: Párthasárathi Krśńa and Sáḿkhya Philosophy – 1 (Discourse 8)

items.quote: One may argue that it is sufficient to act morally, but this is not supportable because morality is based on dharma, or imán. Without a strong dharmic base, morality cannot stand. A strong current of selfishness or a flowing river of sin can easily wash away the sandy walls of morality. The only solution is to build the concrete embankment of dharma.
items.statement: Morality is fragile and unstable unless anchored in dharma, because selfish impulses can erode unsupported moral codes.
items.title: Párthasárathi Krśńa and Sáḿkhya Philosophy – 2 (Discourse 9)

items.quote: What is the meaning of vinásha? It means a vishiśt́a [special] form of násha. And násha means change of form from an undeveloped form to a more developed one. In this process something is apparently destroyed, but actually is metamorphosed into something better.
items.statement: Vinásha does not mean absolute annihilation (prańásha), but rather a special transformation wherein an entity's crude or unrighteous form is destroyed to allow for metamorphosis into a better form.
items.title: Párthasárathi Krśńa and Vishiśt́ádvaetaváda (Discourse 16)

items.quote: “The life of every creature is as valuable to itself as one’s own life is valuable to a human being: one who remembers this and shows kindness to all, is termed sádhu.”
items.statement: A true sádhu is defined not by external dress or ascetic marks, but as one who leads an honest life in God-awareness and treats the lives of all creatures as dearly as their own.
items.title: Párthasárathi Krśńa and Vishiśt́ádvaetaváda (Discourse 16)

items.quote: What is upádhi? In Sanskrit, upádhi refers to a special quality, whereas an ordinary quality or title is termed padavii.
items.statement: Padavii refers to a general designation or common quality, whereas upádhi denotes an acquired differentiating functional attribute or title.
items.title: Párthasárathi Krśńa and Vishuddha Advaetaváda– 2 (Discourse 14)

items.quote: In Tantra, the nigama, that is, the collection of Párvatii’s questions, and the ágama, the compilation of Shiva’s answers, have been compared to the two wings of a swan. A bird cannot fly on one wing; similarly, Tantra philosophy, with its nigama and ágama is complete. If one of the aspects is excluded, the inner essence of Tantra is jeopardized.
items.statement: Tantra shástra is composed of two indispensable parts: nigama shástra, representing the spiritual queries posed by Párvatii, and ágama shástra, representing the practical and philosophical solutions given by Shiva.
items.title: Párvatii, Consort of Shiva – Excerpt F

items.quote: Now to create a link between the táńd́ava invented by Shiva and the lalita mármika invented by Párvatii, certain rhythms were invented or discovered. The common term for all these rhythms is tála: the tá of táńd́ava and the la of lalita.
items.statement: The term tála is an acronym formed by combining the initial syllable 'tá' from Shiva's táńd́ava dance and 'la' from Párvatii's lalita mármika dance.
items.title: Párvatii, Consort of Shiva – Excerpt I

items.quote: Shiva is called by three different names at three different levels of sádhaná. When a sádhaka is on the material level, he or she calls Him “Pashupati” when on the mental level, he or she calls Him “Viireshvara”; and when on the spiritual level, he or she calls Him “Mahádeva”.
items.statement: In Tantra, Shiva is addressed under three distinct names corresponding to stages of spiritual development: Pashupati at the material pashvácára stage, Viireshvara at the mental viirácára stage, and Mahádeva at the vibrational/spiritual divyácára stage.
items.title: Pashupati, Viireshvara, and Mahádeva

items.qualifiers: occurs if so desired by Parama Puruśa
items.quote: He explained that actually the eyes, nose, ears, etc., are not the organs. They are only gateways through which different waves enter and activate the mind, and the mind starts seeing, smelling, hearing, etc. If the mind can be activated otherwise, the mind can perceive things even without the help of any organs.
items.statement: Sense organs are merely gateways for waves rather than perceiving entities; perception can take place without bodily organs if the mind is directly activated.
items.title: Perception

items.qualifiers: required on the eve of final merger if not accepted earlier
items.quote: But in order to attain the goal of salvation, of final emancipation, one will have to accept Neohumanism [if not at the first step, then] as the final course of action; one will have to establish oneself in Neohumanism just on the eve of one’s final merger with Parama Puruśa – maybe for a few moments only; otherwise it is impossible for one to establish oneself in perfect spirituality and attain Parama Puruśa. Neohumanism is the last word for attaining Him.
items.statement: Accepting Neohumanism at least just prior to the final merger with Parama Puruśa is mandatory for establishing oneself in perfect spirituality and attaining salvation.
items.title: Perfect Spirituality and Neohumanism

items.quote: While doing sadhana, while doing your meditation, you should always think, remember, that whatever you are doing, He is seeing. That is, you are the object, He is the subject. He sees whatever you do. He sees whatever you think.
items.statement: During spiritual meditation, the practitioner should not look upon Parama Puruśa as an object, but should ideate that Parama Puruśa is the supreme observing Subject and the practitioner is His object.
items.title: Permanent Shelter

items.quote: A language normally lasts about one thousand years and a script about two thousand years before undergoing metamorphosis. Script, however, is not sound. It is alphabetical order. The Bengali script came into existence approximately fifteen hundred years ago and it will survive for some time longer.
items.statement: Languages and scripts have regular life cycles, with a spoken language normally enduring approximately 1,000 years and a script about 2,000 years before undergoing metamorphosis.
items.title: Phonetics – 1 (Discourse 1)

items.quote: Thus these four letters – ya, ra, la and va – are antahsthavarńa rather than pure consonants. Why? Because in fact they are each a diphthong of two vowels. Specifically, ya = i + a, ra = r + a, la = lr + a, and va = o + a. They are mistakenly taken to be consonants but they are actually not consonants.
items.statement: The letters ya, ra, la, and va are categorized as antahsthavarńa rather than pure consonants because each is functionally a diphthong composed of two vowels (i+a, r+a, lr+a, and o+a).
items.title: Phonetics – 2 (Discourse 2)

items.qualifiers: prashna is a noted exception accepted by grammarians
items.quote: In phonetics there is a hard and fast rule that members from the three different groups of letters cannot combine together to form diphthongs. For example, in the word nishcala, ca is a palatal letter, thus it must have sha as its conjunct, not śa or sa. Similarly, caiṋcala combines ina + ca, not n + ca. Kaśt́a cannot be spelled kast́a.
items.statement: Phonetics prohibits letters from different phonetic classes (palatal, cerebral, dental) from combining into conjuncts, requiring conjunct letters to conform to the class of their partner.
items.title: Phonetics – 3 (Discourse 3)

items.quote: Silik in Arabic means “fine fibre”. The fine fibres that came to Bengal from China were given the Sanskrit name ciináḿshuka. This ciináḿshuká was given the Farsi name resham and the Arabic name silik. Arab merchants used to export this ciináḿshuka to the markets of Europe. When they were heard saying the Arabic word in Europe, ciináḿshuka became “silk” with the help of a little faulty pronunciation.
items.statement: The English word 'silk' originated from the Sanskrit term 'ciináḿshuka', which was transmitted by Arab traders using the Arabic term 'silik' (meaning fine fibre).
items.title: Phonetics, Prefixes and Suffixes (Discourse 5)

items.quote: This human body is a composite of protoplasmic cells, and these protoplasmic cells are made of the food we take in. If the food and drink is defective, then the protoplasmic cells will also become defective, and the human mind, which is the collective mind of so many protoplasmic minds, will also become defective. That is why támasik or static food has a negative influence on the human mind.
items.statement: Static (támasik) food degrades the human mind because protoplasmic cells are directly formed from ingested food, making the composite protoplasmic mind defective.
items.title: Physical Propulsion, Psychic Propensities and Spiritual Attainment

items.quote: Sevá means rendering selfless service to the universe, not to a particular group of people but to anybody and everybody, to all living creatures – animals, plants or human beings. Service is unilateral, not mutual. Where it is mutual, it is not service – it is commercial transaction.
items.statement: Genuine service (sevá) is strictly unilateral with no expectation of return, whereas mutual transactions constitute commercial activities rather than spiritual service.
items.title: Physical Propulsion, Psychic Propensities and Spiritual Attainment

items.qualifiers: permitted only for special reasons with approval from the Ácárya Board
items.quote: But at the same time, attempts at birth control by physical damage to men or women, or by permanent destruction of their procreative capacity, can never be supported, because such attempts may bring about a severe mental reaction in them at any time. But if one has to accept permanent birth control for some special reason, then permission should be requested from the ácárya. The ácárya in such cases will ascertain the views of the Ácárya Board and then guide the person.
items.statement: Surgical or permanent sterilization as a method of birth control is disapproved due to severe psychological risks; exceptions require formal permission from an ácárya and the Ácárya Board.
items.title: Physical Restraint

items.qualifiers: six seeds and flowers on the 6th day, eight on the 8th day
items.quote: On the Ashokaśaśt́hii day every menstruating woman should take in one gulp six mung or máskalái seeds along with six ashoka flowers or buds. They should be taken either in a ripe banana or with water or milk. Similarly, on the Ashokaśt́amii day, eight mung or máskalái seeds and eight ashoka flowers or buds should be taken.
items.statement: During the Ashokaśaśt́hii and Ashokaśt́amii observances, menstruating women are prescribed to ingest mung or máskalái seeds together with ashoka flower buds.
items.title: Physical Well-Being – Excerpt A

items.quote: In rágánugá bhakti, the idea is that you love Him because by doing so you derive pleasure. Greater devotees don’t even like this. They love God, not because they get pleasure, but because He gets pleasure. To give him pleasure is what they want. “I don’t even want pleasure for myself. I want to please you; therefore I love you.” This alone is the supreme devotion. This is known as “rágátmiká bhakti”.
items.statement: Rágánugá bhakti involves loving God because it gives oneself pleasure, whereas rágátmiká bhakti represents supreme devotion where one loves exclusively to give pleasure to the Supreme Lord.
items.title: Pleasing the Lord

items.quote: The fifty main propensities of the human mind are expressed internally or externally through the vibrational expression of these cakras. These vibrations cause hormones to be secreted from the glands, and the natural or unnatural expression of the propensities depends on the degree of normal or abnormal secretion of the hormones.
items.statement: Cakras are intersections of subtle nerve channels whose vibrational expressions regulate the secretion of hormones from physical glands and sub-glands, thereby controlling mental propensities.
items.title: Plexi and Microvita

items.quote: Not only is the light reflected or refracted here, but also microvita, moving along the light rays, affect the body and the twelve sub-glands of this cakra. Positive and negative microvita move along these media. What are the media of microvita for their movement, for their status, for their location, as their abode? Tanmátras – inferences and ideas.
items.statement: Microvita traverse inferences (tanmátras) and light rays to interact directly with the glands and sub-glands of human cakras.
items.title: Plexi and Microvita

items.quote: Bhagavat Dharma has four aspects – vistára or expansion, rasa or flow, sevá or service and tadsthiti or attainment of the supreme stance. The fundamental aim of Bhagavat Dharma is vistára – that is, psychic expansion.
items.statement: Bhágavata Dharma (human dharma) comprises four specific pillars: vistára (psychic expansion), rasa (flow with the cosmic rhythm), sevá (selfless service), and tadsthiti (merger into the Supreme Stance).
items.title: Plants, Animals and Human Beings

items.quote: The plain philosophic meaning of “guńa” is a binding string – a string used to bind some objects. Here, “guńa” connotes the Cosmic Force whereby the Universal Consciousness is bound to various shapes or ideas.
items.statement: Guńa in its philosophical sense does not mean quality, but rather signifies a binding string or Cosmic Force whereby Universal Consciousness is bound to various shapes or ideas.
items.title: Prakrti Tattva and Oṋḿkára Tattva

items.quote: When the mind goes from subtleness to crudeness and gets engrossed in material objects, the process is termed mental detraction or saiṋcara kriyá. When the mind passes from material objects to subtleness it merges into the Cosmic “I” feeling and the process is termed mental attraction or pratisaiṋcara. Saiṋcara is principally guided by tamoguńa and pratisaiṋcara by sattvguńa.
items.statement: Saiṋcara is guided by tamoguńa and moves the mind from subtleness to crudeness, whereas pratisaiṋcara is guided by sattvaguńa and moves the mind from material objects to subtleness and Cosmic 'I' feeling.
items.title: Prakrti Tattva and Oṋḿkára Tattva

items.qualifiers: based on vibrational frequency and guńas
items.quote: This variation in vibration is responsible for the generation of white colour by sattvaguńa, red colour by rajoguńa and dark colour by tamoguńa. The greater the degree of crudeness, the lesser is the force of vibration. It is for this reason that tamoguńa is coloured black. Black is no colour. In fact, the perception of black colour is due to the absence of all colours. White, on the other hand, is the combination of all colours.
items.statement: The perception of the color black is due to the absence of all colors and lower vibrational force, whereas white is the combination of all colors expressing the fullest enlightenment of sattvaguńa.
items.title: Prakrti Tattva and Oṋḿkára Tattva

items.quote: The meaning of the root verb má is “to measure”, “to fathom”. So the etymological meaning of pramá is “balance”. In English the two words “equilibrium” and “equipoise” are used in this sense, but there is some practical difference between these two words. “Equilibrium” is used in the sense of balance in physical strength and “equipoise” is used in the sense of balance in weight.
items.statement: Pramá is etymologically defined as balance, encompassing both equilibrium (balance in physical strength) and equipoise (balance in weight).
items.title: Pramá – 1 / Dynamic Equilibrium and Equipoise

items.qualifiers: in analysis of historical Buddhist philosophy
items.quote: As these teachings do not include Saḿvrti (material acquisition) they lack charm and do not give a good reason for living. This explains perhaps why Buddha never considered the idea of forming a society or outlining a system of social ceremonies such as child-naming, marriage, etc. Nor did he attempt to bring balance to economic activities or harmonize the norms of social obligations.
items.statement: Buddha's philosophy and spiritual path over-emphasized abnegation (Nivrtti) without incorporating material acquisition and social adjustment (Saḿvrtti), leading to an absence of social ceremonies, economic balance, and full social equilibrium.
items.title: Pramá – 3

items.quote: For spiritual practice you are to create a spiritual urge. Therefore you are to create a proper system of education. Education should be imparted in a spiritual and psychic style. When they get proper education, a proper spiritual urge is created and then they will start Sádhaná. So we must start primary schools throughout the entire world to create a spiritual urge amongst the little pupils. I am not in favour of starting colleges; I am in favour of starting primary schools.
items.statement: To create a genuine spiritual urge globally, emphasis must be placed on opening thousands of kindergarten and primary schools with a spiritual-psychic curriculum rather than opening colleges and high schools.
items.title: Pramá – 4

items.quote: Some microvita are, in effect, your friends and some are your enemies. By nature, no microvitum is either a friend or enemy of human beings.
items.statement: No microvitum is inherently a friend or enemy to human beings by nature; rather, inimical microvita can become friends if controlled by good people.
items.title: Pramá – 4

items.quote: Internal discipline in the psychic sphere of individual life is what we may call the Práńa Dharma of individual life. When the national characteristics are expressed in a particular vein, we may call it the Práńa Dharma of the nation.
items.statement: Práńa Dharma is the distinctive internal psychic discipline of an individual life, which expands into national Práńa Dharma when expressed as common national characteristics and life outlook.
items.title: Práńa Dharma

items.quote: The root verb “gam” + suffix “kvip” = “jagat”. The suffix “kvip” is added in Saḿskrta to denote the wont of an object. Here the root verb “gam” means “to go”, and “kvip” denotes “wont”, so “gam” + “kvip”, equalling “jagat”, means an article whose wont, that is whose characteristics, whose properties, are to move.
items.statement: The term 'jagat' is derived from the root verb 'gam' and suffix 'kvip', denoting an entity whose inherent characteristic or wont is to move.
items.title: Prańáma Mantra

items.quote: Shásanát tárayet yastu sah shástrah parikiirtitah – “That which helps the sádhaka in attaining that supreme stance of salvation by prescribing the code of discipline and the code of spiritual cult is called shástra.”
items.statement: Shástra is defined as that which liberates a spiritual aspirant and helps achieve supreme salvation by prescribing a code of spiritual discipline and cult.
items.title: Prańava

items.quote: This sound is caused by the process of thinking of the Creator when He thinks of creation. The entire universe is within His mind. Every action produces a particular sound. The average of all sounds produced within Him, is this sound: the sound caused by the creation of a thing, the sound due to the existence of a thing, and the sound due to the destruction of a thing – as everything is happening only within Him.
items.statement: The prańava dhvani, or sound of silence, is generated by the average of all vibrational sounds of creation, existence, and destruction produced within the Creator's mind.
items.title: Prańava Dhvani

items.quote: The process by which the práńas in the body are controlled is called práńáyáma. Práńa, apána, samána, udána, vyána, nága, kúrma, krkara, devadatta, and dhanaiṋjaya – the collective name of these ten vital forces is práńáh.
items.statement: Práńáyáma is the process of controlling the práńáh, which is the collective name for the ten vital forces operating in the human body.
items.title: Práńáyáma

items.quote: The practice of shiitalii or siitkári kumbhaka is forbidden for a period of one hour before and after the practice of práńáyáma connected with sádhaná. As far as possible it is not advisable to practise more than one type of práńáyáma.
items.statement: Special práńáyámas such as shiitalii or siitkárii kumbhaka must not be practised within one hour before or after the practice of práńáyáma connected with sádhaná.
items.title: Práńáyáma

items.quote: All the vrttis [propensities] of the human mind (fifty primary ones, and one thousand secondary) are dependent for their activities on the capacity of the body. The arms and legs should do work; all parts of the body should be utilized properly; you should get work out of them, hard work – this is a must. Else hormone secretion from the glands and sub-glands will be hampered. And the over-activity and under-activity of the propensities are caused by the hormone secretion.
items.statement: Physical activity and karma yoga are necessary because proper bodily exercise regulates hormone secretions from the glands and sub-glands, which directly govern mental propensities (vrttis).
items.title: “Prańipátena Pariprashnena Sevayá” – 2

items.qualifiers: geographical and spiritual divisions of Tantra
items.quote: From the viewpoint of geography, Tantra has two main divisions – one is the Bengal school of Tantra, the other is the Kashmir school of Tantra. The Bengal school is less ritualistic and more practical, while the Kashmir school is more ritualistic and less practical. And from the viewpoint of spiritual practice, Tantra has five main divisions: Shaeva Tantra, Shákta Tantra, Vaeśńava Tantra, Saora Tantra, and Gáńapatya Tantra.
items.statement: Geographically Tantra is divided into the practical Bengal school and the ritualistic Kashmir school, while spiritually it comprises five schools: Shaeva, Shákta, Vaeśńava, Saora, and Gáńapatya Tantra.
items.title: Prapatti, Viprapatti, and Aprapatti (Discourse 6)

items.quote: Whatever people learn from the external world – be it from a book of facts or a learned discourse, or any source of knowledge – is “prápta vákya” or “relative knowledge”. It is sometimes correct, sometimes incorrect. When human beings, through psycho-spiritual practice, make their minds as expansive as the Comic Mind, they can receive instructions or directions directly from Him due to His proximity. The knowledge thus acquired is called “ápta vákya” or “absolute knowledge”.
items.statement: Prápta vákya represents relative knowledge acquired from the external world through perception, inference, or scripture, whereas ápta vákya represents absolute knowledge received directly from the Cosmic Mind through psycho-spiritual practice.
items.title: Prápta Vákya and Ápta Vákya

items.quote: The difference between dhyána [meditation] and dhárańá [concentration] is that dhyána is something stationary; that is, the object is a stationary one in the case of dhyána. In the case of dhárańá, the mind moves along with the object; that is, there is a dynamic force behind dhárańá. And dhyána, although sentient, has no movement in it.
items.statement: In dhyána (meditation) the ideational object is stationary and without movement, whereas in dhárańá (concentration) the mind moves along with the object, carrying a dynamic force.
items.title: Pratyáhára Yoga and Paramágati

items.quote: If the propensities are withdrawn, but not goaded towards the citta, then there will be a dangerous reaction. I think you have understood. That is why it has been said, Yacched váun manasi prájiṋah – “What are intelligent spiritual aspirants to do? They are to goad their mental propensities to the citta.”
items.statement: When withdrawing mental propensities from the external world in pratyáhára, the propensities must be actively directed inwards to the citta, then the citta to ahaḿtattva, ahaḿtattva to mahattattva, and mahattattva to the Cognitive Principle to avoid dangerous subconscious disturbances.
items.title: Pratyáhára Yoga and Paramágati

items.quote: For a perfectly balanced economic environment, it is required that some thirty to forty percent of the people should depend directly on agriculture, and about twenty percent on agro-industries, twenty percent on agrico-industries, ten percent on general trade and commerce, and ten percent on intellectual or white collar jobs.
items.statement: A balanced economic structure requires roughly 30 to 40% of the population dependent on agriculture, 20% on agro-industries, 20% on agrico-industries, 10% on general trade and commerce, and 10% on intellectual or white-collar occupations.
items.title: Principles of Balanced Economy – Excerpt A

items.qualifiers: for national development and socio-economic elevation
items.quote: Remember that no country should depend on imported raw materials for development. Indigenous raw materials, that is, materials available within the country itself, must be used for this purpose.
items.statement: An industrial revolution should rely entirely on indigenous raw materials available within one's own socio-economic unit rather than imported foreign resources.
items.title: Principles of Balanced Economy – Excerpt B

items.qualifiers: collective atrocities cannot be pardoned by individual representatives
items.quote: So it has to be said that pardoning is a practice for individual life only, not for collective life.
items.statement: Pardoning cannot be applied in collective life when an entire human group is oppressed, even if an individual may choose to pardon a personal oppressor.
items.title: Problems of the Day

items.qualifiers: divergent national interests are minor compared to leaders' apprehension
items.quote: The main obstacle is the apprehension of local leaders that they will lose their leadership. With the establishment of a world government, the total domination which they exercise today in their respective countries, societies and nations will cease to exist.
items.statement: The primary barrier to establishing a world government is local leaders' fear of losing their unquestioned regional authority.
items.title: Problems of the Day

items.qualifiers: rejects both landlord ownership and strict worker-exclusive ownership slogans
items.quote: The people in general are the real owners of all the wealth in this world, and that is why I have used the term “socialization”.
items.statement: Socialization is distinct from nationalization because true ownership of wealth belongs to the collectivity of people rather than strictly to the state or specific workers.
items.title: Problems of the Day

items.qualifiers: within the systaltic movement of the social cycle
items.quote: Evolution which takes place as a result of this forward galloping jump is properly called viplava [revolution].
items.statement: Revolution is evolution caused by a forward galloping leap resulting from forceful contraction, while counter-evolution and counter-revolution are backward regressions.
items.title: Problems of the Day

items.qualifiers: associated with the secretion of digestive fluids
items.quote: It is good to take food when the main flow of breath is through the right nostril. Even after meal, it is good if the flow of breath is mainly through the right nostril and continues for some time, because that is the time when the digestive glands start secreting a sufficient quantity of fluids to help digestion.
items.statement: For optimal digestion, food should be consumed when the breath flows predominantly through the right nostril.
items.title: Procedure for Eating

items.quote: (For proper digestion, fill the stomach halfway with food, one quarter with water, and leave one quarter full of air.)
items.statement: Proper stomach proportioning for digestion requires half food, one quarter water, and one quarter air.
items.title: Procedure for Eating

items.qualifiers: when fasting is performed according to the system
items.quote: If one fasts according to the system, no excess shukra will excite the lower vrttis of the mind, and the mind will be led toward the higher vrttis.
items.statement: Fasting prevents excess shukra from stimulating lower mental propensities and directs the mind toward higher mental propensities.
items.title: Procedure for Fasting

items.qualifiers: on and around times of new and full moon
items.quote: On and around the times of new and full moon, one may observe that the gaseous and aqueous factors in the body rise up into the head and chest, creating an uncomfortable feeling. Therefore, if a person does not take food at these times, these factors will be drawn down from the higher portions of the body to the lower portions, thereby alleviating the uncomfortable feeling.
items.statement: Fasting on new and full moon days counteracts the upward surge of gaseous and aqueous factors into the head and chest.
items.title: Procedure for Fasting

items.qualifiers: applies exclusively to the Macrocosm / Parama Purusha
items.quote: The movement of the propensities in Pravrtti is always extroversial, and as there is nothing outside Macrocosm, there cannot be any extroversial movement at all – the movement is always introversial, every movement is within the Macrocosmic arena.
items.statement: The Macrocosm possesses only introversial propensities because there is no external realm outside the Macrocosmic structure.
items.title: Propensities and Pramá

items.qualifiers: maintains the triangle of forces undisturbed in its final stage
items.quote: Pramá is psychic equilibrium – equilibrium in the arena of psychic faculty, and equipoise in the arena of psychic mass.
items.statement: Prama is psychic equilibrium in the arena of psychic faculty and psychic equipoise in the arena of psychic mass.
items.title: Propensities and Pramá

items.qualifiers: strictly masculine gender in Sanskrit etymology
items.quote: Its creator is addressed as “Savitá”. “Savitá” means “Progenitor”. Some people wrongly name their daughters “Savitá”. The name of a girl should not be “Savitá”. “Savitá” means “father”, (masculine gender).
items.statement: The Vedic name Savita denotes the masculine Progenitor or creator of the seven strata of the universe.
items.title: Proper Intellect

items.qualifiers: universal to human linguistic and physical movement
items.quote: Human beings try to find rhythm in everything because human life itself is rhythmic. Movement is the natural characteristic of life so rhythm must exist within human movement. If life’s movement were continuous or linear then there would be no scope for rhythm, and without rhythm there can be no happiness either.
items.statement: Human beings create rhyming and repetitive words in language because life itself moves systaltically and seeks rhythm.
items.title: Proper Names – 1 (Discourse 16)

items.quote: Approximately seven hundred or seven hundred and fifty years ago a terrible ocean storm caused great swells in the waters of the Bay of Bengal. Due to these swells, the water of the Bay of Bengal inundated one hundred and fifty miles inland. All of the settlements in that hundred and fifty miles were wiped out in the blink of an eye.
items.statement: Seven to eight centuries ago an ocean surge inundated 150 miles of southern Bengal, wiping out settlements and transforming the area into a saline jungle subsequently repopulated from western Rarh.
items.title: Proper Names – 1 (Discourse 16)

items.qualifiers: evolved via phonetic displacement of initial 'n'
items.quote: The old Sanskrit for “orange” is nágarauṋga. From this comes the word náráuṋgii even though the orange is a Mediterranean fruit; that is, it is native to Europe. Nevertheless the English word “orange” is neither originally English nor European. Its origin is this Urdu word náráuṋgii.
items.statement: The English word orange derives from the Urdu narangi, which originated from the Sanskrit nagaraunga.
items.title: Proper Names – 2 (Discourse 17)

items.qualifiers: relative to the base of the living entity (jiiva)
items.quote: A person may have immense capacity, but to the extent that he or she does not utilize it, it does not become helpful in God-realization. Bala, therefore, depends on the extent of the use of one’s capacity.
items.statement: Bala or spiritual strength is defined by the degree to which an individual actually utilizes their available capacity, regardless of how small or great that inherent capacity is.
items.title: Properly Utilize Yourself to Reach God

items.qualifiers: minority causes persist if rooted in bad education or mean propensities
items.quote: If India is to be freed from this sin, the vaeshya social system must be terminated because eighty percent of the cause is economic injustice. Of course, where people indulge in prostitution due to bad education or mean propensities, it will continue even after economic injustice is rooted out.
items.statement: Prostitution cannot be eradicated through legislative prohibitions alone because eighty percent of its root cause is economic injustice generated by the vaeshya social system.
items.title: Prostitution – Excerpt A

items.qualifiers: balance among all three is mandatory to cross the spiritual threshold
items.quote: PROUT is the socioeconomic approach, Neohumanism is the psycho-intellectual approach and spiritual practice is the spirituo-intuitional approach. This three-fold approach will take human beings along the path of salvation.
items.statement: PROUT serves as the socioeconomic approach, Neohumanism as the psycho-intellectual approach, and spiritual practice as the spirituo-intuitional approach leading to salvation.
items.title: Prout and Neohumanism

items.qualifiers: applies equally to plants, animals, and non-useful creatures
items.quote: Rather it will be a great loss for human society, because each and every living entity, whether plant or animal, has two types of value: one, its utility value, and the other, its existential value.
items.statement: Every living entity possesses both utility value and existential value, and the right to exist is not contingent upon providing utility to human beings.
items.title: Pseudo-Humanism (Discourse 8)

items.quote: “Yes, what my opponents [revolutionaries] say is correct; but if this really materializes, it will greatly inconvenience me and disturb my individual sentiment. So what we must do is to try to adjust with the existing situation. We don’t want any great changes; we will just go ahead step by step. Externally we may speak of reform, but in our heart of hearts, we have decided not to allow any change to take place.” This is pseudo-reformist strategy.
items.statement: Pseudo-reformist strategy outwardly adopts gradual reform while internally preventing significant structural change.
items.title: Pseudo-Humanism (Discourse 8)

items.qualifiers: encompasses expressions of all living beings, including flora and fauna
items.quote: So perfect spirituality is our goal, and Neohumanism is our approach. What is Neohumanism? The collection of all natural human expressions, the collection of all natural expressions of all flora and fauna, is Neohumanism. All these movements of human sentiment and all these movements of flora and fauna are towards perfect spirituality. So that perfect spirituality cannot be the cult – it is the goal, it is the desideratum, it is the culminating point of all movements.
items.statement: Perfect spirituality serves as the goal or desideratum of existence, while Neohumanism constitutes the dynamic cult and practical approach.
items.title: Pseudo-Spirituality and Neohumanism

items.qualifiers: requires transcending both attraction and repulsion
items.quote: In fact samádhi is neither a positive nor a negative state of mind. Samádhi is a sate of equilibrium.
items.statement: Samadhi is a state of psychic equilibrium that transcends both the path of attachment (pravrtti) and the path of repulsion (nivrtti).
items.title: Psychic Assimilation in Psycho-Spiritual Practice

items.qualifiers: bound by temporal, spatial, and personal relative factors
items.quote: What is karma? Karma implies the change of place of an object. And what is place? Place is one of the three rudimental relative factors – time, place and person. Where there is karma, there are temporal, spatial and personal factors.
items.statement: Karma is defined as the change of place of an object within the relative factors of time, place, and person.
items.title: Psychic Development and Karma

items.qualifiers: fundamental to all languages and musical sound scales
items.quote: First a vibration arises in the nerves when an object is seen, then a mental sound is created and finally a word is made based on that sound. In this way the original verbal roots of language are created based on psychic sounds, and different words have been created, and are being created, from these verbal roots.
items.statement: Language and acoustic roots originate from nerve vibrations created by mental impressions when objects are perceived.
items.title: Psycho-Acoustic and Inferential Acoustic Notes (Discourse 9)

items.qualifiers: excludes mere materialistic or political principles
items.quote: This psycho-spiritual parallelism is known as “idea”, or bháva. When this bháva or idea is conceived on the psychic level, it is “ideology”. Ideology, therefore, is the conception of idea and nothing else.
items.statement: Ideology is the psychic conception of psycho-spiritual parallelism, which represents the alignment of psychic waves with the spiritual waves of the atman.
items.title: Psycho-Spiritual Parallelism

items.qualifiers: achieved through bhava sadhana during activity
items.quote: This is what Ananda Marga philosophy means by Brahmacarya. Brahmacarya does not mean celibacy but means the assimilation of the psychic wave of the unit mind into the eternal waves of the Macrocosm.
items.statement: Brahmacarya is the assimilation of unit mental psychic waves into the eternal waves of the Macrocosm, rather than mere physical celibacy.
items.title: Psycho-Spiritual Parallelism

items.qualifiers: relative to the individual's degree of virtue versus vice
items.quote: A man whose company will deteriorate or deprave the standard of others is a durjana for those persons. Suppose you have fifteen degrees of virtue and another man has vice of twenty degrees. What will be the resultant balance? The resultant balance will be five in favour of vice. You will acquire five degrees of vice. So that man having twenty degrees of vice is a durjana for you.
items.statement: A durjana is a relative designation referring to anyone whose negative moral degree exceeds one's own positive moral degree, causing moral deterioration upon contact.
items.title: Puńya All Twenty-Four Hours

items.qualifiers: requires proper initial practice and adjustment to respiration
items.quote: Now this japa is adjusted to your breathing, inhalation and exhalation. So if you practise it properly what will happen? Even while sleeping, automatically this japa kriyá will go on in accordance with your respiration – in accordance with your inhalation and exhalation. So while asleep you can do this thing. This is called ajapájapa .
items.statement: Ajapajapa enables an individual to accumulate spiritual merit continuously through sleep by synchronizing internal mantra ideation with respiration.
items.title: Puńya All Twenty-Four Hours

items.qualifiers: tribal populations and southern regions without Pathan rule remained free of it
items.quote: The purdah was not in use among the ancient Aryans. It was originally a Semitic concept. Indian women did not use the purdah before the Pathan rule.
items.statement: The custom of purdah and head veiling was not present among ancient Aryans in India and was introduced during Pathan rule.
items.title: Purdah – Excerpt A

items.qualifiers: though infinite, Prakrti's infinitude is conditioned by Purusa
items.quote: In the same way, Prakrti is constantly undergoing depletion. Why? Because due to the constant ideation of Puruśa, She is gradually merging in Puruśa. As Prakrti is infinite, although She undergoes this constant depletion, She is never totally exhausted. And when She merges into Puruśa, She becomes transformed into Puruśa. Thus Brahma is one without any second.
items.statement: Prakrti undergoes continuous depletion and merges into Purusa through His constant ideation, ensuring that Brahma remains non-dual.
items.title: Puruśa

items.quote: “Parama Puruśa is infinite and omnipresent; therefore His hands and feet are spread in all directions. As this entire creation is His mental projection, it has no absolute existence to Him. He does not require any physical hands or feet; even without them He can get any work done or go anywhere He likes, through mental imagination.”
items.statement: Creation lacks absolute existence for Parama Purusa because it is entirely His mental projection.
items.title: Puruśatattva

items.quote: A developed economy should consist of four parts – people’s economy, psycho-economy, commercial economy and general economy. This quadri-dimension of the economy is a vast expansion on the contemporary and co-contemporary conceptions of economic activity.
items.statement: A developed economy encompasses four distinct branches: people's economy, psycho-economy, commercial economy, and general economy.
items.title: Quadri-Dimensional Economy

items.quote: The minimum requirements can be assured through guaranteed purchasing capacity which should be enshrined in the constitution as a fundamental or cardinal human right. This will give the citizens of the country legal power if their minimum requirements are not met, hence the necessity of purchasing capacity will be reinforced by constitutional law.
items.statement: Minimum human requirements should be legally guaranteed by establishing purchasing capacity as a cardinal constitutional right.
items.title: Quadri-Dimensional Economy

items.quote: The dharma of the mind is to seek the infinite. The mind attains this goal by concentrating on a particular idea. As material objects are finite, those who seek to attain the infinite through material objects will eventually feel frustrated. They fail to attain bliss because no one can obtain or enjoy any wealth or material objects or objects of enjoyment in a way that will infinitely quench his or her thirst. Moreover, if those who try to satisfy their infinite hunger with material objects take this too far, their personal interests will come in conflict with those of other people, because in such a situation they try to accumulate excess wealth or material objects or objects of enjoyment by depriving others of the same objects, which are extremely necessary for the preservation of their existence.
items.statement: Seeking bliss through material objects causes psychological frustration and social conflict because finite matter cannot satisfy an infinite hunger.
items.title: Questions and Answers on Society – 1

items.quote: PROUT suggests that increases in per capita income are not a sufficiently reliable and scientific index to determine the standard and progress of a particular socio-economic unit. Rather, this approach is misleading and deceitful, because it refers to a simple mathematical calculation of total national income divided by total population. This does not give the correct picture of the standard of living of the people of a particular socio-economic unit, as the wealth disparity in society is concealed. Per capita income shows the mean and not the variation of income distribution.
items.statement: Per capita income is a misleading mathematical average that conceals wealth disparity, whereas purchasing capacity accurately reflects economic living standards.
items.title: Questions and Answers [on Society] – 2

items.quote: Agrico-industries represent a set of pre-harvesting industries. Agrico-industries directly or indirectly promote the rapid qualitative and quantitative growth of agricultural products. Agro-industries comprise those post-harvesting industries which depend on agricultural production.
items.statement: Agrico-industries are pre-harvesting enterprises that promote agricultural growth, whereas agro-industries are post-harvesting enterprises dependent on crop yields.
items.title: Questions and Answers [on Society] – 2

items.quote: According to PROUT, agriculture should be given the status of industry. In industry raw material costs, labour costs, interest on loans, depreciation, maintenance costs, profit, the rate of outturn, etc. are fixed and included in costing. In agriculture this has not been done, so produce is usually priced uneconomically. Farmers are forced to sell their produce at low prices due to the pressure of circumstances. (This is known as a “distress sale”.) If agriculture is treated as an industry, all the conditions of industry should apply to agriculture.
items.statement: Agriculture must be accorded the structural status of an industry to ensure comprehensive production costing and eliminate distress sales.
items.title: Questions and Answers [on Society] – 3

items.quote: In the cooperative system there should not be any scope for interest earning shares; that is, there should not be profit earning shares in cooperatives. Rather shares should be according to the production of the land. If there are profit earning shares in farmers or agricultural cooperatives, then these shares will be sold in the share market, capitalists will buy the shares, the rate of share prices will fluctuate according to share market prices, and cooperatives will become commercial enterprises.
items.statement: Cooperatives must issue only dividend-earning shares based on net profits rather than profit-earning or preferential fixed-interest shares to prevent capitalist commercialization.
items.title: Questions and Answers [on Society] – 4

items.quote: Due to the preponderance of Consciousness in Puruśottama He is sometimes considered as Nirguńa. However, upon closer observation, it is discovered that this conclusion is incorrect because, unlike the expressed universe, Puruśottama is neither “guńádhiina” (under the bondage of the guńas) nor “guńasrśt́a” (created by the guńas). However, due to His witnessing relationship with the guńadhiina universe, He maintains a contact with the guńas, and thus we call Him “guńadaniish” (beyond the periphery of the guńas). Therefore Puruśottama cannot be pure, unexpressed Nirguńa Brahma because in Nirguńa Brahma there is no witness-ship and therefore no association with the guńas.
items.statement: Unlike the gunadhiina universe, Purusottama is associated with the gunas as their witness without being bound by or created from them.
items.title: Questions and Answers on Ananda Marga Philosophy

items.quote: We may conclude that the mind enjoys the shadow of an object, and that this creation of the five fundamental factors is itself a shadow of the Cosmic Mind. Thus, from the viewpoint of the Cosmic Mind, whatever the unit mind enjoys is neither the original object itself, nor a shadow of the object, but rather a shadow of the shadow of the object.
items.statement: The unit mind experiences only tanmatras rather than objects directly, making its perception a shadow of the Cosmic Mind's mental creation.
items.title: Questions and Answers on Ananda Marga Philosophy

items.quote: When, due to extreme fear, stupefaction, crudity, or an excessive expression of any ripu or pásha, the kámamaya becomes temporarily suspended in the next higher kośa and the imagined objects appear real. This is also the case when a person sees various gods and goddesses. Psychologically, seeing a ghost, god or goddess is the same thing; none of them actually exist.
items.statement: Apparitions and possessions are mental ectoplasmic projections and self-hypnotic trances where lower mental sheaths become suspended.
items.title: Questions and Answers on Ananda Marga Philosophy

items.quote: The third definition is: Saḿyogo yogo ityukto jiivátmá Paramátmánah – “When the unit consciousness and the Supreme Consciousness are fused into one, that is real yoga.” This takes place when the spiritual aspirant establishes a relationship of sweet love with Parama Puruśa [Supreme Consciousness].
items.statement: True yoga is the sweet, loving union and fusion of the unit consciousness with the Supreme Consciousness.
items.title: Questions and Answers on Meditation

items.quote: No, because it increases the production of semen from lymph, and consequently the brain will not get sufficient lymph as food to practise sádhaná properly. Intoxicating liquor will affect the semen and lymph, which in turn will affect all the other glands. The entire nervous system will get agitated, and as a result mental concentration will be lost and sádhaná will be impaired.
items.statement: Intoxicating liquor disrupts spiritual meditation by over-converting lymph to semen and depriving the brain of essential nourishment.
items.title: Questions and Answers on Meditation

items.quote: Supra-psychic means where the psychic comes in continuous touch, continuous contact, with the spiritual – the silver lining between the spiritual and psychic. The spiritual level, the spiritual space, is not for microvita because they are something created by the cosmic mind. Some microvita occupy the subtlest layer of the physical sphere, and some are subtler than that: they are psychic. And some are still higher, they are supra-psychic.
items.statement: Microvita operate within ethereal, psychic, and supra-psychic strata, but cannot function in the pure spiritual stratum.
items.title: Questions and Answers on Microvita – Excerpt A

items.quote: Positive microvitum is pro-ectoplasmic – it is more ectoplasmic than matter. Negative microvitum is pro-materialistic – it is more matter than mind, than ectoplasm. Positive microvitum, being more of ectoplasmic nature, starts functioning or working first in the mental level then filters down towards physical matter. Negative microvitum starts functioning in matter and moves towards the mind, towards ectoplasmic stuff and endoplasmic coverage.
items.statement: Positive microvita are pro-ectoplasmic and travel from mental to physical levels, whereas negative microvita are pro-material and travel from matter to mind.
items.title: Questions and Answers on Microvita – Excerpt B

items.quote: Negative microvita can function directly at the physico-psychic plexus (at the Vishuddha Cakra) but they cannot move upwards to the occult plexus (at the Guru Cakra). Only with the application of force by a powerful personality, can they be raised to the lunar plexus (at the Ájiṋa Cakra). This raising of negative microvita above the physico-psychic plexus is called “rusti” or “risti”. The application of negative microvita on the human mind deranges the mind and causes many psychic ailments such as eccentricity, schizophrenia, mania, melancholia, etc. In the case of positive microvita, the reaction takes place after they cross the lunar plexus, both in female and male bodies. Only positive microvita can touch the lunar plexus and be elevated up to the occult plexus. They start their journey in the lunar plexus, and as they move upwards they increase their speed and bring about acceleration in spiritual progress, both in the case of males and females.
items.statement: The forced elevation of negative microvita above the psycho-physical plexus is termed rusti, whereas raising positive microvita above the lunar plexus constitutes krpa.
items.title: Questions and Answers on Microvita – Excerpt B

items.quote: When negative microvita devour the positive microvita of a diseased person, then that person dies. Medicines only reduce the pain caused by disease in different parts of the body, and so it is not proper to say that medicine cures a disease. The disease can be cured only when the numbers of positive microvita are increased, and they devour the negative microvita.
items.statement: Physical medicines alleviate localized pain but do not cure diseases, which occurs when positive microvita increase and consume negative microvita.
items.title: Questions and Answers on Microvita – Excerpt B

items.quote: Microvita are the initial stage of matter. Microvita are the silver lining between idea and matter, though they are closer to the realm of ideas than matter.
items.statement: Microvita constitute the subtle silver lining between the physical and mental realms, representing the initial stage of matter and crude idea.
items.title: Questions and Answers on Microvita – Excerpt F

items.quote: Ectoplasm gives mental faculty but endoplasm gives unit “I” feeling. Endoplasm is the outer coverage of ectoplasm.
items.statement: Ectoplasm represents unitary structure and mental faculty, whereas endoplasm serves as its outer coverage and represents collective structure with unit 'I' feeling.
items.title: Questions and Answers on Psychology

items.quote: Running blindly without discrimination between proper and improper behaviour is called “sentiment”. The path of discrimination between proper and improper behaviour is called “rationality”. When human beings discriminate between proper and improper behaviour and select the proper path, it is called “conscience”.
items.statement: Sentiment is unreflective action, rationality is the discrimination between proper and improper conduct, and conscience is selecting the proper path.
items.title: Questions and Answers on Psychology

items.quote: When a sentiment affects the subsidiary glands, that is, when a sentiment finds its expression affecting subsidiary glands and organs, then it is known as “instinct”. The term “subsidiary glands” refers to any gland other than the pineal and pituitary glands.
items.statement: Instinct is the physical expression of a sentiment acting upon subsidiary glands and organs.
items.title: Questions and Answers on Psychology

items.quote: When human beings become restless for the attainment of Parama Puruśa, when they strive hard to realize Him in all their actions (and ultimately succeed) do so, their zeal, their irresistible urge for God is called árádhaná in Sanskrit. The prefix a – rádh (the root verb) + anat́ + t́á in feminine gender = árádhaná. The entity who does this árádhaná is known as Rádhá. Here Rádhá represents the mind of a devotee.
items.statement: Aradhana is the intense urge to attain Parama Purusa, and Radha represents the devotion-driven mind of a spiritual aspirant.
items.title: Rádhá's Devotion – Excerpt C

items.quote: So we clearly understand that to know the Cognitive Faculty means to merge in It. It is like a salt doll trying to fathom the depth of the ocean, and in the process becoming one with the ocean itself; it could not return and tell others the story of how it felt while fathoming the ocean. This sort of becoming one with the ocean while trying to fathom it is termed “self-knowledge”.
