items.title: Carnamrtam

items.qualifiers: Distinguishes the operational process from the resulting created entity.
items.quote: A sadhaka possessing occult powers, just to help someone, can project himself by assuming any form while keeping his original body protected. The process is called 'Kayabaddha' and the body form created is known as 'Chayamurti'. Sometimes, realized souls, seeing that they have not fully exhausted their reactive momenta (samskaras) and which cannot be done in this body, adopt the technique of 'Kayabaddha' by assuming different bodies to do so and get liberated from the bondage of Samskaras to enter the realm of bliss. Baba said, "For my devotees, I had to assume ten bodies in a single day, sometimes".
items.statement: Kayabaddha is the process by which an occult practitioner or realized soul projects an assumed form while protecting the original physical frame, whereas Chayamurti is the projected form itself, which does not possess internal organs such as intestines.
items.title: Carnamrtam

items.qualifiers: Applies as a distinct cognitive mechanism beyond ordinary sensory perception.
items.quote: If science is to advance in rapid strides, it will have to utilize a sixth antenna which Baba called "special perception". This special perception is "the reflection of conception within the periphery of perception." (I shall discuss this topic in more detail later.)
items.statement: Special perception in intuitional science is defined as the reflection of conception within the periphery of perception.
items.title: Glimpses of a Mystery

items.qualifiers: Tatsthiti is specifically the resultant state of the first three active practices.
items.quote: The very, essence of manava dharma, human dharma, lies in three factors, plus a fourth factor which is the resultant of the first three: (1) vistara, the principle of expansion; (2) rasa, the principle of total surrender to Parama Purus'a; (3) seva, selfless service to Parama Puru'sa and His creation; and (4) tatsthiti, the final ensconcement in Parama Purus'a.
items.statement: Human dharma (manava dharma or Bhagavat Dharma) consists of four factors: expansion (vistara), the flow of cosmic bliss (rasa), selfless service (seva), and final spiritual ensconcement (tatsthiti).
items.title: Glimpses of a Mystery

items.qualifiers: Longing melts endoplasm; ego annihilation explodes it into cetanasphota.
items.quote: This "I" feeling, however, becomes a block or an impediment in further expansion or progress. Now in what way does this "I" feeling explode? This aspect I still had to understand. Baba appeared in another dream and explained, "When you are crying for Parama Purus'a, out of longing for the Great, the endoplasm gets melted. If one is insulted, on the other hand, then the endoplasm explodes and cetanasphot'a occurs." The clash, tension and helplessness one feels when being insulted, and the subsequent resignation to the Cosmic will, develops wisdom, which is the impression of the Cosmic Mahar.
items.statement: Ectoplasmic expansion occurs through sadhana and psychic clash to enlarge awareness, while cetanasphota or cosmic explosion occurs when endoplasm dissolves through intense spiritual longing or the complete shattering of ego.
items.title: Glimpses of a Mystery

items.qualifiers: Presented as a comprehensive categorization of prevalent socio-political worldviews.
items.quote: Bábá once told that this world is suffering from three types of ideas and people: 1. Self-centred, 2. Matter-centred, and 3. God-centred. Self-centred persons are capitalists. Matter-centred people are communists. And God-centred persons are religious and spiritually minded people. Self-centred and matter-centred people have exploited the society by political power, and God-centred persons have only talked about God, they did not consider the real problems of human beings. They never thought of problems concerning housing, food, clothes, medicine, education – the minimum necessities of life. Ananda Margis are to work for God-realization of all members of the society by teaching them spiritual practices as well as by creating a societal structure wherein the basic necessities of life are available to one and all, so that everyone would have the opportunity to develop their higher spiritual faculties.
items.statement: Human social and political ideas are historically divided into three orientations: self-centred (capitalism), matter-centred (communism), and God-centred (spiritual/religious).
items.title: Glories of Baba

items.qualifiers: contextualized within the chapter titled Paralelismo psicoespiritual in Idea e ideología
items.quote: Al final, cuando la longitud de onda de la mente se vuelve infinita, y esas ondas también fluyen en una línea recta, la mente se transforma en el atman (la consciencia o el alma). Este estado se llama samadhi. Es aquí donde las ondas psíquicas alcanzan un paralelismo con las ondas espirituales del atman. Este paralelismo psicoespiritual es conocido como "idea" o bhava. Cuando este bhava o idea es concebida en el nivel psíquico, es "ideología".
items.statement: Ananda Marga defines ideological conception as a psycho-spiritual parallelism where mental wavelengths align with the spiritual waves of the atman.
items.title: Historias_de_un_Maestro_Tantrico

items.qualifiers: grounded in yogic vital energy theory
items.quote: El cuerpo humano —dijo—, tiene diez vayus o aires vitales, cinco internos y cinco externos. De los cinco vayus internos, prana gobierna el área desde el punto del ombligo hasta la garganta; apana, el área debajo del ombligo; saman, localizado en el ombligo, mantiene el equilibrio entre apana y prana; udana gobierna el área de la garganta; y vyana está distribuido en el cuerpo. Cada uno es responsable de las funciones corporales en sus áreas respectivas. Por ejemplo, prana controla la respiración. —Después de elucidar en detalle cada uno de los vayus internos, explicó los vayus externos de la misma manera, y luego empezó a explicar lo que pasa con los vayus durante la muerte—: En el cuerpo humano el ombligo es el punto de equilibrio entre la porción superior y la inferior. Cuando el saman no puede mantener el equilibrio entre prana y apana, entonces prana se disloca, lo que incrementa la respiración umbilical. Cuando estos tres vayus no pueden mantener su integridad individual, se funden y chocan en el udana. Cuando udana también pierde su integridad individual, los cuatro vayus se fusionan en vyana y buscan una forma de escapar del cuerpo.
items.statement: The physical human body contains ten vayus, whose loss of internal balance and subsequent fusion into vyana causes the vital force to dislocate and escape at death.
items.title: Historias_de_un_Maestro_Tantrico

items.qualifiers: contrasted with purely materialistic philosophical models
items.quote: La filosofía de Ananda Marga penetra profundamente en la causa última de todos los efectos manifiestos y enuncia que la materia es la forma metamorfoseada de Purushottama, la Consciencia Nuclear que existe como la causa noumenal. De este modo, como resultado del choque dentro de la estructura material, se crea una base sutil y esta a su vez da cabida a la formación de la mente cruda o citta individual, la cual no tiene ni al ego ("Yo hago" o la segunda subjetividad mental), ni a la primera subjetividad mental ("Yo soy")⁶.
items.statement: The physical universe originates from the nuclear consciousness through the involution of consciousness into matter, whereupon internal clashes pulverize physical structures back into crude ectoplasm to start conscious evolution.
items.title: Historias_de_un_Maestro_Tantrico

items.quote: At one point Baba was speaking about people trying to expand their minds to Parama Purusa. And He said very clearly, that was not the way He was suggesting people meditate. Instead of bringing your mind to a point and expanding it, bring your mind to a point and then at that bindu have the awareness that Parama Purusa is infinite and totally surrounds you with infinite love and awareness encompasses you. Instead of trying to make yourself so big, make yourself tiny and small and then realize that only God, only Parama Purusa is there.
items.statement: In meditation on the Supreme, the mind should not attempt to forcefully expand outwards, but should reduce itself to a pinpoint (bindu) and recognize that Infinite Consciousness completely surrounds it.
items.title: I Am Yours

items.qualifiers: explained by Baba regarding their socio-spiritual functions
items.quote: He said, “Renaissance Universal (RU) is like this” and made motions like two cymbals clashing together, “to create clash in the mind, and to bring people, by powdering down the mind, closer to Parama Purusa.” Then He said, “RAWA is to attract people’s hearts to love Parama Purusa, to get closer, by the attraction of love through art.”
items.statement: Renaissance Universal (RU) and Renaissance Artists and Writers Association (RAWA) employ distinct mechanisms: RU creates intellectual clash to breakdown ego, whereas RAWA attracts the heart to divine love through art.
items.title: I Am Yours

items.qualifiers: stipulated as mandatory conditions for revolutionary success
items.quote: Baba at that time talked about the essential elements for a successful revolution. I still remember the three points He mentioned. Morality, a strong spiritual/moral foundation must be there. Second, you should never lose sight of who is being served, never lose track of humanity. Third, pinnacled intellect. You must start with your foundation, a broad foundation, and build more pointed and specific to an apex, to specific points. Your intellect must be sharp and pinnacled.
items.statement: A successful revolution requires three essential elements: a strong moral/spiritual foundation, maintaining focus on serving humanity, and a sharp, pinnacled intellect.
items.title: I Am Yours

items.qualifiers: Outlines a specific 4-step framework of mental control in spiritual progress.
items.quote:
These are the four steps in the Spiritual Path:

1. Yatamana – The first step is to make an effort. At this step the aspirant is trying all means to overcome the vrittis (attitudes or propensities of the mind).

2. Vyatireka – When one of the disturbing vrittis gets fully under controlled it brings confidence in the aspirant's mind.

3. Ekendriya – In the third step the aspirant is able to regulate many vrittis, but sometimes one vritti remains beyond control. Sometimes, the aspirant takes it with such despondency that it seems like there is no hope left. There should not be any worry. The Guru is there. His help is to be requested.
items.statement: There are four progressive stages on the spiritual path: Yatamana (making initial effort to control mental propensities), Vyatireka (bringing one disturbing propensity under full control), Ekendriya (controlling many propensities while one remains obstinate), and Vashiikar (attaining complete mental control and balanced peace).
items.title: I Meet My Beloved, Dada Dharmavedananda

items.qualifiers: Distinguished from mere respect or reverence.
items.quote: Shraddha' comes from shrat, meaning satyam, and dha' from the root verb dha. When one ascribes everything to one's goal, or one's object, or to the Supreme Subjectivity appearing as one's object, and moves, or rather directs one's everything towards Him, then that movement is shraddha'. First ascribing that supreme veracity to the object (actually it is the Supreme Subjectivity taken as an object) and then directing one's everything towards Him, is that mental movement which is called shraddha'.
items.statement: Shraddha is defined as the mental movement where one first ascribes supreme veracity to the goal or Supreme Subjectivity, and then directs one's entire being towards Him.
items.title: I Meet My Beloved, Dada Dharmavedananda

items.qualifiers: Explains why holistic three-stratum exercise (physical, psychic, spiritual) is necessary.
items.quote:
If exercise is done only for the development of physical body and the mental body is neglected, those physically strong people will become intellectually a bit deficient. If it goes on for generation after generation, the cranium itself will become smaller and as such, the brain will also be smaller in size resulting in less intellectual faculty.

If exercise is done for psychic development along with physical exercises and there no spiritual practice, then those psychically strong persons would use their intellect to fulfill their mundane desire of depriving others. They would be no better than a plant. So there should be Samyak Vyayam, proper exercise of physical body, psychic body and also of spiritual body. This is the fifth instruction.
items.statement: Exercising exclusively for physical development while neglecting mental development leads to intellectual deficiency, whereas combining psychic development with physical exercise without spiritual practice causes individuals to use intellect maliciously to deprive others.
items.title: I Meet My Beloved, Dada Dharmavedananda

items.quote:
He says that the process of spiritual attainment is 'TANTRA'. 'TAN' means to expand and 'TRA' means that which liberates. Thus 'TANTRA' means that which brings liberation by expansion of mind. In 'TANTRA', 99 percent is practice, only 1 percent is theory.

My Master said, "What is TANTRA?" He explained that TANTRA has two aspects—'A'gama' and 'Nigama', like the two wings of a bird. 'A'gama' is the philosophical aspect and 'Nigama' is the practical cult.
items.statement: Tantra is defined etymologically as the process that brings liberation through the expansion of mind, comprising two complementary aspects: Agama (theoretical/philosophical aspect) and Nigama (practical cult).
items.title: I Meet My Beloved

items.qualifiers: Distinguished from Taraka Brahma who is completely free from the limitations of Saguna Brahma.
items.quote:
In general, there are three types of manifestations of the Supreme Consciousness:

Firstly, Jiivakoti: they are the normal human beings.

Secondly, Iishvarakoti: they are those who have been given special power to do spiritual work and, to some extent, social work. Their power is one hundred times that of a jiivakoti. There are three types of Iishvarakoti in order of increasing greatness. They are (i) kalavatara, who has one-sixteenth of the full power of Iishvarakoti, (ii) amshavatara, who has even more power, and (iii) khandavatara, who is still more developed. Iishvarakotis advance due to their sadhana or meditation. They work in a particular time and place and then leave the world.

Thirdly, Brahmakoti: he is a person with full manifestation of Saguna Brahma. In such saints there are no worldly bondages at all. This manifestation is also known as Maha'kaola or one who has the power to raise not only his own kundalini, but that of others also.
items.statement: Manifestations of Supreme Consciousness are categorized into Jiivakoti (normal human beings), Iishvarakoti (beings endowed with special spiritual and social powers in varying degrees such as kalavatara, amshavatara, and khandavatara), and Brahmakoti (full manifestation of Saguna Brahma/Sadguru/Mahakaola who has the power to raise their own and others' kundalini).
items.title: Living With Baba- Dada Tapeshvarananda

items.qualifiers: Sadguru falls into the category of Uttama guru.
items.quote:
Adhama guru: This is the lowest guru who may have achieved some spiritual advancement. He just gives advice and does not bother to see if the disciple follows his instructions. He can only help them in resolving worldly problems.

Madhyama guru: This is the mediocre guru, who is able to elevate the disciples a little by singing spiritual songs or by going into spiritual states himself, thus indirectly affecting the disciples. He advises his disciples on spiritual matters and enquires whether the disciples are following his instructions, but does not bother with those who do not listen or follow such instructions.

Uttama guru: This is the highest guru, who not only teaches his disciples, but compels those who have left the spiritual path to return by creating circumstantial pressure. He can directly raise the kundalini of a disciple who surrenders to Him. He keeps strict vigilance on the disciples to ensure that they follow His directives.
items.statement: Gurus are classified into three types: Adhama guru (gives advice only without ensuring adherence), Madhyama guru (elevates disciples indirectly and checks on compliance but disregards non-followers), and Uttama guru (highest guru who compels wandering disciples to return, keeps strict vigilance, and directly raises kundalini upon surrender).
items.title: Living With Baba- Dada Tapeshvarananda

items.qualifiers: Children generally lose extra-cerebral memory after age five due to parental attachment.
items.quote: He explained that cerebral memory is the ability to think, remember and memorize something with one's brain about things that have happened in this life. Extra-cerebral memory refers to the ability to think, remember or memorize anything of one's past life with one's brain in this life. Hence, cerebral memory is common and every human being possesses it in the present life.
items.statement: Cerebral memory refers to the brain's ability to retain and recall experiences from the current lifetime, whereas extra-cerebral memory refers to the brain's capacity to recall memories and events from a previous lifetime.
items.title: Living With Baba- Dada Tapeshvarananda

items.qualifiers: Prescribed as a specific temporal discipline to accelerate spiritual progress and resolve mental ailments.
items.quote: He clarified that every sadhaka should get up from bed before a certain time, which is 45 minutes before sunrise. At that time the sun emits a particular wave beneficial for sadhakas, and it is through this wave that He removes all negative vibrations from the human mind and injects positive ones in their place. In order to make this a formal system within the framework of our spiritual practice, He instructed all His devotees to start paincajanya at 5.00 a.m. sharp.
items.statement: Performing paincajanya starting at 5:00 a.m. sharp (45 minutes before sunrise) exposes the practitioner to specific solar waves that eliminate negative mental vibrations and infuse positive ones.
items.title: Living With Baba- Dada Tapeshvarananda

items.quote: Very often He would say, “If your love for someone is 100%, see that your chastisement does not exceed 75%. The degree of control should never go beyond the degree of love.”
items.statement: An individual's degree of chastisement or control over another should never exceed seventy-five percent of their love for that person.
items.title: My Days with Baba

items.quote: Where an elaborate definition is given about what should and should not be done, and advice is given in addition, we say it is upadesha, which translates as “advice”. Where, after explaining what should and should not be done, positive direction is given, it is nirdesha, that is, “pointing out” or “directions”. Where an order or command is made, whether explanations are given or not, it is ádesha, or “command”.
items.statement: Bengali words derived from the root 'dish' differ functionally: upadesha is advice with elaborate analysis of dos and don'ts, nirdesha is positive direction following explanation, and ádesha is an imperative order or command.
items.title: My Days with Baba

items.quote: To begin with, He expands economic thought and recategorizes it into four parts. He calls these people's economy, psycho-economy, the commercial economy and the general economy.
items.statement: Economics is categorized into four distinct branches: people's economy, psycho-economy, commercial economy, and general economy.
items.title: My Master The Supreme Guide

items.quote: PROUT suggests that increases in per capita income are not a sufficiently reliable and scientific index to determine the standard and progress of a particular and deceitful, because it refers to a simple mathematical calculation of total national income divided by total population.
items.statement: Purchasing capacity is the only true and scientific measure of economic standard and prosperity, rendering per capita income a deceitful and unreliable index.
items.title: My Master The Supreme Guide

items.quote: "Yes. In nirvikalpa sama'dhi, all the va'yus (internal vital airs of the body) are concentrated in the pineal gland. For that reason, the body becomes completely stiff like a corpse. After coming out of that type of sama'dhi, one will experience wonderful bliss. Yet two or three persons must massage the aspirant's body for about two hours. Only then can the person sit up. The aspirant will remain weak for a long time afterwards."
items.statement: In Nirvikalpa Samádhi the internal vital airs concentrate entirely in the pineal gland, rendering the physical body corpse-like and requiring extended physical massage to revive.
items.title: My Spiritual Life With Baba

items.qualifiers: regarding occult healing versus spiritual evolution
items.quote: Those who are cured by occult powers will not adopt a spiritual path, Ba'ba' said. Why should they take the trouble to adopt a spiritual path when their disease has already been cured so easily? Ba'ba' concluded by stating that using occult powers to cure someone of disease is an "anti-God action."
items.statement: Curing physical diseases through the application of occult powers prevents individuals from pursuing genuine spiritual paths, making such intervention anti-spiritual.
items.title: My Spiritual Life With Baba

items.quote: He said, “My son, you are in my imagination. I am imagining you. You cannot imagine me. You think you are imagining me, but you are not. You cannot imagine me. When you think upon me I am with you!”
items.statement: A spiritual aspirant cannot imagine the Guru; rather, the devotee exists within the Guru's imagination, and contemplating the Guru immediately manifests His presence.
items.title: My Time With Baba

items.quote: Every object has two kinds of values: one is its utility value and the other its existential value. Human beings have up until now accepted the utility value of animals, birds and plants, but not their existential value. Baba emphasized their existential value.
items.statement: Every created entity possesses both utility value and existential value; Neo-Humanism explicitly emphasizes the recognition of existential value across all animate and inanimate entities.
items.title: Namami Kalyanasundaram Part II

items.quote: Microvita is a mysterious emanation of the Cosmic Mind, a mysterious expression. Microvita or microbes do not only work in the biological sphere. Microbes move in the biological, the mental as well as in the spiritual domains. These microvita are more subtle than atoms, electrons, protons and neutrons.
items.statement: Microvita are mysterious emanations of the Cosmic Mind that operate across biological, psychic, and spiritual realms, existing in both crude observable states and subtle wave forms.
items.title: Namami Kalyanasundaram Part II

items.quote: Cosmic mind is beginning-less and endless, and therefore its creation is also endless. Creation has been going on since eternity and it will go on until eternity. There may be destruction here and there, but the whole creation will never be finally destroyed.
items.statement: Creation is a continuous, eternal thought-flow of the Cosmic Mind; while localized destruction occurs, the total universe is never completely annihilated.
items.title: Never Shall We Forget You, Dada Chandranath

items.quote: This flow from crude to subtle is called prati-saiñcara. In the first stage of this flow towards the subtle, práńáh, or vital energy, arises. In the water, algae begin to accumulate, and on trees and the soil a layer of moss, and grass on the Earth and thereafter the more developed forms of trees bearing flowers and fruits in which we find the signs of life force.
items.statement: The evolutionary return flow of the universe towards subtlety is called pratisaiṋcara, progressing from vital energy in plants to moving life, animals with thought, and ultimately independent-minded human beings.
items.title: Never Shall We Forget You, Dada Chandranath

items.quote: However, there is a state of Brahma between these two states. This state of Brahma is the connecting link between the qualified and non-qualified Brahma. He is called Taraka Brahma (literally, the Brahma who can liberate).
items.statement: Taraka Brahma is the tangential connecting link between non-qualified Nirguna Brahma and qualified Saguna Brahma, serving as the liberating bridge across worldly bondage.
items.title: Sambhavami

items.quote: One of Baba's most significant contributions in the theoretical field is his concept of the six spokes of the social cycle (Sadara Samaj Cakra). These are: 1) spiritual philosophy. 2) spiritual practice. 3) socio-economic theory. 4) social outlook, 5) spiritual scriptures and 6) preceptor.
items.statement: An ideal and balanced society requires the presence of six specific spokes in the social cycle: spiritual philosophy, spiritual practice, socio-economic theory, social outlook, spiritual scriptures, and a preceptor.
items.title: Sambhavami

items.quote: In biology He explained that evolution is guided by micropsychic longing for the Great, and not by a random transformation of genes selected by survival factors. The passage from the psychic longing to the actual genetic mutation is effected through subtle physico-psychic entities which He calls Microvita.
items.statement: Biological evolution is driven by the psychic longing for the Great rather than random mutation, with microvita acting as the subtle physico-psychic mediators of genetic change.
items.title: Shraddhainjali

items.qualifiers: according to P.R. Sarkar's physical philosophy
items.quote: In physics He said that the basis of the atomic structure is not constituted by the subatomic particles discovered by modern science, but is the result of the union of billions of Microvita. In other words, Microvita are responsible of the evolution of the whole universe.
items.statement: The physical atomic structure is composed of the union of billions of microvita rather than subatomic particles alone.
items.title: Shraddhainjali

items.quote: He gave the definition of sannyasi as “one who will have only the universal family, and not any small family”, and to the family persons He said they would have both the small and the universal family.
items.statement: A sannyasi is defined as one who belongs entirely to the universal family without maintaining a small personal family, whereas a family person maintains both.
items.title: Shraddhainjali

items.quote: You see, Keshavananda, one should usually sleep where maximum people are walking, because this habit will not allow the perverted ego to grow.
items.statement: One should sleep where the maximum number of people walk in order to prevent the growth of perverted ego.
items.title: Shraddhainjali

items.quote: Baba said the green turmeric should be used as a medicine not the dried one which is commonly available in the market. A small piece of green turmeric should be eaten with a little piece of “Kashir Chini” (Rock Candy) or few drops of honey on an empty stomach in the morning.
items.statement: Green turmeric eaten in the morning on an empty stomach with rock candy or honey serves as a primary remedy for skin diseases and venereal infections.
items.title: Stories of Baba

items.quote: You know, these spots of light are Luminous Bodies. They want a human body, because they have only three factors - Ethereal, Aerial and Luminous. They cannot get liberation until they get a human body. They don't do any harm to human beings, rather they help in many ways.
items.statement: Luminous bodies possess only ethereal, aerial, and luminous factors, and must obtain a human body to achieve liberation.
items.title: Stories of Baba

items.qualifiers: distinction between collective social and individual personal spheres
items.quote: For collective social life people will demand their minimum necessities but in individual personal life they have to practice Santosa all the time.
items.statement: Practitioners must demand collective necessities for social life while strictly observing contentment (santosa) in individual personal life.
items.title: Stories of Baba

items.qualifiers: mechanism of altered perception demonstrated by Baba
items.quote: Both of them are correct. I changed the tanmatras (minute fractions of waves) coming from the hair before they are perceived by their eyes. When I changed them to golden tanmatras, they saw the hair was made of gold. When I changed them to silver tanmatras, they saw the hair was made of silver. It is nothing but a play of inferences.
items.statement: Perception of altered sensory qualities like color, taste, and smell occurs through the modification of inferential waves (tanmatras) before sensory organ contact.
items.title: Stories of Baba

items.qualifiers: contextualized within the book's spiritual philosophy
items.quote: Tantra, as it is understood in this book, is an approach to life rooted in the struggle to overcome inner and outer obstacles to self-realisation.
items.statement: Tantra is defined as an approach to life rooted in the struggle against internal and external obstacles to achieve self-realization.
items.title: Tantric Women Tell Their Stories

items.qualifiers: formal philosophical definitions from Human Society Part 1
items.quote: When morality leads human beings to the fullest expression of their finer human qualities, then alone is its practical value fully realized. The concerted effort to bridge the gap between the first expression of morality and establishment in universal humanism is called "social progress." And the collective body of those who are engaged in the concerted effort to conquer this gap, I call "society."
items.statement: Social progress is defined as the concerted effort to bridge the gap between initial morality and universal humanism, and society is defined as the collective body engaged in that effort.
items.title: The Jamalpur Days

items.qualifiers: explains the origin of mind out of matter
items.quote: Thus, as a result of clash within the material structure, a subtle base is created and this in turn gives rise to the formation of crude mind or unit citta, which has neither the ego (“I do” or second mental subjectivity) nor the first mental subjectivity (“I am”).
items.statement: Crude mind or ectoplasm originates when the extreme momentum of cosmic involution (saincara) causes structural clash that pulverizes portions of matter.
items.title: The Jamalpur Days

items.qualifiers: normally active up to age five, or age twelve in jatismara
items.quote: The revival of past experiences is what we call ‘extracerebral memory,’ and is the principal task of the causal mind. The experiences of a crude mind cannot be reflected in a subtle mind. In the case of a child, since the crude experiences are relatively few, the subtle mind remains tranquil. Thus the waves of the causal mind easily surface in the child’s subtle mind. As a result, the accumulated experiences of the child’s previous life can easily be recollected.
items.statement: Extra-cerebral memory in young children arises because their tranquil subtle mind allows past experiences stored in the causal mind to surface without interference from environmental waves.
items.title: The Jamalpur Days

items.qualifiers: conditional upon contemplating objects as expressions of Brahma before dealing with them
items.quote: That is why the sa'dhaka will have to deal with preya in such a manner that it does not become a cause of bondage or extroversion of tendencies, but will instead lead to the introversion of tendencies and thereby to mukti or liberation. This technique is known as madhuvidya'.
items.statement: Madhuvidya is defined as the technique of dealing with objects of worldly gratification by contemplating them with cosmic feeling to ensure tendencies introvert toward liberation rather than outward bondage.
items.title: The Life & Teachings of Shrii Shrii Anandamurti

items.qualifiers: only through these practices can the kos'as be perfected
items.quote:
The annamaya kos'a is perfected through a'sanas (physical postures). Yama and niyama sa'dhana' perfects the ka'mamaya kos'a. The manomaya kos'a is perfected through pra'n'a'ya'ma. Through pratya'ha'ra the atimanasa kos'a is perfected. The vijina'namaya kos'a is perfected through dha'ra'na' and the hiran'maya kos'a through

dhya'na.
items.statement: The five kos'as of human existence are consummated through specific aspects of eight-fold yoga (astanga yoga): annamaya via asanas, kamamaya via yama and niyama, manomaya via pranayama, atimanasa via pratyahara, vijnanamaya via dharana, and hiranmaya via dhyana.
items.title: The Life & Teachings of Shrii Shrii Anandamurti

items.qualifiers: culturally advanced people are not necessarily civilized if their expressions lack control and rationality
items.quote:
Crude manifestations of expressions are

called krs't'i. The sum total of both crude and subtle manifestation of expressions is sam'skrti. Krs't'i may differ from one group of people to other but the sam'krti of human being is one.

Cultural expression and civilization are not synonymous. Where there is a control and rationality in the different expressions of life, there is civilization.
items.statement: Culture across the entire human race is fundamentally one, whereas local differences in songs, dances, and customs represent varied local expressions (krs't'i), and civilization exists where there is rational control over these expressions.
items.title: The Life & Teachings of Shrii Shrii Anandamurti

items.qualifiers: applies as long as unit beings perceive separation from Parama Purus'a
items.quote: One's nerve cells, glands, and sub-glands are created according to one's individual flow. In fact, various structures are created based on this individual flow. The various thought-waves of the mind are all identified with the individual flows.
items.statement: Individual microcosmic nerve cells, glands, and bodily structures are formed and differentiated according to an individual's unique psychic flow (svarasa).
items.title: The Life & Teachings of Shrii Shrii Anandamurti

items.qualifiers: framed as an explanatory teaching by Baba
items.quote: Suppose Parama Puruśa makes a boundary of goodness and keeps all the people inside. Then all will be good, and none will become bad. None can go out of this jurisdiction. But this is also a problem, for to remain in the bondage of goodness means they cannot know the Infinite. Their progress will be stopped. If there is no boundary, people can go where they like, good or bad. Parama Puruśa does not make any bondage of goodness because He does not want to stop the progress of those who desire liberation.
items.statement: God does not impose an inescapable boundary of goodness around humanity because confining beings to goodness would stop their progress toward the Infinite and impede those desiring liberation.
items.title: The Supreme Friend

items.qualifiers: regardless of whether the advice comes from someone younger or older
items.quote: Anushásana is the Sam'skrta word for discipline. What is the meaning of anushásana? Hitárthe shásanam ityarthe anushásanam. "Hit" means "welfare" or "benefit". If anyone gives you any advice or a rule for your benefit, then you follow it, that will be discipline.
items.statement: Anushásana (discipline) is defined as following advice or rules that are given specifically for one's welfare or benefit.
items.title: The Supreme Friend

items.qualifiers: permissible only when motivated by collective welfare
items.quote: This type of diplomacy is good because it is for the welfare of the people. Diplomacy should always be for the welfare of the people. It should not be used for personal gain. Then it will be a sin.
items.statement: Diplomacy must exclusively serve the collective welfare of the people; using it for personal gain constitutes a sin.
items.title: The Supreme Friend

items.qualifiers: specific to authorship naming conventions in Anandamurti's works
items.quote: Back at the office, Bábá made the comment, “Ánandamúrti does not deal in any material things. Wherever I have discussed mundane things, there is written P. R. Sarkár.”
items.statement: The name P. R. Sarkar is used when discussing mundane and social philosophies, whereas Shrii Shrii Anandamurti is the spiritual embodiment that does not deal directly in material objects.
items.title: The Supreme Friend

items.qualifiers: revelation correcting common assumptions regarding saincara and prati-saincara
items.quote: The association of a unit mind with a group of physical cells is what we call an animate entity. But the matter of those so-called animate cells is actually still in the sainchara phase. It is the unit mind alone which is in the prati-sainchara phase.
items.statement: An animate entity consists of a unit mind evolving in the introversial phase (prati-saincara) associated with physical cells moving in the extroversial phase (saincara), guided indirectly by Cosmic Mind via microvita.
items.title: Travels With the Mystic Master

items.qualifiers: cellular protoplasm possesses no independent will power apart from Parama Purusha
items.quote: For the expression of will power, the periphery of the doer “I” feeling must be greater than the periphery of the done “I” feeling. Nevertheless, you should not forget that the will power of Parama Purusha is omnipresent—even within your smallest protoplasmic cells.
items.statement: A person cannot experience expression of will power unless the periphery of their doer 'I' feeling exceeds the periphery of their done 'I' feeling.
items.title: Travels With the Mystic Master

items.qualifiers: must be distinguished from questions asked whimsically, casually, or to befool others
items.quote: Pariprashnena has only one meaning, only one import, and that is that you are to ask a question in order to get a certain reply, and that reply will be followed by you in the practical field. You ask the question knowing that you will act according to the reply. So all the questions of spiritual aspirants must be pariprashnena, and not ordinary questions.
items.statement: Pariprashnena is defined as an inquiry asked by a spiritual aspirant with the firm commitment to act upon the answer in the practical field.
items.title: Walking With the Master

items.qualifiers: invisible in daylight and distinct from positive or negative hallucinations and presita manas
items.quote: It is said that there are seven kinds of luminous bodies: yakśa, siddha, vidyadhara, gandharva, kinnara, prakrtiliina and videhaliina. They are categorized according to their respective psychologies.
items.statement: Luminous bodies (devayonis) are entities composed solely of luminous, aerial, and ethereal factors without solid or liquid factors, categorized into seven types (yakśa, siddha, vidyadhara, gandharva, kinnara, prakrtiliina, and videhaliina) based on their unexpressed psychological desires.
items.title: Walking With the Master

items.qualifiers: functions only for two to four minutes before dissolving
items.quote:
Now if, under certain circumstances, the ectoplasm of a living person is associated with that disembodied mind, then that disembodied mind gets a mental body temporarily, for a short time. Then that mental body can start functioning with the help of the nerve cells and nerve fibres of that living person, but only for about two to four minutes. What is this called? Neither is it positive hallucination or negative hallucination, nor is it a luminous body (devayoni). Then what is it?

A living person’s ectoplasmic cells become the mental body of a dead person for a few minutes until, after two to four minutes, that mental body again dies. This mental body I will call ‘presita manas’ – ‘recreated mind’.
items.statement: A 'presita manas' (recreated mind) occurs when the disembodied mind of a deceased person temporarily adopts the ectoplasm and nerve cells of a living person for two to four minutes.
items.title: Walking With the Master

items.qualifiers: added as an appendage to Prout social theory
items.quote: “A person may be an intellectual, but not necessarily a Vipra. An intellectual must be doing their duty to society to be called a Vipra. Do you follow?”
items.statement: An intellectual cannot automatically be classified as a Vipra unless they actively utilize their intellectual capacity to perform their duty toward collective social welfare.
items.title: Walking With the Master

items.qualifiers: Described specifically within the socio-economic context of India
items.quote:
Baba explained that there are four types of beggars in India:

1) Professional beggars.
2) Kidnapped people, often children, who would be purposely deformed by gangs and then forced to beg.
3) Persons who are lame and disabled through natural calamities.
4) Orphans.
items.statement: Beggars in India are classified into four categories: professional beggars; kidnapped persons (often children purposely deformed by gangs); individuals disabled through natural calamities; and orphans.
items.title: With My Master

items.qualifiers: Applies directly to Anandamurti's spiritual and organizational instructions
items.quote: My orders and injunctions consist of two types: affirmative, stated as advice; and negative, a prohibition or forewarning. If I give orders in an affirmative way, then you may or may not choose to follow My advice. I will be responsible for a person who obeys Me, and I may or may not be responsible if one does not. However, if I give an order with a negative assertion (by way of a refusal or prohibition), then I am not responsible for the consequences to the person disobeying Me.
items.statement: Anandamurti distinguished between affirmative orders given as advice, where compliance is optional and Guru responsibility is conditional, versus negative orders (prohibitions or forewarnings), where disobedience removes all Guru responsibility for subsequent consequences.
items.title: With My Master

items.qualifiers: Depends on the mental state at the moment of receiving initiation
items.quote: The proof of the power of Ista Mantra is that the condition in which a sadhaka takes initiation gets exaggerated further. If one has taken initiation in a painful condition the person will face more calamities in the future, and if initiation has been given when the mental condition was pleasant, he or she will feel plenty of happy occasions coming in life. Ista Mantra works like fire in the powder of the person's samskaras.
items.statement: The practice of Ista Mantra exaggerates the initial condition under which initiation took place, acting like fire on unexhausted reactive momenta (samskaras).
items.title: With My Master

items.qualifiers: Sequential ordering condition for yogic dances relative to meditation
items.quote: Tandava should be performed after sadhana. If the body gets exhausted by tandava, sadhana can't be done properly. Lalita marmiika and kaoshikii dances should be done before sadhana.
items.statement: Tandava dance must be performed after sadhana to avoid exhausting the body beforehand, whereas Lalita Marmika and Kaoshikii dances should be performed prior to sadhana.
items.title: With My Master

items.qualifiers: Contrasts mental action/service (puja) with ecstatic union and surrender (vandana)
items.quote:
Baba explained the difference between Guru Puja and Guru Vandana explaining that puja is when we with our mental force do any work to satisfy our Ista (Ideational Desideratum). When with one-

pointed determined longing and action we strive to please the Guru through shravana (hearing and singing His name, stories of Him), manana (meditation) and nididhyasana (concentrating all propensities, all mental force into one point and surrendering it to Him within one's I-feeling) — this is Guru Puja. Baba said that without Guru Puja, success couldn't be achieved in the physical world, psychic world or the spiritual world.

Baba then said that puja can be completely done in the psychic sphere and it can be carried out through righteous actions. Vandana however, is beyond this. In addition to what is done in puja, vandana is a special form of pleasing Him wherein the puja is done drenched with para stuti or shuddha stuti.
items.statement: Guru Puja involves one-pointed action and meditation to satisfy the Ista, whereas Guru Vandana transcends puja by being drenched in higher, pure adoration (para stuti or shuddha stuti) characterized by total surrender and permanent union.
items.title: You-Are-Never-Alone-Vandananda

items.qualifiers: Prescribed as a specific spiritual technique to quiet the conscious mind
items.quote: Baba took my hand in His and repeated three times in Hindi, “You can do meditation, you can do meditation, you can do meditation.” He added, “But from today you should do kiirtan before doing meditation.” There were a few other visitors in the room. Baba asked me, “What happens when the electricity goes off in a room with a bulb?” I said, “Baba, it becomes dark.” Baba said, “Yes, it becomes so dark that you will not eve be able to see your own hands. So through kiirtan black out your mind. Then there will be very good meditations.”
items.statement: Singing kiirtan before meditation acts to black out the mind and enables deep meditation, especially when physical weakness or distraction hinders practice.
items.title: Dada Ik: Baba Stories

items.qualifiers: Must be taken upon waking in the morning
items.quote: He told me that from today onward, I had to drink lemon water with salt ever morning after getting up. Since then, I have drinking lemon water. Baba talked that day a lot about lemon water. Basically he said that the lemon can cure several illnesses, including mine as it was originating in the digestive system and the lemon water cleanses it.
items.statement: Drinking lemon water with salt every morning cleanses the digestive system and cures related digestive ailments.
items.title: Dada Ik: Baba Stories

items.qualifiers: Represents hierarchical stages of mental development in spiritual practice
items.quote:
To meet the needs of all, the scriptures prescribe four kinds of worship: ‘‘The highest worship is to think of oneself as Brahman; the second method of worship is meditation on God; the third method is japam, prayer, and glorification of God; and the last method is external, ritualistic worship.”’
The highest sadhana is to experience the Atman all the time. The stage prior to this is meditation. At that time the aspirant feels that only God and he exist. In deep meditation he sees the form of his Chosen Deity and cannot continue his japam. In the stage prior to meditation the aspirant glorifies God, chants his name, and at the same time thinks of his form. The last method is the ritualistic worship of God embodied in an image or symbol.
items.statement: Scriptures prescribe four methods of worship adapted to different stages of mental evolution: highest is thinking of oneself as Brahman; second is meditation on God; third is japam, prayer, and glorification; fourth is external ritualistic worship.
items.title: A guide to spiritual life spiritual teachings of Swami Brahmananda (Brahmananda, Swami, 1863-1922, Chetanananda etc.)

items.qualifiers: Contrasts mental conquest with mere mortification of the physical body
items.quote: Real austerity is not in performing feats such as those. Anyone can do such things by practice. It is easy to conquer the body, but it is extremely difficult to conquer the mind and its desires for lust and gold, name and fame. Real austerity depends on three things: First, you must be truthful. Completely establish your life on truth and then per- form action. Second, you must conquer lust. Third, you must conquer worldly cravings. Observe these three basic princi- ples. To assimilate them in your life is real austerity.
items.statement: True austerity (tapasya) consists of three foundational achievements rather than physical feats: establishing life completely on truth, conquering lust (brahmacharya), and conquering worldly cravings.
items.title: A guide to spiritual life spiritual teachings of Swami Brahmananda (Brahmananda, Swami, 1863-1922, Chetanananda etc.)

items.qualifiers: May apply to one, many, or all areas of life.
items.quote: Tradition distinguishes three degrees of intensity in prarabdha karma. These may apply to one, many, or all areas of your life: dridha, dridhaadridha, and adridha. Dridha (“fixed”) karma is so intense that it is effectively nonchangeable. Dridha karma creates those seemingly “fated” events, pleasurable and painful, that either occur despite all our efforts to avoid them or fail to take place despite all our efforts to create them. The good or bad results produced by dridha-adridha (“fixed-unfixed” or “fixed but not completely fixed”) karma can be changed by anyone who is willing to apply the concentrated creative will needed to change them; in the absence of any sustained effort their predicted results will appear. Adridha (“unfixed”) karma can be altered with relative ease, meaning that that you may do more or less what you please (within reason) in those areas of your life.
items.statement: Tradition categorizes prarabdha karma into three levels of intensity: dridha (fixed and effectively unchangeable), dridha-adridha (modifiable through sustained creative will), and adridha (easily alterable).
items.title: Aghora 3: The Law of Karma

items.quote: Vimalananda, who was not concerned about which raindrop you may have boarded on your journey here, did believe that jivas find their parents via the law of attraction. Karmas are not performed in a vacuum; performed action always has an object, however obscure. Energy (shakti) of all kinds flows only when it has some destination to flow to, just as electrical energy flows only when a circuit is created. Your action creates a relationship with its object, be it of dense or subtle matter. Even something so seemingly insubstantial as a thought can act as an action’s object. Vimalananda called the relationship thus created rnanubandhana (“the binding of karmic debt”). The energy flux that your action initiates creates a debt (rna) that is payable to you if you sent energy to your object, and that you must pay if you extracted something from that object. Every action creates another ‘’tie that binds”, another bond that will draw you back toward that object so that you can square up your karmic account when that residue matures.
items.statement: Rnanubandhana is defined as the binding of karmic debt created whenever an action establishes a subtle or gross energetic relationship with its object.
items.title: Aghora 3: The Law of Karma

items.quote: Prakriti Siddhi is in the realm of anyathakartum, that which is not only impossible but also unimaginable. Prakriti Siddhi is the ability to change the innate nature of any part of the Universal Prakriti, which means the ability to alter the consciousness of any being in the universe. When we talk about fate we are talking about Prakriti Siddhi. This is very deep; think about it very carefully. Fate is an ethereal being who knows and uses the highest of all the siddhis: Prakriti Siddhi. This is the only way he can do his work.
items.statement: Prakriti Siddhi is the highest siddhi, characterized as the ability to alter the consciousness of any entity or modify the nature of Universal Prakriti beyond the constraints of destiny.
items.title: Aghora 3: The Law of Karma

items.quote: “Yes. The sade sati is the seven-and-a-half year period during which Saturn afflicts the Moon in a horoscope.” This was sounding less and less pleasant. “In Jyotisha we respect the Sun as the planet of light, but we regard its effects as harsh; its light ‘burns’ you. The Moon’s light, however, cools and nourishes you, which makes the Moon the most important planet in Jyotisha—the most important, that is, after Saturn. When Saturn, the planet of dryness, constriction and disappointment, transits the Moon it pinches off the flow of life’s juice and promotes desolation.”
items.statement: The primary cause of sade sati's disruptive power is Saturn transiting the natal Moon, constricting vital life currents and precipitating the disruption of personal protection networks.
items.title: Aghora 3: The Law of Karma

items.qualifiers: Contrasted with physical focus of Ayurveda and ascetic focus of Yoga.
items.quote: Tantra is the science of personality. Just as Ayurveda was promulgated by the ancient sages of India as a truly holistic way to maintain the physical body, and just as Ashtanga Yoga is meant to optimize one’s spiritual nature, Tantra is a mental science, a meta-psychology, a method for exploring the mind and developing the range of one’s perceptions.
items.statement: Tantra is defined as a mental science and meta-psychology aimed at expanding perception and systematically transmuting a limited individual personality into an unlimited permanent one.
items.title: AGHORA, At the Left Hand of God

items.qualifiers: Literal physical union applies only to the Tamasic category.
items.quote: The ritual in which sex appears, which is known as Panchamakara, is actually of three types depending again upon the class of the celebrant, and in only one type does actual sexual intercourse occur. That version is meant only for Tamasic people, Tamas being mental inertia or dullness. The intensity of the five (Pancha means five) articles of worship — meat, fish, parched grain, wine and sex — overwhelms the dullness of the mind with stimulation. If the aspirant has been properly prepared, this increased mental energy can assist his or her spiritual evolution. An ill-prepared aspirant will be overcome by stimulation and will descend into debauchery.
items.statement: The Panchamakara ritual is practiced in three distinct forms corresponding to the temperament of the practitioner: Tamasic using literal physical substances, Rajasic using mild plant and dairy substitutes, and Sattvic utilizing internal meditative equivalents.
items.title: AGHORA, At the Left Hand of God

items.qualifiers: When one fire is elevated in dominance, the other is weakened.
items.quote: When I offer that drop I repeat a certain mantra and then say “Prajvalita!” because both the yeast cells and I should have our intellects become prajvalita (enkindled). By doing this the alcohol enkindles my Bhuta Agni and enables me to soar into the astral regions. Anyone else who drinks will enkindle his Jathara Agni which will increase his appetite and drag him further and further down into physical consciousness. Jathara Agni is the fire which digests our food; it is the body’s power of digestion. Bhuta Agni is associated with the subtle body; it enkindles and inflames Jathara Agni. When the mind is disturbed the Bhuta Agni is weakened, which weakens the Jathara Agni. This results in indigestion, which causes disease.
items.statement: In the human energetic economy, Bhuta Agni serves as the subtle digestive fire fueled by japa and mental discipline, operating inversely to Jathara Agni, the physical digestive fire fueled by food.
items.title: AGHORA, At the Left Hand of God

items.qualifiers: Requires the practitioner to create an internal vacuum to allow entry.
items.quote: So, you can worship an image which has been made to live or you can use your subtle body, which is already living. And there is a third way also, which I am sure you have never even imagined. The deity can enter into someone’s body, and you can worship Him or Her in that way. Your sadhana is very easily accomplished; the deity is pleased; and the person into whose body the deity enters plays with his Beloved and is purified in the bargain. Besides deities, you can call the spirit of some saint or fakir, who can do many mundane works for you. Isn’t this useful? We call this Avishkara in Sanskrit, and baithak or hazri in Hindi or Urdu.
items.statement: Avishkara is the esoteric mechanism through which a deity or discarnate spirit enters and temporarily operates through a living body by creating an internal spiritual vacuum and aligning subtle identification.
items.title: AGHORA, At the Left Hand of God

items.quote: The very same energy that ties us down to our limitations when acting as ahamkara, frees us from those limitations when serving as Kundalini. One’s personal existence as a human being is defined by the equilibrium that develops as ahamkara strives to move us further into manifestation and Kundalini seeks to move us away from materialization.
items.statement: The same cosmic power of self-identification binds an individual to limitation when operating as ahamkara, but frees the individual from limitation when operating as Kundalini.
items.title: AGHORA BOOK II: KUNDALINI

items.qualifiers: According to traditional yogic principles explained by Vimalananda
items.quote: If you sleep on your right side the functioning of surya nadi will be impaired, which permits chandra nadi to work harder, keeping your mind cool and reducing your desires. This gives you a sounder sleep and, because Bhuta Agni is strengthened at the expense of Jathara Agni, helps you control your mind and become a yogi.
items.statement: Sleeping on the right side restricts the solar nadi and activates the lunar nadi, cooling the mind and strengthening subtle digestion (Bhuta Agni) over physical digestion (Jathara Agni).
items.title: AGHORA BOOK II: KUNDALINI

items.quote: The four levels of speech are, from lowest to highest, vaikhari, madhyama, pashyanti and para. Vaikhari, vocal speech, is only for mundane things; it is physical speech, which always has an external object. Dullards and ignoramuses like you and me use vaikhari to communicate.
items.statement: Speech operates across four ascending levels: vaikhari (gross vocal speech), madhyama (mental speech), pashyanti (visionary perception), and para (telepathic intention).
items.title: AGHORA BOOK II: KUNDALINI

items.qualifiers: Must be observed strictly to achieve the manifested form of the deity
items.quote: Both anusthanas and purashcharanas require you to follow what we call in Sanskrit the panchasakara, the Five S’s: sthana, samaya, sankhya, samagri, and samyama. The purpose of these rules is to achieve the sa-guna or manifested form of the deity.
items.statement: To complete a mantra purashcharana or anusthana, an aspirant must strictly adhere to the five requirements of the panchasakara: fixed location, fixed time, fixed number of repetitions, consistent ritual materials, and strict self-restraint.
items.title: AGHORA BOOK II: KUNDALINI

items.quote: Kriya Yoga is a simple, psychophysiological method by which the human blood is decarbonized and recharged with oxygen. The atoms of this extra oxygen are transmuted into life current to rejuvenate the brain and spinal centers.
items.statement: Kriya Yoga is a psychophysiological method of neutralizing the breath to decarbonize and recharge the blood with oxygen, transmuting extra life force to rejuvenate the brain and spinal centers.
items.title: Autobiography of a Yogi

items.qualifiers: Requires proper guru guidance and preparation
items.quote: The Kriya Yogi mentally directs his life energy to revolve, upward and downward, around the six spinal centers (medullary, cervical, dorsal, lumbar, sacral, and coccygeal plexuses) which correspond to the twelve astral signs of the zodiac, the symbolic Cosmic Man. One-half minute of revolution of energy around the sensitive spinal cord of man effects subtle progress in his evolution; that half-minute of Kriya equals one year of natural spiritual unfoldment.
items.statement: According to the mathematics of Kriya Yoga, one half-minute revolution of energy around the human spine corresponds to one year of natural spiritual unfoldment.
items.title: Autobiography of a Yogi

items.quote: Man as an individualized soul is essentially causal-bodied," my guru explained. "That body is a matrix of the thirty-five ideas required by God as the basic or causal thought forces from which He later formed the subtle astral body of nineteen elements and the gross physical body of sixteen elements.
items.statement: Human individualization consists of three concentric encasements: a causal body of thirty-five thought categories, an astral body of nineteen subtle elements, and a gross physical body of sixteen elements.
items.title: Autobiography of a Yogi

items.qualifiers: Requires proper weight and direct contact with the skin
items.quote: Ages ago our yogis discovered that pure metals emit an astral light which is powerfully counteractive to negative pulls of the planets. Subtle electrical and magnetic radiations are constantly circulating in the universe; when a man's body is being aided, he does not know it; when it is being disintegrated, he is still in ignorance.
items.statement: Astrological bangles, specific combinations of metals, and faultless gems of sufficient weight worn against the skin emit electromagnetic radiations that counteract negative planetary vibrations.
items.title: Autobiography of a Yogi

items.qualifiers: From the standpoint of the absolute Self
items.quote: You have no birth or death, no memory, no bondage or liberation, nor have you good or evil. Why do you weep, O my dear? Name and form belong neither to you nor to me.
items.statement: The Atman is untouched by good and evil, action and inaction, and has neither bondage nor liberation, since all distinctions and dualities belong solely to the realm of the body and mind.
items.title: Avadhuta Gita (Dattātreya, Swami Chetanananda)

items.quote: The syllable A of Avadhuta indicates that he is free from the snare of hopes and expectations. His life is pure from its beginning, through its middle, to its end; and he always dwells in bliss.
items.statement: The four syllables of the title 'A-VA-DHU-TA' signify: freedom from hopes (A), uprooting of desires (VA), purity of mind despite physical dust (DHU), and absorption in the thought of Brahman (TA).
items.title: Avadhuta Gita (Dattātreya, Swami Chetanananda)

items.qualifiers: Occurs exclusively by the grace of God's will
items.quote: When God wills it, the illusion of a separate “I” will totally disappear and only God will remain. ( pause…) You see… “Enlightenment” is simply this… The awareness that ONLY GOD has ever existed. That is enlightenment. The question of enlightenment itself is finally dropped completely!
items.statement: The personal self or ego is an illusion created by God, and individual enlightenment is merely the spontaneous realization that only God has ever existed and acted.
items.title: BE - Beyond Enlightenment by Claudio (C.)

items.qualifiers: Understood within the realization that God is everything
items.quote: Within the concept of “God Is Everything”, we can understand the concept of “Meditation”. Meditation is simply…The Practice of “Letting Go and Letting God”. There should be no effort in one’s meditation. Because for effort to exist, there needs to be an “I” to make that effort.
items.statement: True meditation is the effortless practice of letting go of all mental concepts and personal effort, recognizing that God alone is the doer.
items.title: BE - Beyond Enlightenment by Claudio (C.)

items.quote: That in relation to which the awareness does not change is real; that in relation to which it changes is unreal. Thus, since the distinction between the real and the unreal is dependent on awareness, therefore in all cases (of empirical experiences) everyone has two kinds of awarenesses with regard to the same substratum
items.statement: The criterion distinguishing the real from the unreal is based on awareness: that in relation to which awareness is constant and unchanging is real, whereas that in relation to which awareness changes is unreal.
items.title: Bhagavad Gita: With the Commentary of Adi Shankaracharya

items.quote: One should know that severance of contact with sorrow to be what is called Yoga. That Yoga has to be practised with perseverance and with an undepressed heart.
items.statement: Yoga is defined as the severance of contact with sorrow, rather than merely an active physical or meditative technique.
items.title: Bhagavad Gita: With the Commentary of Adi Shankaracharya

items.qualifiers: Described as avidya (nescience) by the learned, and distinguished from true discrimination (vidya)
items.quote: If it be asked, "What is it that is called superimposition?"the answer is: It is an awareness, similar in nature to memory, that arises on a different (foreign) basis as a result of some past experience.'
items.statement: Superimposition is defined as an awareness, resembling memory, that appears upon a different substratum as a consequence of past experience.
items.title: Brahma Sutra Bhasya Of Sankaracharya

items.qualifiers: Contrasting the nature of knowledge of Brahman with ritual actions and injunctions
items.quote: Options depend on human notions, whereas the valid knowledge of the true nature of a thing is not dependent on human notions. On what does it depend then? It is dependent on the thing itself.
items.statement: Valid knowledge of an existing reality is strictly determined by the object itself, whereas actions and meditative options depend on human notions and effort.
items.title: Brahma Sutra Bhasya Of Sankaracharya

items.qualifiers: Explains why the physical body persists for a realized sage until the momentum of prarabdha karma is spent
items.quote: After the acquisition of knowledge, those virtues and vices that have not begun to yield their fruits and that were accumulated in earlier lives or even in this life before the dawn of knowledge are alone destroyed, but not so are those destroyed whose results have already been partially enjoyed and by which has been begun this present life in which the knowledge of Brahman arises.
items.statement: Knowledge of Brahman annihilates only past accumulated karmas that have not yet begun to bear fruit, whereas karmas that have already commenced fruition must be exhausted through bodily experience.
items.title: Brahma Sutra Bhasya Of Sankaracharya

items.qualifiers: applies to conditioned, qualified Brahman and not to the supreme omnipresent Brahman
items.quote: For this conditioned Brahman can properly be a goal to be reached, since It has a locus. But with regard to the supreme Brahman there can be no such conceptions as an approacher, a goal, and progress towards It, for the absolute Brahman is omnipresent and is also the inmost Self of the travellers.
items.statement: The departure along the path of the gods and progression through different stages relates exclusively to the knower of the conditioned Brahman, as the supreme Brahman is all-pervasive and cannot be an object of spatial attainment.
items.title: Brahma Sutra Bhasya Of Sankaracharya

items.qualifiers: except running the universe (creation, preservation, dissolution)
items.quote: The released soul gets all the divine powers except that of running the universe (with its creation, continuance, and dissolution), as is known from the context (which deals with God) and from the non-proximity (of the individual soul).
items.statement: The released soul that attains the conditioned world of Brahman receives all lordly and divine powers with the explicit exception of cosmic functions like creation, preservation, and dissolution, which belong solely to God.
items.title: Brahma Sutra Bhasya Of Sankaracharya

items.qualifiers: apparent presentation operating by way of remembrance
items.quote: Superimposition, says Sankara, is the apparent presentation to consciousness, by way of remem- brance, of something previously observed in some other thing.
items.statement: Superimposition (Adhyasa) is defined as the apparent presentation to consciousness, by way of memory, of attributes previously observed in another entity.
items.title: Brahma Sutras - According to Sri Sankaracharya (Swami Vireswarananda)

items.qualifiers: only Sanchita karma is destroyed; Prarabdha persists until exhausted
items.quote: The Sutra refutes this view and says that only the Sanchita works are destroyed by Knowledge, but not the Praérabdha, which are destroyed only by being worked out. So long as the momentum of these works lasts, the knower of Brahman has to be in the body.
items.statement: Knowledge of Brahman destroys only accumulated (Sanchita) works that have not begun to fructify, while commenced (Prarabdha) works must run their course through experience until physical death.
items.title: Brahma Sutras - According to Sri Sankaracharya (Swami Vireswarananda)

items.quote: The identification of the ego1 with the reflection of Consciousness, the body and the Witness are of three kinds, namely, natural,2 due to (past) Karma,3 and due to ignorance,4 respectively.
items.statement: The identification of the ego with the reflection of Consciousness, the physical body, and the Witness is categorized into three types: natural, born of past Karma, and born of ignorance, respectively.
items.title: Drg-Drsya Viveka - An Inquiry Into The Nature Of The 'seer' And The 'seen

items.qualifiers: classified based on practice in the heart
items.quote: Two kinds of Samādhi to be practised in the heart (within one’s self) are known as Savikalpa1 and Nirvikalpa2 Savikalpa-Samādhi is again divided into two classes, according to its association with a cognizable object or a sound (as an object).
items.statement: Meditation practiced within the heart is twofold, Savikalpa and Nirvikalpa, with Savikalpa further dividing based on whether it is associated with a cognizable object or a sound idea.
items.title: Drg-Drsya Viveka - An Inquiry Into The Nature Of The 'seer' And The 'seen

items.qualifiers: distinction across three levels of Jiva experience
items.quote: He who is the empirical1 Jīva sees this empirical2 world as real.3 But the real4 Jīva knows it5 to be unreal.6
items.statement: The illusory Jiva takes the dream world to be real, the empirical Jiva recognizes the dream world as unreal while viewing the waking world as real, and the Paramarthika (Real) Jiva knows the empirical world itself to be unreal.
items.title: Drg-Drsya Viveka - An Inquiry Into The Nature Of The 'seer' And The 'seen

items.quote: Do you not remember what was pointed out (in the introduction) that the antithesis between knowledge and karma is irremovable like a mountain?
items.statement: Knowledge and ritual work (karma) are completely antithetical and mutually exclusive, rendering it impossible to combine knowledge of the supreme Self with ritual action.
items.title: Eight Upanishads, With the Commentary of Shankaracharya (2 Vol. Set)

items.quote: An adjective distinguishes a noun from things of its own class, whereas a definition marks it out from everything else, as for instance, (the definition -) akasa is that which provides space.
items.statement: An adjective separates a noun from things within its own class, whereas a definition differentiates a substantive from everything else in existence.
items.title: Eight Upanishads, With the Commentary of Shankaracharya (2 Vol. Set)

items.quote: There is no dissolution, no origination, none in bondage, none striving or aspiring for salvation, and none liberated. This is the highest truth.
items.statement: From the standpoint of absolute reality, there is no dissolution, no origination, no bondage, no aspirant striving for liberation, and no one liberated.
items.title: Eight Upanishads, With the Commentary of Shankaracharya (2 Vol. Set)

items.quote: By asserting that the Self exists', does not exist', exists and does not exist', or again, does not exist, does not exist', the non-discriminating man does certainly cover It up through ideas of changeability, unchangeability, both changeability and unchangeability, and non-existence.
items.statement: The four alternative ontological positions of the disputants—that the Self exists, does not exist, both exists and does not exist, or neither exists nor does not exist—serve only to veil the Lord.
items.title: Eight Upanishads, With the Commentary of Shankaracharya (2 Vol. Set)

items.quote: Yoga is the control of thought-waves in the mind.
items.statement: Yoga is defined as the control and cessation of thought-waves in the mind.
items.title: How to Know God

items.quote: According to Patanjali, the mind (chitta) is made up of three components, manas, buddhi and ahamkar. Manas is the recording faculty which receives impressions gathered by the senses from the outside world. Buddhi is the discriminative faculty which classifies these impressions and reacts to them. Ahamkar is the ego-sense which claims these impressions for its own and stores them up as individual knowledge.
items.statement: The mind is composed of three faculties: manas for recording sensory impressions, buddhi for discriminating and classifying, and ahamkar for the ego-sense.
items.title: How to Know God

items.quote: The samskaras are built up by the continued action of the thought-waves, and they, in their turn, create new thought-waves—the process works both ways.
items.statement: Character consists of subconscious samskaras, which are built by recurring thought-waves and in turn generate subsequent thought-waves.
items.title: How to Know God

items.qualifiers: Prescribed as a preliminary mental attitude for yoga aspirants.
items.quote: Undisturbed calmness of mind is attained by cultivating friendliness toward the happy, compassion for the unhappy, delight in the virtuous, and indifference toward the wicked.
items.statement: Calmness of mind is cultivated by adopting specific psychological attitudes: friendliness to the happy, compassion for the unhappy, delight in the virtuous, and indifference toward the wicked.
items.title: How to Know God

items.qualifiers: spoken only by a few yogis and sages during sushumna; has no worldly vocabulary
items.quote: It is a purely yogic language, spoken by only a few fortunate yogis, sages, and adepts. Philosophically and ideally, it is very similar to Sanskrit, for every word of Sandhya Bhasha flows full of meaning from its root sound. Sandhya Bhasha can be used only for the discussion of spiritual matters and contains no vocabulary for the business affairs of the world. When the sun weds with the moon, when the day weds with the night, and when ida and pingala [the left and right energy channels of the human body] equally flow, that union is called sandhya or sushumna. Sushumna is the mother from whose womb was born the language Sandhya Bhasha or twilight.
items.statement: Sandhya Bhasha is a purely yogic sound-based language spoken by adepts during the union of ida and pingala (sushumna), containing vocabulary solely for spiritual matters.
items.title: Living with the Himalayan Masters

items.qualifiers: Kaula focuses on muladhara, Mishra on anahata, Samaya on sahasrara/antaryaga
items.quote: There are three main schools of tantra: Kaula, Mishra, and Samaya. The Kaulas, or left-hand tantrists, worship Shakti, and their way of worship involves external rituals, including sexual practices. They meditate on the latent power within (kundalini) and awaken it at the muladhara chakra, which is situated at the base of the spinal column. Laymen often misuse this path. In the Mishra (mixed or combined) school, inner worship is combined with external practices. The latent force is awakened and led to the anahata chakra (heart center), where it is worshipped. The purest and highest path of tantra is called Samaya or the righthand path. It is purely yoga; it has nothing to do with any ritual or any form of worship involving sex. Meditation is the key, but this sort of meditation is quite uncommon. In this school meditation is done on the thousand-petaled lotus, the highest of all.
items.statement: Tantra philosophy is divided into three main schools: Kaula (left-hand with external rituals), Mishra (mixed inner and external practices), and Samaya (purely internal yogic meditation on the sahasrara).
items.title: Living with the Himalayan Masters

items.qualifiers: applies when comparing individual self-centered focus with universal focus
items.quote: When intense worry controls the mind, the mind becomes inert and insensitive. But if a great man contemplates on the miseries of the world it is not a worry at all, but a loving and selfless concern for humanity. In this case the individual mind expands and unites itself with the cosmic One. When the mind is engrossed in individual interests one-pointedly, it is called worry. When the mind is made aware of the misery of others, it starts contemplating positively. In both cases mind can become one-pointed, but in the latter case consciousness is expanded.
items.statement: Worry and meditation both focus the mind, but worry contracts it around individual interest causing illness, whereas meditation expands consciousness by directing attention positively or selflessly toward the universal.
items.title: Living with the Himalayan Masters

items.qualifiers: practical understanding is possessed by very few adepts
items.quote: According to my grandmaster it involves a particular type of meditation on the solar plexus, and is very beneficial for removing all obstacles created by physical and mental diseases. The solar system is the largest network in the human body, and its center is called manipura chakra. There are various ways of meditating on this chakra, but by including advanced pranayama, solar science brings forward an awareness of a level of energy finer than the pranic level. At this level the energy rhythms are studied by meditating either on the morning sun or on udaragni, which is the internal center of fire. [This fire is created by the friction of the upper hemisphere and the lower hemisphere, which in the Upanishads are called upper arani and lower arani.] This healing science, though described in the Upanishads and known about by scholars, is understood in a practical way by very few. By learning this science one can have absolute control over his three sheaths—physical, pranic, and mental.
items.statement: Solar science is an advanced esoteric yogic healing discipline focused on the solar plexus (manipura chakra) to master energy finer than prana and gain control over the physical, pranic, and mental sheaths.
items.title: Living with the Himalayan Masters

items.qualifiers: action purifies the mind but cannot directly eliminate ignorance
items.quote: Action cannot destroy ignorance, for it is not in conflict with ignorance. Knowledge alone destroys ignorance, as light destroys dense darkness.
items.statement: Action cannot destroy ignorance because action operates within the framework of doer, instrument, and result, whereas only knowledge of non-duality destroys ignorance.
items.title: Self-knowledge - An English translation of Shankaracharyas Atmabodha with notes, comments and introduction (Swami Nikhilananda)

items.qualifiers: due to non-discrimination between Spirit and matter
items.quote: Such a notion as “I know” is produced by the union, due to non-discrimination, of a modification of the mind with two aspects of Atman, namely, Existence and Consciousness.
